Or, they can just choose to sell everything too, though that’s a very rare case."
"I see..." Soren nodded, his mind racing with this new info.
If he could somehow turn this into an investment, what would the returns be?
’...Let’s give it a try after joining.’
Doran noticed the interest in Soren’s expression, and his lips curled up.
Satisfied with the result of his plan, he continued.
"As for high-ranking members, they obviously enjoy the most benefits.
Along with what I mentioned till now, they will acquire voting power in the Association’s decisions and leadership elections.
They will also get high-tier access to the recipes library and sponsorships or funding to develop new recipes, cooking techniques, or even equipment.
They will be protected by the Association and its partners, and can even work for royal families..."
Doran went on to explain the remaining details, then finally came to a stop and turned to Soren with an expectant look.
"...What do you think?"
"Honestly, I’m really impressed.
It’s more than I expected.
Thank you for taking the time to explain everything." Soren bowed politely.
"Hehe, as long as you are willing to join us, my time was well spent." Doran laughed and came to a stop in front of a door.
"This will be where your exam takes place.
Let’s go in..."
He pushed the door open and led them inside.
The testing room was larger than Soren expected, filled with stations arranged in order.
There was enough space for both the cook and any observers.
The stations were equipped with all the necessary tools.
There were a few people inside, probably the examiners or other test-takers.
They quickly noticed their arrival and immediately greeted Doran before giving a nod to them.
"This is the young man I talked about yesterday," Doran said.
"He already passed the beginner rank exam yesterday.
So you can start with the 3rd rank examination directly."
"Understood, President." One of them turned to Soren and briefly explained the process, what was expected of him, and the criteria for passing.
Soren listened carefully, nodding along.
When the explanation was done, the examiner stepped back and gestured toward an empty station.
"Whenever you’re ready."
Soren glanced at Ethea, who gave him a small nod, then walked over to his station, rolled up his sleeves, and donned the apron.
’Hmm...
I guess there were really grades to meals.’ He thought as he prepared the tools. ’I wonder what grades the meals I got from the returns are...’
He knew they were probably rare recipes, considering their effects, but without a proper benchmark, he had no way of knowing where they stood on the Association’s scale.
Maybe after passing this exam, he could look into it further.
For now, he pushed the thought aside and focused on the task at hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 261: Master Chef?
paragraphs: The exam started, and time passed.
Soren cooked while the examiners, Ethea and Doran, observed him work. The examiners whispered to each other from time to time, discussing his technique and the process itself.
Ethea could hear their conversation and managed to pick up a few things related to grading magic chefs and meals.

She heard about five ranks for chefs, starting from Apprentice Magic Chef to Junior, then Expert, then Senior, and Master Magic Chef. As for meal grades, they started with Common, then Fine, Superior, Exquisite, and finally Masterwork. Though Ethea preferred to call it by numbers.

And right now, Soren was taking an Expert Magic Chef’s exam, so he must be able to prepare at least three Superior Grade meals. From what she heard, a Superior Meal was required to reach perfect integration of the ingredients and mana while bringing out their full potential.
She didn’t understand other parts since she didn’t know much about cooking, but looking at their expressions, it was obvious Soren was doing a good job.
"Don’t worry, he is gonna pass it easily."
"?" Hearing the sudden remark, Ethea looked to her right. It was Doran who spoke, staring at Soren intensely.
"I am sure about it now."
"...I know," Ethea replied, feeling a little happy. "...You must be a chef too, right?"
"Oh," Doran’s eyes lit up as he turned to Ethea. "Was it that obvious?

"...Yes." Ethea barely stopped her lips from twitching as she didn’t expect him to react like that. However, since the man had initiated the conversation, she decided to fish for some information. "Mr. Doran, are you a Master Chef?"

"Huh? You think I’m a Master?" Doran’s smile widened even further. "I’m flattered, but no. I’m a Senior Magic Chef. Have been stuck at it for nearly a decade now." He let out a self-deprecating chuckle. "The jump from Senior to a Master is... well, let’s say it’s not something most chefs ever manage in their lives."
"I see... But I think you will be able to achieve it." Ethea replied. "It’s obvious how much you love cooking. Anyone who watches you talk about it can tell."

Doran blinked, then let out a genuine laugh. "You know, most people just tell me I talk too much. But thank you, Mrs. Everly. That means more than you know." He turned his gaze back toward Soren, who was deep in focus at his station. "Your husband has that same passion. I could see it the moment he started cooking yesterday. That’s why I’m sure he’ll pass."
"Then... what do you think about his chances at the tournament? Do you think he can win it?"

"Hmm... While he certainly has talent and passion for cooking, I don’t think he’s at that level yet. However, I don’t know much about him or his real capabilities, so it’s hard to tell. Perhaps there is a chance for him to rise as a dark horse and make a name for himself, but winning... It will be extremely difficult."
"Why do you think so?" Ethea continued to probe.

"..." Doran paused, sensing something was wrong. But thinking she might be just curious because of her husband, he answered. "Well, there are a few reasons for it. First, I don’t know whether he participated in other contests before, but this will be a big one, with countless eyes watching him work. It might put pressure on him and mess with his concentration. Cooking around a few people is one thing, but doing it with a massive audience, judges, and competitors all around you is a completely different experience. Trust me, I’ve been there myself.

Ethea nodded in understanding. While she hadn’t experienced it herself, she still knew how nerve-wracking it could be to perform with so many eyes watching, especially for someone who had never done it before. But at the same time, she had watched Soren face far worse than a crowd of strangers. If he could keep his head calm while fighting for his life, then cooking in front of an audience shouldn’t break him either.
"Furthermore," Doran added, "his opponents are a force to be reckoned with. Especially the strongest candidate for this year’s championship."
"Are they that good?"

"Mm, there are five Experts, two Seniors among them. One of the Seniors is the apprentice of the famous Grandmaster Chef Tamimi, and the other is a guest from another nation. Everyone knows about Grandmaster Tamimi’s disciple, and he is the favorite, but the other Senior is almost unknown. No one seems to know much about him, just that he arrived in the empire a few weeks ago and hasn’t participated in any public competitions before this one."

’...Is this information public or...?’ Ethea squinted briefly at Doran’s words and guessed it was probably something he had dug up himself. As the president of the Association’s Bagdad branch, he would have access to the participant lists and background checks long before the tournament began. Still, sharing it so freely with her felt less like an official briefing and more like gossip between two spectators. She decided not to comment on it and simply filed the information away for later. ’But with this, there’s a high chance for Soren to reach the semi-finals.’

"And last but not least, there are the wild cards." Doran rubbed his chin. "Every year there are a few contestants that come out of nowhere and surprise everyone. However, there is a high chance your husband could be one of them. He has a natural instinct for balancing flavors, and his mana control is better than most chefs I have seen at his age. If he can keep his nerve, he can go further than anyone expects."
"I hope he wins and surprises everyone," said Ethea. "But above all, I want him to enjoy himself."
"..." Doran glanced at Ethea, his lips curling up. "He’s really lucky to have a supportive partner like you."
Ethea shook her head. "I’m the lucky one."

"..." Doran smiled and said nothing more, turning his focus back to Soren, who was already close to finishing his first dish. His expression flickered for just a moment, a brief shadow passing over his features before he masked it with his signature smile. ’...Must be nice, having someone who believes in you that much.’

chapters.title: Chapter 262: Golden Ladle Championship [1]
paragraphs: Four hours passed in the blink of an eye.

Soren managed to cook three different Superior Grade meals and pass the exam with flying colors. He was asked if he wanted to take the exam for a Senior Chef, but Soren declined since he was a little exhausted from the intense work and felt this was already enough. He made an excuse that he wasn’t at that level yet, though deep down he knew he wasn’t that far off.

Regardless, they proceeded with his certificate, and before lunch, he was officially registered as an Expert Magic Chef. The certificate itself looked similar to his hunter license and ID card, with his name, rank, issue date and place, and unique identification number etched into its surface.

However, the happiest with the results wasn’t Soren or Ethea but Doran himself. He beamed with joy as if he were the one who had passed the exam, leaving the two a little baffled. Because Doran already knew they were foreigners as well and had arrived in the city just two days ago.
They guessed there must be some reason for it, like one would get a bonus or a reward for recruiting a new talented member to the Association.

Whatever the case, they’d got what they’d come for, and before leaving, Soren had pulled Doran aside to ask if it was possible to find a private viewing room available for Ethea during the tournament, somewhere safe and away from the crowds.
"Sure thing," Doran told him. "I’ll make sure you get a reserved seat with a good view of the stage."
With that settled, Soren and Ethea left the Association building and walked back out into the streets of the festival.
They had lunch together before heading back to the hotel. They chose to rest for the remainder of the day, as the competition was scheduled to begin tomorrow morning at 8 am.
Along the way, Ethea shared what she learned from Doran and told Soren he might be able to win a good prize if he participates seriously.
"Alright, I will research a bit more then," Soren promised, and they arrived at their room. "You should rest while I study. I don’t want you exhausting yourself before tomorrow."
"Mm, but remember to take a break too." Ethea gave him a small smile before closing her eyes and sinking into her soul space to continue her mental cultivation.
’I will...’
"Ladies and gentlemen! Welcome to the grand opening of the Golden Ladle Championship!"

The announcer’s voice boomed across the arena, amplified by special arrays that carried every word to the farthest seats. The crowd roared in response, a sea of faces filling the stands around the massive open-air arena. At the center, dozens of cooking stations had been arranged in neat rows, each one equipped with enchanted tools and ingredients. Massive floating screens hovered above the arena, broadcasting the stage from every angle.
"I’m your host, Faris Renn, and joining me today is none other than former Golden Ladle winner, now Master Magic Chef, Lady Layla Voss!"
A second voice, gentler and feminine, joined in.

"Thank you, Faris. It’s an honor to be here." The voice carried a hint of nostalgia. "I still remember the first time I stood on this very stage as a contestant. The nerves, the excitement... it never really goes away."
"Well, of course, you ended up being the champion on your debut after all."
A ripple of laughter passed through the crowd at Faris’s remark.

Layla let it settle before replying. "That was a long time ago. The competition has grown fiercer since then. Even I would think twice before stepping into the arena now." She paused, then added with a wry smile. "I can see how terrifying this year’s lineup is."

"That’s right!" Faris exclaimed. "After all, we’ve got contestants from all over the continent this time. Some are seasoned veterans, and some are fresh faces hoping to make a name for themselves. It’s definitely going to be an exciting tournament!"
"Without a doubt." Layla agreed. "But... I think there are too many participants. Do you think they’ll be able to finish the preliminary round in one day?"
"I’m not exactly sure either." Faris rubbed his chin. "But I’m sure the organizers have everything under control. We just have to trust them and do our job!"
"Haha, you’re right. Then should we begin by reminding everyone of the rules once more? I heard there were small changes to them this year."
"Mm, but let’s keep it short and not bore our audience. Right, guys?" Faris flashed a smile at the cameras, which earned another round of applause and laughter.

Layla also chuckled before looking at the papers in her hand. "Let’s see... Since the participants are over six hundred, the time limit had been decreased from ninety minutes to one hour. But the task remains the same; they have to cook a meal using only the ingredients provided at their stations. No outside ingredients allowed.

"If anyone tries to smuggle in some, they will be punished accordingly," Faris added with a stern expression. "You might even end up losing your certificate and get banned. So I recommend that our participants think before acting."

Layla nodded in agreement. "Fortunately or unfortunately, there was no change in the theme for the preliminaries. But considering the festival celebrates the harvest, it makes sense that they kept it. It’s tradition at this point, and changing it would feel wrong."

"As expected of Lady Layla. She keeps spitting facts!" Faris grinned once more. "But there is also good news. The number of participants who can advance to the next round has been increased from fifty to a hundred. So don’t lose hope just yet!"
"That’s indeed good news. But..." Layla paused, flipping the page. "I think they will extend the next round because of this."

"Well, that means we get to see more incredible dishes before the tournament ends." Faris turned to the crowd with a widening grin. "And speaking of incredible, we have a very special guest here today to officially open this year’s Golden Ladle Championship!"
"A special guest?" Layla raised her brow. "Why don’t I know about it?"
"Well, it’s because..." Faris leaned in closer to the camera, clasping his hands, his expression turning serious as if he were about to reveal a massive secret.
A few seconds passed.
"...Because?" Layla repeated.
"...It’s because I... I forgot to tell you."

chapters.title: Chapter 263: Golden Ladle Championship [2]
paragraphs: "...I forgot to tell you."

The arena went deathly silent for a moment and then erupted in laughter. Layla kept staring at him, her expression caught between disbelief and the urge to smack him right then and there. But recalling they were on a live broadcast, and thousands or even millions of people watching them, she held back. Taking a deep breath, she ’smiled’. "Alright, I won’t hold it against you and think you just wanted to surprise me."
Faris’s eyes lit up, and he bowed a few times, wiping away the nonexistent sweat on his forehead. "Thank you for your mercy, Senior!"
"Now, hurry up and introduce them." Layla urged him. "Just who is this special guest?"

"Right, right. Ahem." Faris coughed a few times and cleared his throat, his usual enthusiastic expression returning. "Ladies and gentlemen, throughout the history of this great empire, there are figures who embody its very soul. Our guest is one such figure. She carries herself with a grace that captivates every eye, a wisdom that silences every doubt, and a kindness that lifts every heart. She is beloved not because of her title, but because of the light she brings to all who stand in her presence."
He paused for effect, letting the anticipation build.

"She is a patron of the arts, a guardian of our traditions, and a voice for the voiceless. Her beauty is spoken across nations, her intellect respected by scholars and warriors alike, and her heart... her heart belongs entirely to her people. There is no one more fitting to open this year’s tournament than the woman we are about to welcome."
Faris rose from his seat and spread his arms wide.
"Everyone, put your hands together for the jewel of the Temur Empire, the star of the imperial family, Her Highness, Princess Roya!"
As soon as Faris finished speaking, the arena erupted once again.

The applause rolled through the stands like a wave as the spectators rose to their feet. Camera drones swiveled toward the Celestial Pavilion, capturing every angle of the royal viewing gallery as the crimson and gold lights brightened. A soft fanfare echoed through the arena, and every screen flickered before focusing on the figure stepping out from the pavilion’s shadow.
It was Princess Roya.

She moved with an easy grace, her dark hair falling past her shoulders and a delicate golden circlet resting on her brow. She wore a gown of silver and deep crimson, embroidered with patterns of wheat and leaves. Her features were refined and elegant, and there was a warmth in her eyes that made her feel less like a distant royal and more like someone genuinely happy to be here.
She approached the edge of the balcony and lifted a hand in greeting.
Faris placed a hand over his heart and bowed deeply. "Your Highness, you honor us with your presence."

"The honor is mine." The princess Roya smiled. "Both the Harvest Festival and the Golden Ladle have always held a special place in my heart. The harvest is the lifeblood of this empire, and today, we celebrate the hands that feed us."
Layla inclined her head as well. "We are grateful for your continued support, Your Highness. The chefs are ready, and with your blessing, we can begin."

Princess Roya lifted her hand once more. Golden light gathered at her fingertips, shimmering like wheat in sunlight. "Then let us not wait any longer. I hereby declare this year’s Golden Ladle Championship... officially open!"
"WOOOH!"
"YEAAAH!"
The crowd roared even louder, and the screens above the arena flickered as the first group of contestants started working.
The countdown appeared on the main screen, ticking down in glowing golden numbers.
"That was one of the best openings I had ever witnessed in my life!" Faris quickly got back to his job. "Thank you, Your Highness."
Roya subtly nodded.
Faris cleared his throat before turning back to the camera. "And now, let’s take a look at our contestants and see what they have in store for us..."

Layla joined the commentary as well, and the competition continued smoothly. Group after group took their places on the stage, with one hour given to show their skills and another half for judging. It came to a stop at lunch and picked up right after. And a few hours later, it was finally Soren’s group’s turn.
As Soren entered the arena, he was immediately hit by the breathtaking sight. While he had already seen everything from the waiting room, experiencing it himself was vastly different.

However, he managed to recover quickly and kept walking while taking in his surroundings. His gaze stopped briefly at one of the private watching rooms, his lips curling. Ethea was in there, watching him. That thought alone settled his nerves more than any breathing exercise Doran recommended could.
’...Huff.’

After taking his position, Soren took a deep breath and let his gaze sweep over everything. Perhaps because he had already taken two tests in the last two days, he was already used to the setup and the feeling of being watched. He also didn’t feel any nervousness, probably because of his high mental power.

’Alright, the theme is ’harvest’, and we are free to cook whatever we want.’ He squinted as he recalled the ideas he came up with while waiting and watching. ’Hmm... this will be a good opportunity to test out that recipe. But... it might be a bit too risky...’

He had just one hour, and the aim was to break the top hundred. A new dish could impress the judges, but if mistakes were made, there wouldn’t be enough time to fix them. A proven and dependable recipe was more secure, but it also risked being overlooked among the other contestants.
’...Let’s go with something in between.’ He decided. ’A dish I know well, but with a harvest twist.’

’...Good, let’s get started.’

sentences.text: "...I forgot to tell you."
The arena went deathly silent for a moment and then erupted in laughter.
Layla kept staring at him, her expression caught between disbelief and the urge to smack him right then and there.
But recalling they were on a live broadcast, and thousands or even millions of people watching them, she held back.
Taking a deep breath, she ’smiled’.
"Alright, I won’t hold it against you and think you just wanted to surprise me."
Faris’s eyes lit up, and he bowed a few times, wiping away the nonexistent sweat on his forehead.
"Thank you for your mercy, Senior!"
"Now, hurry up and introduce them." Layla urged him.
"Just who is this special guest?"
"Right, right.
Ahem." Faris coughed a few times and cleared his throat, his usual enthusiastic expression returning.
"Ladies and gentlemen, throughout the history of this great empire, there are figures who embody its very soul.
Our guest is one such figure.
She carries herself with a grace that captivates every eye, a wisdom that silences every doubt, and a kindness that lifts every heart.
She is beloved not because of her title, but because of the light she brings to all who stand in her presence."
He paused for effect, letting the anticipation build.
"She is a patron of the arts, a guardian of our traditions, and a voice for the voiceless.
Her beauty is spoken across nations, her intellect respected by scholars and warriors alike, and her heart... her heart belongs entirely to her people.
There is no one more fitting to open this year’s tournament than the woman we are about to welcome."
Faris rose from his seat and spread his arms wide.
"Everyone, put your hands together for the jewel of the Temur Empire, the star of the imperial family, Her Highness, Princess Roya!"
As soon as Faris finished speaking, the arena erupted once again.
The applause rolled through the stands like a wave as the spectators rose to their feet.
Camera drones swiveled toward the Celestial Pavilion, capturing every angle of the royal viewing gallery as the crimson and gold lights brightened.
A soft fanfare echoed through the arena, and every screen flickered before focusing on the figure stepping out from the pavilion’s shadow.
It was Princess Roya.
She moved with an easy grace, her dark hair falling past her shoulders and a delicate golden circlet resting on her brow.
She wore a gown of silver and deep crimson, embroidered with patterns of wheat and leaves.
Her features were refined and elegant, and there was a warmth in her eyes that made her feel less like a distant royal and more like someone genuinely happy to be here.
She approached the edge of the balcony and lifted a hand in greeting.
Faris placed a hand over his heart and bowed deeply.
"Your Highness, you honor us with your presence."
"The honor is mine." The princess Roya smiled.
"Both the Harvest Festival and the Golden Ladle have always held a special place in my heart.
The harvest is the lifeblood of this empire, and today, we celebrate the hands that feed us."
Layla inclined her head as well.
"We are grateful for your continued support, Your Highness.

Princess Roya lifted her hand once more.
Golden light gathered at her fingertips, shimmering like wheat in sunlight.
"Then let us not wait any longer.
I hereby declare this year’s Golden Ladle Championship... officially open!"
"WOOOH!"
"YEAAAH!"

Roya subtly nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 264: Golden Ladle Championship [3]
paragraphs: ’First, let’s put the spirit rice into water...’
’Now, cut the meat and vegetables...’
’Let’s infuse a bit of ice mana into it so anyone who eats it will feel like their effort has finally paid off after working in the sun for so long...’
Time passed, and Soren kept working while talking to himself inwardly. He became so engrossed in it that he even forgot about his surroundings, the competitors, the spectators, and so on.
"We have one minute left! Those who haven’t finished yet, hurry up! Or else you are gonna fail."
Faris’s voice boomed across the arena.
"...Done."

Soren took a step back from his station, looking at his masterpiece with a satisfied smile. It took him much longer than he initially planned, probably because he kept getting creative and making changes along the way, but it was definitely worth the effort.
Now, the only thing left was to wait for the judges’ decision.
’It was fun, though.’
It felt like he was discovering a new side of himself.
’I guess it’s the ’magic’ of working under pressure?’

He watched as his dish was carried to the judges’ table, alongside the other plates from his group. He also noticed some who failed to finish on time and took their leave, their heads hanging low. That was also when he realized how high the pressure was and how abnormal he was for not paying it any mind.
While he kept thinking about such things and cleaning his workspace, the judging period ended, and the results were announced.
Soren watched as the main screen flickered one after another, finally revealing his results.
[Soren Everly: Pass]
’...’ His lips curled up faintly as he turned in Ethea’s direction. ’I did it, dear.’

Then he turned back, finished cleaning up, and left the arena with the other competitors. There were few who tried to make conversation with him, and he replied accordingly before excusing himself and heading straight to Ethea’s side.
’I hope she didn’t get bored...’
"Your Highness, was there anyone who caught your eye?"

Roya turned to her left with a smile. "There are so many talented candidates that it would be unfair to name just one. Each of them has their own charm, and it has been a pleasure watching them cook. Though..." She paused, her gaze drifting back toward the stage. "I do find myself drawn to those who remain calm under pressure. Especially that long-haired chef. She is doing it with such elegance, as if nothing affects her. Can you tell me about her, Lord Asad?"
"You certainly have a gift for recognizing talent, Your Highness." Asad, the bald man sitting beside the princess, replied while stroking his mustache. "She’s actually one of the special candidates."
Roya raised her brow. "You mean... she’s not from our empire?"
"That’s right." Asad nodded, his expression becoming a bit serious. "In fact, she’s not even from our world..."
"...I see." Princess Roya immediately connected the dots. ’So she’s one of the people from the URF I heard about in the reports.’
"...Is she an elf then?" She asked after analyzing what she knew from them and watching her work. "She looks really skilled at controlling mana after all."
"You guessed it correctly. She’s indeed an elf." Asad replied. "In fact, we suspect she might have a high status."
’...I hope they are being closely monitored then,’ Roya spoke telepathically this time. ’We can’t have any problems occur and need to ensure everything remains under control.’
’Rest assured, Your Highness,’ Asad replied. ’I have already dispatched the best team to handle the situation.’
"Then we should show them appropriate courtesy!" Princess Roya added out loud to continue the real conversation. "We have to show them our empire’s hospitality at its finest."
"Don’t worry about it, Your Highness," Asad laughed. "This old man here already took care of everything."
Roya let out a soft laugh. "I should have known. You have always been reliable, after all."
"Your Highness, you’re flattering me too much." Asad laughed again. "Bagdad is my city, and the Temur Empire is my nation. I’m just doing what any citizen would do in my position."
"Then I will leave the rest in your capable hands." Roya nodded before turning her attention back to the stage. However, her mind was still occupied with lingering doubts. ’Hmm...’
’Saya.’
’What’s your order, my lady?’
’...Learn the situation, check every foreign participant and tourist, and report back everything tonight. I have a bad feeling about this.’
’Understood.’
’Good, but don’t alert anyone. If anything goes wrong, you know what to do.’
’Rest assured, my lady.’

With that, Roya finally felt at ease. While City Lord Asad was truly reliable and experienced, she still felt it was necessary to be extra cautious. It was ten times better than being caught off guard when an unexpected problem arises.
’I just hope my intuition is wrong.’
However, deep down, she knew how terrifying her intuition was. After all, it helped her survive many incidents to this day.
’Perhaps this is exactly why Father sent me here...’
She recalled what he had told her before she set off. While he hadn’t mentioned anything notable, he told her to be safe and...
’Watch out for ’variables’...’
She didn’t know what ’variables’ he talked about, but perhaps this was his way of telling her to expect the unexpected.

She let her gaze wander, searching for such ’variables’, but nothing caught her eye or intuition. However, she wouldn’t let her guard down, at least until the competition and the festival came to an end.
’And till the special guests take their leave...’
Her eyes paused at the long, green-haired young woman.

’...Now that I think about it, there were two other candidates who caught my attention earlier. The first one was Grandmaster Tamimi’s apprentice, Sir Damir. However, I already know him well, and he was born in the empire and has shown his loyalty enough times, protecting our honor in international competitions. And the other...’
She recalled the young man who kept glancing at one of the private watching rooms. He kept doing it occasionally even when he was deeply engrossed in cooking.
’He didn’t look like anything special, but... Why did he do it?’
’...I should investigate it. Just in case.’

chapters.title: Chapter 265: Princess’s Investigation
paragraphs: ’Master, we are being watched.’
’...I see.’ Soren replied after a pause. ’How many of them are there? And are they hostile?’

’...They don’t feel hostile. It feels more like they are monitoring us.’ Malakor answered as he scanned the hidden watchers. ’However, we should still keep our guard up and not repeat the mistake we made the previous time.’
’...You’re right.’ Soren agreed as he recalled that painful experience from two weeks ago. ’Keep watching and be ready to act if anything happens.’
’Understood.’
Relieved to have Malakor as their guard, Soren activated the bond and sent a message to Ethea, explaining the situation and asking for her opinion.

’...I think they might have been sent by the princess.’ Ethea guessed after pondering for a moment. ’From what I remember, she was a very cautious person and preferred to be thorough in everything.’ She explained. ’We probably aren’t the only ones who are being watched. She likely has eyes on every foreigner and unfamiliar face in the city. It is simply how she handles things.’
’I see... Then we should just keep acting natural and not give them a reason to dig any deeper?’ Soren voiced his opinion.

’Mm, let’s do that.’ Ethea agreed, although she knew it wouldn’t be that easy. ’Moreover, if she is this serious, there must be something going on, probably related to the festival or participants from other nations. Perhaps there are some special visitors that she needs to be wary of and protect at the same time.’
’That makes sense.’ Soren nodded inwardly, his own thoughts aligning with hers. He knew it was about politics, though he wasn’t as informed as Ethea about it.
’It would have been great if I could see her close...’ He thought to himself. ’That way I could appraise her and determine the truth.’

’Perhaps Icanmeet her.’ If he manages to place in the top 3, he might have a chance to get closer to her, in case she was one of the award presenters. ’But we will have to waste another day for that...’
’Ethea, let’s take our leave after tomorrow. We will finish the ’hunt’ after the competition. There are only a few ingredients left to find anyway.’
’...Alright.’ Ethea wanted to argue but decided to go with Soren’s decision this time. They couldn’t afford to get caught up in any more chaos than they were already in.
’Good, you can continue to cultivate then. Malakor and I will keep watch.’
’Thank you. But remember to take a rest.’
’You too.’
"My lady, here is all the data we collected."
A figure dressed in pitch-black robes presented a tablet to Princess Roya.
"Thank you for your hard work." Roya smiled warmly as she took the tablet. "You can take your leave now. I will contact you if necessary."
"Understood." The figure replied and vanished into the darkness.
"...Sigh." Roya lay down on her bed and started analyzing the information. "Hmm..."

’They couldn’t find anything else about her other than this basic info?’ She raised a brow as she inspected the elf candidate’s file. ’But... this only confirms that she is truly special. I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s an Emperor secretly protecting her. However...’
She couldn’t comprehend why they would come here. Surely it’s not just to participate in this competition?
’Or is it?’
Her mind raced as she considered all the possibilities.
’...Perhaps they want to win the championship and prove something? Or... get the spot to participate in the Grand Magic Chef Tournament?’
This was the only logical explanation she could come up with based on the data she’d been given.
’Well, let’s keep reading, perhaps I’ll uncover something else...’
Sighing once again, she continued her analysis and finally came to a stop.

’Soren Everly... arrived three days ago... joined the competition the next day... met with the Association President Doran... revealed to be an Expert Chef with the potential to become a Grandmaster? Hmm...’
Squinting her eyes, she continued to read, and at one point, her gaze froze on a single line.
[He is traveling with his disabled wife... Ethea Everly...]
’...Ethea?’ To make sure she wasn’t hallucinating, she re-read it a few times. ’...Gulp.’
’Is this... really her?’ Roya sat up, her heartbeat fastening. She scrolled another page where their images were displayed, and her breath caught in her throat. "I-I-It’s definitely her!"
There was no mistaking it. Although her current self was a bit different from the fearless woman she remembered, those mesmerizing eyes and indifferent face had not changed at all.
’B-But... Why is her surname Everly? ...Wait.’ She froze again, realizing it in an instant. ’When did she get married?’
She quickly scrolled back to the previous page, her eyes landing on Soren’s profile. She read it again, carefully this time. After finishing, her first thought was:
’...Why did she marry this guy?’

She could understand that she got married, but why to an average guy like him? Sure, he had the potential to become a Grandmaster Magic Chef and was a bit handsome, but there was nothing else special about him. He was just a 4th Circle, C-rank Hunter with no background. While Ethea was a 7th Circle, S-rank Hunter, with the potential to become a Paragon. She was the rising star; she was... she was...
’...Right... It’s all in the past now.’
Roya let out a deep sigh, the initial shock fading and giving way to something heavier.
’I think I overreacted a bit...’

She respected and admired Ethea both as a woman and a warrior. She helped the Empire many times and the imperial family owed her a great deal. More importantly, she was a woman Roya saw as her rival. The one person she could never catch, no matter how hard she trained or cultivated. She was always a few steps ahead, whether in cultivation, talent, swordsmanship, or even... beauty. She was untouchable. But...
Seeing her now, in a wheelchair, with a husband no one had ever heard of, felt like a cruel twist of fate.
’...Perhaps she married him because she had no other choice.’
’...Or maybe there is a story behind it we don’t know of...’
’They could be even secret lovers who eloped after her family disapproved of him.’
Roya’s thoughts spiraled, each theory more dramatic than the last. She only stopped when she realized they were getting out of hand.
’...I’ll have to find out the truth myself.’
She decided. But for that...
’...I... I should visit her.’

I should visit her.’

chapters.title: Chapter 266: ’Unexpected’ Reunion
paragraphs: ’...Master, that princess is really moving toward Lady Ethea.’
Soren squinted briefly, his senses suddenly widening and landing on Ethea’s room. He could easily ’see’ the figure stealthily making way to the door.
’...She really guessed it correctly.’ Soren replied. ’I guess their relationship was much better than I expected. But...’
’Don’t worry, I’ll keep an eye on them.’ Malakor reassured Soren. ’You can focus on the competition.’
’Alright, thank you.’ Soren let out a breath and turned back to his station. ’But... what about the ’princess’ sitting there? Is she fake? Some sort of illusion?’
’...I believe it’s a real person using some kind of spell or artifact.’ Malakor replied. ’A pretty powerful one at that.’
’I see.’ Soren recalled the stories and rumors he’d heard. That royalty would often have stand-ins, body doubles to protect themselves from assassinations and whatnot. Guess that was true.
"Huff..."
He took another deep breath and cleared his mind of distracting thoughts and got straight to work.
Ethea watched as the quarterfinals of the competition started. A few minutes passed before the door was knocked on.
’...She’s here.’ Ethea’s lips curled up behind her mask. She only spoke when the door was knocked on again. "Who is it?"
"...It is me, junior." A gentle voice echoed.
Ethea kept silent to appear natural before replying. "...Come in."

The door opened without making a sound, and a figure dressed in red robes entered the room. Ethea turned the wheelchair toward the entrance at the same time the figure took off their hood, and their eyes met.
They stared at each other for a long moment.
"...It really is you." The figure was the first to break the silence. "Right?"
"Long time no see, Your Highness." Ethea subtly nodded. "How have you been?"

’...Not Senior but Your Highness...’ The figure, Princess Roya to be more exact, repeated her words in her mind. Her heart ached a little at the distance in Ethea’s tone. They had never been close friends, but there was a time when they could speak more freely. But now... Status and formality stood between them like a wall.

Not to mention that she hadn’t even visited Ethea after the incident. While she had sent a word, it was only through an attendant, and even then, she had no way of knowing whether it even reached Ethea at all. Because by the time she learned the full extent of what happened, Ethea had already disappeared from the public eye. And she had always regretted not doing more. And... standing here now, face to face with Ethea, the regret felt heavier than ever.
It took her a few minutes to push it down and put on a smile.
"...T-Thank you... I ...I have been great." But the words barely managed to leave her throat. "What... about you? Have you been well?"
’...Urgh. I messed up.’
Fortunately, Ethea didn’t seem to mind it. "I have been great too. And... what brings you here?"

"I... I’m sorry for visiting without notice." Roya took a small breath and straightened her posture. "And I’m sorry for not coming to see you after the incident. I wanted to, but by the time I found a way, you were already gone."
Ethea listened quietly, her expression unreadable.
"I know that’s not a good excuse." Roya’s hands curled at her sides. "But now that you’re here... if there’s anything I can do, I want to help."
Ethea was silent for a moment, then shook her head. "You don’t need to apologize. Knowing you were worried is more than enough... Senior Sister Roya."
Roya’s eyes lit up at the familiar address. For the first time since entering the room, a genuine smile broke through her composed mask.

"But I really want to help you." Her voice softened. "Please, let me do something. Even if it’s small." Her gaze flickered toward the wheelchair, then back to Ethea’s face. "If there’s anything you need, anything at all..."
Ethea studied her for a moment, and the faint curve of her lips returned. "Then... sit with me and watch the competition for a while." She gestured to the chair beside her. "That will be enough."
"Are you sure?" Roya asked.
Ethea nodded and turned back toward the window, while removing her mask.

Roya took the seat beside her, still unsure what to say, until she noticed where Ethea’s gaze had settled. It was fixed on one person, and only one person. She followed that gaze down to the stage below and landed on that very person.
’...Soren Everly.’
He was focused on his work, his hands moving with practiced precision. There was nothing flashy about him, and yet the way he moved spoke of someone who had spent years perfecting his craft.
’...How did he manage to marry someone like her?’
’...She didn’t get seduced by his looks, right?’

Before she could ponder it further, Soren raised his head and glanced in their direction. For a split second, Roya froze, certain he was looking at her. But then she realized his gaze was aimed past her. She quickly turned her head to the right and froze.
Ethea... was smiling. Her eyes were warm, her expression soft, and she was looking at Soren as if he was the only person in the entire arena, or perhaps in the entire world...
Roya’s mind went blank.

She had known Ethea for years, had seen her in battle and at classes, and not once had she ever seen that kind of smile on her face. It wasn’t the polite curve of a noblewoman or the composed mask of a warrior. It was... the kind of smile a woman wore when she looked at the person she loved with all her heart. And it suited Ethea more than anything Roya had ever seen before.
Roya’s gaze shifted back to the man on the stage, then to Ethea, then back again.
’...I think I understand now.’

She felt a little stupid for all the wild theories she had come up with yesterday and even just now. While she might not be as strong as Ethea, she knew enough about the relationship between a man and a woman to recognize this.
’This is... pure love.’
The realization settled over her like a blanket, pressing down on every doubt she had carried into this room.

And for the first time since stepping into this room, she found herself truly at a loss for words. Not because she was nervous or didn’t know what to say, but because she felt like an intruder, watching something that should have been private.
She turned her gaze away from Ethea and looked down at her own hands. ’...I hope he knows how lucky he is.’
Then, after a long pause, she let out a soft breath and spoke. "So... you got married?"
"..." Ethea’s ’special’ smile vanished as she turned toward Roya. "That’s right. Sorry for not inviting you."
Roya froze for a second, realizing how her question had sounded. She hadn’t meant to make it seem like she was upset about not being invited.

"No, I didn’t mean it like that," she said quickly. "I was just surprised, that’s all." She fumbled for the right words. "I mean... How did it even happen? And why him? Is he truly... I mean, is he worthy of you? He seems... ordinary..."

Before Ethea could respond, Roya added hastily, "I don’t mean any offense. I can see how much you care for each other. It’s just... the Ethea I knew wouldn’t have settled for just anyone or been interested in such matters..." Her voice trailed off, and she found herself unable to meet Ethea’s eyes.
’...Urgh, just what am I saying?’

It was always like this. Whenever the topic turned to Ethea, Roya’s mind became a tangled mess. She could never tell if it was because of the countless times she had lost to her in spars despite being her senior, or because the admiration she carried was so deep that it made her overthink every single word. Either way, the result was the same. She always ended up sounding like a fool and overthinking things.
Fortunately, Ethea replied in time to save her from further embarrassment.

"I can’t tell you the details right now," Ethea said, her voice calm but sincere. "But I can tell you with certainty that Soren is more than I ever deserved. In fact, I believe I’m the one who isn’t worthy of him."
"Huh?" Roya became dumbfounded. "W-What do you mean?"
"He..." Ethea’s gaze drifted back toward Soren. "He gave up so much for me. And... he never once made me feel like a burden, even when I couldn’t do anything for myself..."

She paused, then turned back to Roya, her tone shifting slightly, growing colder. "Your Highness, while we may have been close in the past, I would appreciate it if you didn’t look down on my husband."
Roya flinched, opening her mouth to apologize. "I wasn’t-"
"I know you didn’t mean it that way." Ethea’s expression softened, though her voice remained indifferent. "But if you ever speak of him like that again..."

chapters.title: Chapter 267: Golden Ladle Championship [4]
paragraphs: "But if you ever speak of him like that again..."

Roya felt a shiver run down her spine at Ethea’s words, so she didn’t even register the rest of her words. For that brief moment, she even forgot she was the mighty princess and Ethea the one in the wheelchair. She then realized the situation and cleared her mind of distracting thoughts. "You’re right, Ethea. I shouldn’t have spoken like that or meddled in your private life. For that, I sincerely apologize. I just hope you can forgive my rudeness."
"...Ok," Ethea replied after a moment. "Please, don’t repeat such a mistake again."
Roya nodded in understanding.
"Speaking of which..." Ethea glanced at her. "When areyougetting married, Senior?"

"Huh? Me?" Roya was caught off guard again. "I... I have been busy lately and haven’t had time for such matters. Furthermore... You know how the Imperial Family arranges marriages. I don’t think I will have much of a say in it when the time comes."
"Thank you for your kind wishes."
"Mmm. Now, shall we continue watching?"
"Ah, yes. Of course." Roya agreed hastily and turned her attention to the arena.
Minutes passed in silence, and Roya’s inner curiosity only kept increasing. She didn’t speak because she feared she would mess up and make another mistake.

"...Your Highness, we’ll be leaving tomorrow." Ethea said, breaking the quiet. "So you don’t have to make any arrangements for us. I know you want to help, but the best help you can give right now is not to do anything."
"...I understand." Roya reluctantly nodded, realizing why Ethea said that. ’She probably doesn’t want to draw attention to herself or her husband. But...’

"What about the competition?" Roya asked, because she could understand that Ethea’s husband was unknown and that it didn’t matter if he left the competition. But at the same time, he had talent and passion; it was obvious even without the reports Roya received. "Is it really ok to just leave like this? He might have a chance of winning."

Ethea went silent for a moment. "...It’s ok. He will have plenty of chances to prove himself later. Besides, he is doing it just for fun. If he takes it seriously, his chances of winning the tournament would be extremely high. But right now... There are more important things than winning a trophy."

"...I don’t understand what could be that important, but I believe you have your reasons." Roya let out a sigh. "Alright, as you requested, I won’t do anything. But... I hope you will contact me if you need any help."
Roya stood up, took something out of her ring, and handed it to Ethea. "I am going to take my leave now. ...Take care."
"...Thank you." Ethea accepted the item and nodded. "And... Till we meet again.
Roya nodded back, put on her hoodie, and left the room, leaving a single phrase behind.
’...Be careful.’
"..." Ethea stared at the door intensely for a moment before turning back to the arena. ’Be careful, huh... Then, we should leave before something happens...’
[Soren Everly: Pass]
Soren squinted as he saw himself among the 10 people who passed to the semi-finals.

’The rules were a bit stranger than I expected, but the process wasn’t that different from the Expert Magic Chef exam.’ He thought as he analyzed it. ’They probably wanted to sort out the strongest candidates this way.’
Furthermore, he also learned about the rules for the semi-finals and that 3 people would advance to the finals.
’That way, they won’t have to hold another round for 3rd place. They will find out about it directly in the finals...’

While there was an ingredient he really needed for third place, he had long decided to let it go. It wasn’t worth the risk of drawing more attention to himself or delaying their departure any further. Ethea’s safety, reuniting with Ryan and his family, and rescuing his little sister came first.
’...Though there might be a way to get it without staying for the whole tournament.’
The thought lingered as he slowly took his leave, doing his best to avoid the reporters and other contestants.
’I am already in the semi-finals, so if I participate in it and manage to get into the finals, the first half of the work will be done.’

In the finals, he would just forfeit or not participate at all, which would automatically make him third place. As for the rewards, he could have President Doran collect them on his behalf and send them to him later.
’...I’ll have to discuss it with Ethea and President Doran later.’
There was a chance it might not be allowed after all.
’Let’s hope for the best...’
’...So, what do you think?’
’...That’s actually a great idea,’ Ethea replied after a short pause. ’But is it actually possible? Did you talk about it with President Doran?’

’Yes, I met with him after advancing to the semi-finals.’ Soren answered, recalling how he’d been caught by him after escaping the reporters. ’He agreed to help, but with one condition. He... wanted me to have participated as a candidate from Bagdad’s Magic Chef Association.’
’...That’s it?’

’That’s it. He said having a contestant reach the finals under Baghdad’s name would be good publicity for the branch and also the people of the city. It looks like it has been over a decade since a local candidate made it that far.’ Soren let out a small chuckle. ’While he might have had some ulterior motives, I think he truly wanted to give the people something to be proud of again.’
’...’ Ethea smiled at Soren’s words. ’Then, did you accept it?’
’...I was going to, but I decided to discuss it with you first.’

’...Thank you, but you really didn’t have to ask me. This is something you wanted to do, isn’t it? I trust your judgment.’ She paused, her voice softening. ’But, more than anything, I still want you to do it for yourself. Because... you deserve to have something you enjoy, and I don’t want to take that away from you.’
’...Alright, I will enjoy it as much as I can.’

"Faris, must you introduce me like that every single time?" Layla let out a helpless sigh, though from the look on her face, it was obvious she was satisfied with it.
"Of course! It’s part of the charm, and I’m just speaking the truth." Faris grinned and winked at her before turning back to the arena. "Now then, who’s ready for another exciting round?"
"YEAH!"
"ME!"
"LET’S START ALREADY!"
The crowd roared back in response.

"Haha, now, now, please calm down." Faris made an exaggerated gesture. "I know you’ve been waiting for the semi-finals since yesterday, especially after that special ’news’. But don’t worry, you won’t have to wait much longer. In just a few minutes, all contestants will take their stations, and we will be able to uncover who this ’Bagdad’s Savior’ is!"
The crowd erupted once again, as most of them were locals.
"I wonder who they are to Master Doran to praise them so much," Layla added with a pondering expression.
"Hehe, did you just read my mind?" Faris chuckled. "Because I was thinking the same thing; I couldn’t even sleep last night!"
"..." Layla gave him an ’At least give a convincing lie’ look.

"Why are you looking at me like that? I’m not lying, I swear." Faris defended himself but quickly shifted the topic. "Anyway! Let’s not waste any more time and talk about who the savior might actually be!"
"...Ok, let’s go with that."
"First, we can rule out Senior Chef Damir since he represents his hometown, the capital city."
"True. We can also..."
The two discussed and settled on three candidates with mysterious backgrounds.
"...That leaves us with three candidates."
"Senior Chef Nuelia, Chef Dobby, and Chef Soren.
"...and Chef Soren."
’...Damn it.’ Soren cursed inwardly. ’If I knew it would be like this, I wouldn’t have agreed.’

He had sent his agreement to President Doran yesterday and then woke up to see this in the morning. He hadn’t expected it to blow up like this. Although his identity as the so-called ’Bagdad’s Savior’ hadn’t been revealed yet, the media had already started speculating. Every major outlet ran the same story, calling it the ’Return of Bagdad?’ and so on. And now, his face was being shown to everyone on the big screens along with the two other ’possible saviors’.
’...I made a mistake.’
He shouldn’t have trusted Doran at all. The man had clearly used this to stir up the city, and now Soren was the center of attention.
’...No, it should be the work of those attention-hungry reporters.’

Because he had seen actual video of an official announcement, it was the media who twisted it into what it was now. The dramatic titles, the wild speculation, the sudden wave of public support. They had turned a simple announcement into a frenzy.
’No... I should’ve expected it.’

Because this was how the world worked: a story like this - an unknown contestant rising through the ranks, doing their best to represent a ’fallen’ city - was the kind of story the reporters dreamed of.
’Hah... Whatever.’
’I’ll just do what I intended to do and leave.’

He took a deep breath, and as the contestants were called to the arena, he stepped forward with the rest of them. The noise of the crowd washed over him like a wave, and dozens of cameras turned to track their movements. His name was already being called from somewhere in the stands. He ignored it and walked straight to his station, his expression calm and unreadable.
The rules were reminded to them once again, and then the main screen lit up with the countdown.

Unlike the previous rounds, they were pretty generous with the time limit, probably because there was no fixed theme this time. They could make whatever they wanted, as long as it showed creativity while being close to the original recipe and expressed who they were as a chef.
While the other contestants soon started moving, Soren kept staring at his station, frozen like a statue.
And everyone noticed it.
"Chef Soren seems to be taking his time," Faris remarked, his voice carrying across the broadcast. "Do you think the pressure is getting to him?"
"He’s been the center of attention since this morning," Layla added. "It’s possible he’s still trying to block it all out. So, let’s just hope for the best."
"Right, right." Faris nodded and his eyes lit up. "Perhaps he’s waiting for inspiration to strike. Some chefs do their best thinking when they’re like that, you know."
"Whatever it is, I hope he finds it soon. The clock is ticking."
"Yeah, I agree with you on that. While three hours might feel like a long time, it might disappear faster than people expect."
"Well, we are talking about time after all..."

While the hosts were still in the middle of discussing his lack of movement, Soren was hearing none of that. It was as if he was disconnected from reality, his attention fixed entirely on the task. And just like that, twenty minutes passed and...
"LOOK!" Faris pointed at the stage. "HE’S MOVING!"
"Finally." Layla let out a relieved breath. "It seems he’s made his decision. I was starting to worry he’d spend the whole first hour just standing there."
"Same here. But look at him go! That’s not the movement of someone who’s unsure. That’s the movement of a man with a plan."

The cameras focused on Soren as he worked. His movements were quick and precise, and the way he picked and handled each ingredient made it clear he had already mapped out every step in his head. The earlier stillness was gone, replaced by the kind of concentration that made people stop and watch.
"Looks like he wasn’t stressed after all," Layla observed. "But the real question is what he’s planning to make."
"Whatever it is, it better be worth the wait." Faris grinned. "After all, all the candidates here are incredible in their own way."
"Look at Grandmaster Tamimi’s apprentice, Master Damir." Layla skillfully picked up the topic. "His techniques are similar to those of his master, but I can see he added his own flair to them."
"Urgh, I wish I could eat them too." Faris gulped, wiping away the drool with his sleeve. "I really envy the judges."

chapters.title: Chapter 269: Golden Ladle Championship [6]
paragraphs: [Ding!]
"The Semi-Finals have officially come to an end!" Faris declared, his voice echoing through the arena. "All the contestants, please step back from your stations."
As instructed, the contestants moved away, their expressions either tense or calm.

"Now, let us explain the new rules for the judging process," Layla added. "This round will be scored differently from the previous ones. Each contestant will present their dish individually, explaining the inspiration, why they made it, and so on. The judges will taste and give their scores, but there is one more new rule this year."
"That’s right, everyone!" Faris leaned forward with a grin. "This time, contestants will also judge each other!"
The spectators let out exclamations while contestants had surprised looks on their faces.
"Wait, let me explain." Faris raised his hand to calm them down. "It is a bit different and separate from the official panel’s scoring."

"Just like the official judges, you will get to witness their presentation and taste their dish," Layla explained to the contestants. "However, you will have to give points to them using scorecards from one to ten. The average will be added to the final score, so your opinions will matter too."

"In fact, they might end up deciding the winners." Faris let the words hang for a moment before adding in a solemn voice. "However, I advise you to judge fairly and honestly. After all, countless eyes are watching this stage, and your reputation as chefs will be shaped by how you handle this moment."

"He’s right." Layla joined. "And I trust you won’t let personal feelings or tricks influence your judgment. Because at the end of the day, this is a cooking competition, and the best dishes deserve to be recognized."
"Mm, let’s see whose work truly stands out from the rest."

Applause rippled through the stands as the screens lit up with the order of presentation. From the looks of it, it was decided based on who finished first. So, Grandmaster Tamimi’s apprentice, Damir, was the first to present his dish.
He stepped forward with confidence, a covered plate in his hands for the judges, while assistants followed behind him with smaller portions for the other contestants.
"SENIOR DAMIR!"
"BEST CHEF!"

Cheers filled the arena as he took his place on the platform. They were so loud that the organizers had to activate the sound-blocking barrier. Only then, perhaps realizing they were overdoing it, did they stop. Well, most of them.
As for Chef Damir, he calmly tapped the mic and checked it.
"Are you ready, Chef Damir?"
"Yes."
"Good, then you can start."
Damir took a deep breath and removed the cover from his dish.
A rich aroma immediately spread through the air, while its appearance drew murmurs from the spectators.
"Wait... Isn’t that?"
"Yeah, it’s definitely that."
"But why?"

As if hearing their words despite the sound-blocking barrier, Damir spoke up. "You are all right. This is my master’s signature dish, one many call Tamimi’s Special. However... It is also my own creation."
Confused and curious expressions spread across the crowd and even among some of the contestants. Murmurs intensified.
"While it might look similar, the taste, the ingredients, and the techniques behind it are entirely my own. Its effects are much stronger and more refined than the original."
He paused, letting the curious judges inspect the plates.

"A disciple must learn from their master. But learning doesn’t mean copying everything. It means understanding the foundation well enough to build something new on top of it. This dish is my answer to everything my master taught me... Respect for tradition, but without the fear of change."
He inclined his head slightly. "Please enjoy."

The judges lifted their utensils, and the crowd watched in silence as they took their first bites. A few moments passed as they took a few more, with one judge’s eyes widening with each bite, while another nodded as if to confirm something to himself. The others, including the other contestants, had similar expressions, but it was obvious they all liked it.
Soren first used appraisal to check the dish and then took a bite.
As he chewed and swallowed, his lips curled up in satisfaction. In a few moments, he finished the dish, a thought settling in his mind.
’No wonder he sounded so confident.’
He had never eaten so-called Tamimi’s special before, but after eating this one, he wouldn’t be surprised if it was on the same level, or even surpassed the original.

’Perhaps this is also his way of addressing all the others, as they always keep addressing him as Tamimi’s disciple first. Must have been frustrating, always being someone else’s shadow. Fortunately, it looks like he created it while still respecting his master, not out of resentment.’

He stole a glance at Damir, who was staring at the judges. Then, as if sensing his gaze, Damir turned toward him. Soren smiled, nodded, and received a small nod in return from Damir, along with the faintest hint of a smile before the chef looked away.
Soren also turned back, turning his attention to the floating status screen in his vision.
’Hmm... 7th Circle potential... S-rank Fire Affinity... Oh...’
Time passed, and just as he finished, it was time to score.

The judges ended up reaching a similar conclusion and gave him high points. One of them gave slightly lower, commenting that Damir was trying to outshine his master with this underhanded method and, as a fan of Grandmaster Tamimi, they didn’t like it. Surprisingly, Damir accepted the criticism calmly and made no comment.
Then it was the contestants’ turn. The scorecards went up one by one. There were two eights, one seven, four nines, and two tens. Soren was one of those who gave a ten.
They calculated the average and added it to Damir’s official score.
"Thank you all..."
Damir gave a little speech and bowed politely before leaving the platform and taking his designated seat below.
The main screen updated with his total score and the crowd buzzed with cheers. Thus, the first presentation was finally over, with the bar already set high.
"Next..."
The contestants were called one by one and presented their meals. As expected, none of them managed to surpass Damir’s score. And finally, it was the second-strongest candidate’s turn.
"Are you ready, Chef Nuelia?"
Soren watched as the mysterious candidate climbed to the platform.
"...Yes." Her melodic voice echoed.
"Then, you may begin."

Nuelia nodded gracefully and then raised her hand. With a snap of her fingers, the mana around her rippled, and slowly, her appearance began to change. Her long green hair took a vibrant, livelier shade, while her ears lengthened to elegant points, her features becoming much sharper. Even her aura changed, radiating a strong but gentle pressure.
A ripple of shock swept through the arena as the audience gasped.
"A-An elf?!"
"She was an elf?"
"Whoa!"

Soren widened his eyes, playing along with the crowd’s surprise even though he had known the truth for a while, all thanks to his appraisal ability. Beside him, some of the other contestants were openly staring, with even Damir changing his usual stoic expression.

"..." Nuelia smiled softly, her expression calm despite all the commotion she just caused. "I chose to hide my race until now because I wanted to be judged solely for my skills." She said, her voice carrying through the arena. "I apologize if this startled any of you. I swear that I never meant to deceive you."
"Oh, so that was the reason..."
"But did she really have to hide her race?"
The crowd’s initial shock began to settle. Whispers still spread through the strands, but the tone had already shifted from doubt and suspicion to understanding and curiosity.

"Now, now, everyone." Faris took the opportunity to jump in. "There’s no need to be surprised. We just received a message from the organizers. They informed us that she had registered with her real identity from the very beginning. It just wasn’t made public until now."
The crowd nodded in acceptance.

"But I have to say," Faris turned toward Nuelia with a playful grin, "no wonder I felt so drawn to you this whole time. It was because you were an elf all along. And... you must have hidden it because you feared completely charming the entire arena."
He leaned in closer, his expression becoming a bit embarrassed.
"But the truth is... I was already charmed long before I knew. And if I start forgetting my lines," he turned to the audience, "you all know who to blame now."
"...Pfft."
"Haha!"
In an instant, laughter rippled through the stands, the atmosphere becoming livelier once again.
Even Nuelia herself giggled at his shamelessness, shaking her head as if she couldn’t quite believe what she had just heard.
"Haha-o-ow!"

Faris’s laughter was cut short as a certain someone pinched him on the arm. He turned to the culprit with an ’angry’ expression, but when he saw their ’smiling’ face, he gulped and quickly turned back to the camera. "Ahem. A-Anyway! W-What was I saying?"
"...PFFT!"
"Hahaha!"

chapters.title: Chapter 270: Golden Ladle Championship [7]
paragraphs: The laughter soon died down.
Nuelia bowed politely with a smile. "Thank you, Mr. Faris. And you’re right. We all know who to blame if you start forgetting your lines now."

Laughter echoed through the arena again as Faris became the target of the joke once more. Layla sighed before turning in Nuelia’s direction. "I apologize if my co-host said anything strange. He was just trying to lighten the mood." She paused, her smile becoming genuinely curious. "But if I may ask, why did you choose to reveal it now?"

"It’s because," Nuelia replied, "I wanted my dish to be understood in its true context. Hiding my identity would have been hiding part of the story behind it and might have caused some misunderstandings."
"Oh, I see." Layla nodded in understanding. "Then, you can continue your presentation. Good luck."

"Thank you." Nuelia bowed politely, then turned back to the judges. "Actually, the story behind it isn’t anything special or meaningful. But to me, it means a lot..." She paused and took a deep breath. "It is actually a traditional elvin dish my late grandma used to make me when I was a child. I still remember the delicious smell that filled the kitchen when she cooked, and the melody of her voice as she hummed while stirring the pot. She used to give the biggest portion to me too. And I really loved it. In fact, it was one of the reasons I became a chef. And... I wanted to share that memory with all of you, even if it’s a little different from what she used to make. I hope you will enjoy it and share your honest thoughts with me."
She bowed again and ended her speech.
Applauses filled the arena.
’So that’s why she became a chef...’
Soren muttered inwardly as he picked up his spoon.

’But I guess she’s really on the vegetarian side.’ He added as he scanned the dish. She cooked only vegetables, grains, herbs, and so on, while arranging them to look as natural as possible. Even the portion in front of him looked more like a small garden than a meal. If it weren’t for his ability and the subtle mana flowing through it, he might have mistaken it for a salad. ’This proves elves truly love nature... Well, that guy is an exception since he used to devour any food without caring whether it was meat or plants.’ The thought of his old elven coworker made him smile a little. ’I guess no race is a monolith...’
’Anyway, let’s eat.’
He took the first bite and his thoughts stilled. And just like he did with any other meal, he quickly finished eating. But there was something else that caught his attention.
’It really improves your life force!’
He was a bit suspicious when he saw it on the status, but now that he had experienced it himself, he knew it was true.
’...Well, the ability had never made a mistake, so I guess I was just being a bit skeptical because of the effect.’
After all, he had been looking for recipes that increased one’s life force all this time and knew how incredibly rare they were.
’...I should meet her before we leave.’ Soren decided as the scoring period started. ’And get that recipe.’

His mind started racing as he thought about how to approach her. A dish that could improve life force was the exact thing needed to cure Ethea, and if he could learn the recipe or trade for it, it might be worth more than any prize of this tournament. But he would have to prepare something of equal value too...
While he kept thinking, it was time for them to give their scores. Since he really liked it and it deserved the score even without the effect, he gave it a third 10. It was his third one.
"Next, Candidate Soren, please come to the stage."
"...Huh?" Soren made a dumbfounded face. ’Is it already my turn?’
Then realization washed over him.

’Right, Nuelia was the ninth, and I was the last to finish. I must have forgotten about it.’ He let out a sigh, stood up, and walked toward the platform. Now, all the attention was focused on him. Since all the others had already stated their affiliations, his identity as the ’Bagdad’s Savior’ was already set in stone. ’...Let’s just focus on the task at hand.’
"Are you ready, Chef Soren?"
"Yes."
"Then, you may begin."
Soren nodded and presented his dish; it resembled a broth, but at the same time, it didn’t look like one. It was both darker and clear at the same time, which confused the audience and the judges.
"I call this ’Brother of Life’. I won’t say anything else and let you experience it for yourselves." He inclined his head slightly. "Please, enjoy."

One judge’s face twisted slightly, as if they had eaten something bitter. Another one looked like she wanted to put the spoon down but barely managed to force herself to swallow.
The fellow contestants’ reactions were similar as well, with one even drinking three cups of water in a row while taking ragged breaths.
"Huh? What’s happening?" Faris leaned forward, his usual playful tone replaced by confusion. "They are all reacting... badly, I think?"
"...Right." Layla joined in. "It looks like something went wrong with the dish."
"Could it be... Chef Soren... failed?" Faris asked doubtfully. "But... it doesn’t look like he is worried about it. In fact, he looks like everything is under his control and expectations."
"That’s what makes it so confusing," Layla muttered. "I wish we could really taste them too, even if they are bitter."
"I have been saying that since day one!" Faris exclaimed. "And I really love bitter meals, you know! I always add a pepper to my meals."
"..." Layla stared at him with a deadpan look.
"What! I’m not lying!" Faris defended himself again. "I swear!"
Just as he was about to make up an excuse, they noticed something strange again. Faris frowned, his confusion deepening.
"Hey, why are they reacting like this now?"

chapters.title: Chapter 271: The Broth of Life
paragraphs: "Look at them!" Faris pointed at the judges. "It looks like they are swimming in the clouds!"
"...Just what in the world is going on?" Layla muttered in confusion. "Chef Soren... didn’t make some kind of drug... did he?"
"...My lady," Faris said, staring at her with a deadpan expression this time. "Even I think that’s going too far."
"I know!" Layla exclaimed. "But look at them!"

She pointed at the judges and contestants whose previous frowning and grimaces had now turned to one of pure bliss. One judge was leaning back in his chair, staring at the sky with a peaceful smile, as if he was happy with life, while another one was even crying.
One of them kept drinking spoon after spoon, first with a painful expression and then, after some time, smiling as if they had drunk the sweetest drink in existence.
To those who were watching, it looked really strange.
"...Alright, I take that back," Faris muttered, but then his eyes lit up. "Wait! I think I know what’s going on!"
"You do?" Layla stared at him in surprise. After all, she was a Master Chef and hadn’t figured it out yet, so how could a Junior Chef like Faris do it?
"Yes, yes! Do you remember what Chef Soren called his dish?" Faris grinned. "’Broth of Life’!"
"Urgh... Isn’t it obvious?" Faris grimaced at Layla’s clueless look. "There was a deeper meaning to it. He must have intentionally given that name and made the soup bitter or spicy."
"!" Layla’s eyes lit up this time, realization crossing his features. "I-I get it now! Everything makes sense now."
"Hehe, I guess it finally clicked for you too." Faris chuckled with a smug expression. "There’s no need to thank me, though."
"...Chef Soren really planned everything from the start. He understood the rules and prepared the best dish he could. No! He... He prepared a story!"
"...Hey, don’t ignore me!" Faris weakly added as Layla kept speaking. "..."
"A story anyone could easily connect and relate to! Life! And for most people, life is always bitter!" Layla’s smile grew wider. "Chef Soren... He... He’s a genius!
"...Alright, I can agree with you on that too." Faris let out a helpless sigh. "But... Will that be enough for him to pass to the finals?"
"Hmm? What are you talking about?" Layla looked at him in confusion. "I can say with certainty that he’s definitely gonna advance. He might even take first place in this round."
"He’s that amazing?" Faris made a surprised expression, his expression turning solemn again. "In that case, let’s wait and see how it will actually turn out in the end."
"Mm, I can’t wait to hear their opinions, though."
"We all can’t..."
Faris was right. Spectators, including Ethea, President Doran, and even Princess Roya and City Lord Asad, were waiting for the judging period to end and for the scores to be announced.
Fortunately, they didn’t have to wait for long, as the judges soon finished the whole meal.
"Chef Soren, that was an incredible experience. Thank you for giving us such an amazing dish." The head judge said with a smile. "I will give you the highest score."
"Me too!" The judge who rated Damir low spoke. "Although I don’t really like bitter meals, you really captured the essence. I really loved the philosophy you put behind it."

"I will give a perfect score too." The next judge, the one who cried, added enthusiastically. "The dish itself was amazing, but the story you gave us was something else. You portrayed life with just a simple meal. I have no words to describe how much it moved me."
"I have nothing to add except that I’ll be thinking about this dish for a long time."
All the judges gave their opinions, which were mostly thanking and praising him. Soren thanked them all each time, and at the end, he managed to get a perfect score from all the judges.
Then it was time for the contestants to give their scores.
"I..." Damir spoke. "I admit it. You definitely won this round, Chef Soren. Congratulations."
He raised the ten scoreboard. The other contestants followed his lead and gave him 10 as well.

The queue finally came to the last judge contestant, Nuelia. She looked at Soren, a mysterious smile playing at her lips. "I didn’t think I would meet a rare talent like you in here, Mr. Soren. You really surprised me."

She glanced at the empty bowl in front of her. "At first, I was like everyone else, caught off guard by that bitter taste. But as I forced myself to swallow it, everything slowly changed. It was then I realized it... what you really created." She paused, letting the momentum build. "You wanted to describe ’life’ in your own words. That life is bitter and always throws problems at you, but if you accept and endure them, the reward you get at the end is sweeter than anything else. Well, at least that is the message I received. And I was really moved by it. Thank you for letting me experience such a thing."
She bowed in gratitude before raising another perfect 10 score.
"...Thank you, Lady Nuelia." Soren bowed in return.
And in an instant, the arena exploded in cheers.
"YEAH!"
"A PERFECT SCORE?! THAT NEVER HAPPENED BEFORE, RIGHT?!"
"AMAZING!"
"HE SET A RECORD!"
"CHEF SOREN!"
"HE IS BAGDAD’S SAVIOR!"
Meanwhile, the main screen was updated, and in a matter of seconds, Soren’s name shot to the top of the list.

Soren watched the scene with a smile on his face, his heartbeat still racing as the crowd’s cheers and applause washed over him. Honestly, he couldn’t believe what was happening. After all, he had just entered the competition on a whim, but now he was standing at the top of the rankings, surrounded by fellow chefs who had trained perhaps their entire lives for this stage. It felt...
’...surreal.’
’...’ He couldn’t help but look in Ethea’s direction again, his smile deepening. ’...Thank you. ...Dear.’
A heartbeat passed, and a gentle reply echoed in his mind.
’...Silly. Why are you thanking me? I didn’t do anything.’
’You did.’ Soren replied as he slowly turned away from that direction. ’...More than you know.’
