chapters.title: Chapter 272: Bagdad’s Savior
paragraphs: "Ladies and Gentlemen! The Semi-Final of the Golden Ladle Championship has finally come to an end." Faris announced loudly. "And I have to say, this was the best semi-final I have ever witnessed in my life!"
"It truly was." Lady Layla nodded beside him. "Every chef brought something special to the stage, but what we witnessed today was something beyond our expectations."

"We had an apprentice announcing his independence from his master’s shadow, a young man expressing his love for the love of his life, an elven chef revealing her heritage and past with pride, and finally, a dark horse turning the entire arena upside down." Faris gestured toward the stage, his voice rising with excitement. "If this is just the semi-final, I can only imagine what the final is gonna be like."

"Although everyone is already aware, let us still announce the finalists." Layla smiled and turned toward the main screen. "The three chefs who will be moving on to the final round of the Golden Ladle Championship."
"First is Chef Damir, who finished in third place, with 62 points."
Applause filled the arena.
"Second is Chef Nuelia, who finished in second place, with 64,2 points."
The applause intensified.
"And finally, the star of the Semi-Final, Bagdad’s Savior Chef Soren, who finished in first place with a perfect score of 70!"
The arena erupted once again, the excitement reaching its peak. Soren’s name echoed through the stands, chanted by thousands of voices as the main screen displayed his name in glowing golden letters.
As for the protagonist of the moment, he simply stood there with a smile on his face, accepting the cheers while occasionally waving his hand.

’...So this is what it feels like to be recognized... to be liked...’ His chest felt warm, though he couldn’t tell if it was from the adrenaline pumping through his veins or the sheer weight of the crowd’s affection. But...
It definitely wasn’t a bad feeling. In fact, he liked it more than he wanted to admit. However, he also felt conflicted and guilty. After all, he was going to leave the city today.
’...Should we stay for another day?’
He asked himself, but couldn’t bring himself to answer.

The crowd was still cheering, the cameras still focused on him, and the weight of their expectations was starting to settle on his shoulders. If he... If he left now, he would be walking away from all of this. From the finals. From the chance to see how far he could really go.
However... staying meant more attention, questions, and definitely more risk.
’...What should I do?’

Fortunately, the closing ceremony gave him the excuse to move. He bowed once more toward the crowd, then stepped down from the stage and walked toward the exit. The noise slowly faded behind him, replaced by the hum of the arena’s inner corridors.
Just then, a hand landed on his shoulder.
He turned to find Damir standing there, his expression calm as always.
"Let’s both do our best tomorrow," he said. "I will be looking forward to it."
Soren studied him for a moment, then nodded. "Likewise."
Damir held his gaze for a moment longer, then turned and walked away without another word.
Soren exhaled and was about to continue when another voice echoed behind him.
"Mr. Soren."
He turned to find Nuelia standing a few steps away, her green hair catching the light as she watched him with a faint smile.
"Lady Nuelia." Soren inclined his head slightly. "Do you need something?"
"Mr. Soren..." She hesitated for a moment before asking. "Would it be possible for us to have a talk after this?"
Soren blinked, caught off guard for a moment. "Yes, it would be my pleasure."

He didn’t mention the fact that he had already thought of more than twenty ways to approach her but never settled on one. Yet now, here she was, asking him herself. It was almost funny how things worked out sometimes.
"Then let’s walk together." She gestured toward the path ahead with a bright smile. "We can talk on the way."

"Sure." Soren nodded. "Where should we go? A restaurant or a cafe?" He paused, considering the festival crowds outside. With their identities, he doubted whether they could even move through the streets without being crowded. "I guess somewhere private and peaceful would be better.
Nuelia smiled knowingly. "I have just the place. And you don’t have to worry about us getting recognized. I am a bit skilled in illusion magic, so it shouldn’t be a problem."
She lifted her hand and said something in a language Soren couldn’t understand. Then, a faint sensation and shimmer washed over him, barely visible before fading away.
"There. Now, no one will pay us any mind."

Soren blinked and glanced down at himself. He didn’t feel any different, but when he looked at Nuelia, her features seemed slightly blurry, as if his eyes couldn’t focus on her. "...This’s a handy trick."
"It has its uses." She smiled and gestured for him to follow. "Come, I will take you there."
"Wait." Soren stopped her. "Can I bring someone else with me? My wife, to be more exact."
Nuelia made a surprised expression. "You... are married?"
"Yes." Soren nodded, raising his hand to show the wedding ring. "I can guess why you’re surprised. After all, most elves don’t marry this early."
"...Right." Nuelia chuckled. "And of course, you can bring her with you."
"Thank you." Soren smiled back. "Then, should we part ways here and meet up later, or will you accompany me to pick her up first and then head to the place you mentioned?"

Nuelia pondered for a moment before replying. "...Let’s do this instead. We will part ways here. You will go get your wife while I go meet my own people and let them know about our meeting. Then, we can meet at the exit."
"Sounds good." Soren nodded. "However, let’s exchange contact info just in case."
"Good idea." Nuelia took out her own device. "...Done."
As they finished exchanging numbers, Nuelia pocketed her phone back into her robes and gave him a small smile. "I will see you both then."
"Mm, see you soon."

"Lady Nuelia." Soren inclined his head slightly.
"Do you need something?"
"Mr.
Soren..." She hesitated for a moment before asking.
"Would it be possible for us to have a talk after this?"
Soren blinked, caught off guard for a moment.
"Yes, it would be my pleasure."
He didn’t mention the fact that he had already thought of more than twenty ways to approach her but never settled on one.
Yet now, here she was, asking him herself.
It was almost funny how things worked out sometimes.
"Then let’s walk together." She gestured toward the path ahead with a bright smile.
"We can talk on the way."
"Sure." Soren nodded.
"Where should we go?
A restaurant or a cafe?" He paused, considering the festival crowds outside.
With their identities, he doubted whether they could even move through the streets without being crowded.
"I guess somewhere private and peaceful would be better.
Nuelia smiled knowingly.
"I have just the place.
And you don’t have to worry about us getting recognized.
I am a bit skilled in illusion magic, so it shouldn’t be a problem."
She lifted her hand and said something in a language Soren couldn’t understand.
Then, a faint sensation and shimmer washed over him, barely visible before fading away.
"There.
Now, no one will pay us any mind."
Soren blinked and glanced down at himself.
He didn’t feel any different, but when he looked at Nuelia, her features seemed slightly blurry, as if his eyes couldn’t focus on her.
"...This’s a handy trick."
"It has its uses." She smiled and gestured for him to follow.
"Come, I will take you there."
"Wait." Soren stopped her.
"Can I bring someone else with me?
My wife, to be more exact."
Nuelia made a surprised expression.
"You... are married?"
"Yes." Soren nodded, raising his hand to show the wedding ring.
"I can guess why you’re surprised.
After all, most elves don’t marry this early."
"...Right." Nuelia chuckled.
"And of course, you can bring her with you."
"Thank you." Soren smiled back.
"Then, should we part ways here and meet up later, or will you accompany me to pick her up first and then head to the place you mentioned?"
Nuelia pondered for a moment before replying.
"...Let’s do this instead.
We will part ways here.
You will go get your wife while I go meet my own people and let them know about our meeting.
Then, we can meet at the exit."
"Sounds good." Soren nodded.
"However, let’s exchange contact info just in case."
"Good idea." Nuelia took out her own device.
"...Done."
As they finished exchanging numbers, Nuelia pocketed her phone back into her robes and gave him a small smile.
"I will see you both then."
"Mm, see you soon."

chapters.title: Chapter 273: I Love You
paragraphs: Soren knocked on the door while speaking mentally. ’It’s me.’
Then the door’s lock clicked, and Soren pushed it open. Ethea was already waiting near the entrance, her mask removed, her hands resting on her lap, and a lovely smile on her face as their eyes met.
"Congratulations on your victory, dear." She said, her voice full of pride and happiness. "You were amazing."
Soren felt the corners of his lips rise as he stepped inside and knelt in front of her. "Thank you, dear." He took her hands gently. "But you weren’t bored waiting, right?"
Ethea shook her head. "No, I wasn’t. In fact, I enjoyed it a lot."
"Then I’m relieved." Soren stood up. "Actually, I discovered something during the competition."
"Mmm, I noticed it too." Ethea nodded. "Is it about Miss Nuelia’s dish?"
"Yes," Soren confirmed and then explained everything to Ethea, including the plan to meet up and have a private talk. "What do you say? Will you accompany me?"
"Of course," Ethea replied without hesitation. "I am curious what she wants to talk about, too."

"Good, then let’s not keep her waiting." Soren chuckled and took out something from his inventory. It was an ordinary-looking necklace. But as he gently put it on Ethea, it slowly changed its appearance and then disappeared from view. At the same time, Ethea’s features blurred and changed into a completely different face within seconds. "...Done."
He smiled to himself as he walked behind the wheelchair.
’Let’s go, Mr. Bagdad’s Savior.’
Ethea’s mischievous voice echoed in his mind.
’On your command, my queen~.’
Soren responded with an internal chuckle, matching her playful energy step for step as he rolled the wheelchair forward.
’Hehe~’
Ethea giggled at his words.
And as they moved, a thought popped up in her mind. ’Dear, how did you come up with that idea earlier? And... I feel like the others didn’t fully understand the story behind it.’
While he was smiling faintly the whole time, she knew well enough to guess he wasn’t fully satisfied with their responses.
’...You noticed that?’ Soren raised his brow in surprise.
’Mmm.’
Soren scratched his head with his hand. ’Actually, they weren’t wrong about it. Chef Nuelia, especially, was the closest.’
’Can you tell me the truth then?’

’It’s nothing grand. I just wanted to convey my own life through that meal.’ Soren explained. ’My early life was bitter and painful; that’s why I made it so at first, the meal would taste bitter. But if you endure the bitterness and swallow, the taste will change, just like how my life changed after meeting Nura, Raine, and... you. But the message I wanted to give was, like Miss Nuelia said, if you can endure the hardships of life, you will eventually reach the sweet reward waiting on the other side.’
’...’ Ethea went silent as Soren finished his explanation. However, from the slight curvature of her lips and the overflowing affection in her gaze, it was clear his words had reached her heart.
’Soren... I love you...’

If only she could speak these words aloud. But she didn’t have the courage to do it, not yet, especially when things between them felt so comfortable as they were. That’s why she chose to keep her feelings tucked away, leaving Soren completely oblivious to the sweet truth blooming in her heart.
But even if she couldn’t express it yet, she could still share the sentiment.
’Dear... I think it also applies to my life... You said your life changed after meeting us, but meeting you changed my life as much, if not more.’
’...’ Soren fell silent this time, but he managed to recover quickly. ’Mm, then, we should call it ’Our life’, right?’
’Our life...’ Ethea replied softly, her heart fluttering at the choice of his words. ’I... like it.’
’Good, it’s decided then.’ Soren clenched his fist. ’I’ll share it with this name!’
’Huh? You’re gonna share it?’ Ethea asked in surprise.
’That’s right, and I’m going to release the recipe for free.’ Soren revealed, with a bright spark in his eyes. ’I want everyone to experience our story and keep it in their memory.’
’I see...’ Ethea smiled. ’Then I’ll support you however I can.’
’Mm... Thank you.’

They kept moving down the hallway while continuing their talk and eventually reached the exit. As soon as they stepped out into the open air, someone waved at them. However, their face was a bit blurry.
’Hmm?’ It took Soren a moment to recognize her, as she had changed into new clothes.
’Is it her?’ Ethea asked curiously. ’She looks... a lot different.’
Instead of her usual green robes, Nuelia was wearing light, sporty summer clothes while holding an umbrella with her other hand.
’Yes,’ Soren replied while waving back at her. ’She certainly looks different.’
As they drew closer, Nuelia twirled her umbrella over one shoulder, flashing them a bright smile. "You are here."
"We didn’t make you wait, right?" Soren asked as he brought the wheelchair to a stop in front of her.
"No, I just got out too," Nuelia reassured them, nodding politely to Ethea. "It’s a pleasure to meet you, Mrs. Everly."
Ethea inclined her head. "It’s a pleasure to meet you too. And congratulations on advancing to the final."
"Thank you!" Nuelia smiled even more brightly. "But it’s your husband who stole the show today. You must be very proud of him, right?"
Ethea’s smile softened. "I am. Always."

"Hehe, I can tell." Nuelia giggled. "You look like a wife who is very much in love. And I think I understand why he kept glancing in that direction now. He must have been looking in your direction the whole time."
"Ahem." Soren cleared his throat to get their attention, his ears heating up a little. "Shall we get going?"
"Ah, right, sorry for getting carried away." Nuelia smiled apologetically and turned around. "Please follow me."
Soren nodded and wheeled Ethea after her.
"Can you tell me the location? I can take us in the car if it’s too far to walk."
"Don’t worry, it’s not that far from the festival grounds." Nuelia shook her head lightly. "And I prefer not to use a car as much as possible."
’Right, I almost forgot about this. Elves not only love but also protect the nature...’

chapters.title: Chapter 274: Exchange
paragraphs: The trio soon arrived at their destination. It was a tranquil garden with a small pond and a cozy gazebo set right beside it. Soren and Nuelia sat opposite each other after he parked Ethea’s wheelchair beside him to keep her close.
"So, what did you want to talk about, Lady Nuelia?" Soren asked as he took the tea Nuelia had just poured.

"To be honest, it’s about the dish you cooked earlier, the Broth of Life," Nuelia revealed, her tone becoming earnest. She set her own cup down and looked at him. "It really piqued my interest. If you’re willing, I would like to learn how to make it from you."
’This is a bit unexpected.’ Soren raised a brow in surprise. ’But... It might actually work out in my favor.’
His mind raced as he altered his existing plans for the current situation.
"Of course, I am willing to pay the appropriate price for it," Nuelia added after seeing Soren go silent. "We can even trade with equal-value recipes if you want."

Soren raised his gaze to meet hers. They stared at each other for a moment before Soren’s lips curled up. "Actually, I was going to make a similar request. Since you asked first, I think we can reach an agreement that benefits both of us."
"Oh! Could it be... you are also interested in the meal I prepared?" Nuelia asked enthusiastically.
Soren gave a nod. "You guessed it right. However, I also wanted to ask whether there are meals with strong effects that improve one’s life force."
This time, Nuelia raised a brow. "You noticed that effect?"
"Yes."

"Impressive." Nuelia sounded genuinely amazed, leaning in slightly with a curious look on her face. She looked up and down at him, squinting. "Hmm... I see." She chuckled before backing away. "You must have an affinity for life energy, albeit a bit weak, or it is just your senses that are sharp."
Soren’s eyes lit up. "You think I have an affinity for life energy? Is there a way to check it?

Nuelia was a bit surprised at his sudden enthusiasm, but after giving it some thought, she accepted it as natural. While elves were born with a deep connection to nature, humans rarely possessed even a trace of it. So it was understandable that he reacted this way.
"I hate to break it to you, but even if you possess it, it is far too weak for you to be able to actually use it." Nuelia pointed out gently, taking a sip of her tea.
"I see." Soren nodded in understanding. "But will I be able to make the dish you cooked? Or should one have to have a strong affinity for high life energy for it?"

"Well, I think you should be able to cook the one I made, but for other meals with strong effects, you probably can’t," Nuelia explained. "Especially the ones that can only be prepared with our secret cooking techniques."
"Right," Soren whispered in disappointment. "I didn’t consider that."

She obviously wouldn’t share those secret techniques or recipes with him, considering how valuable they were. But he wasn’t that discouraged and couldn’t afford to drop the topic yet. He turned back to her and smiled.

"I am going to be honest, Lady Nuelia. I was actually going to submit the recipe to the Magic Chef Association and allow others to use it freely." Soren revealed the truth. "So, I obviously can share it with you too. However, I wonder ifyouwould be willing to share yours with me. If you want, I can also pay you via credits or trade it for another recipe."
"!" Nuelia’s eyes widened in disbelief. "You... You intend to give it away... for free?"
Soren nodded. "That’s right."
"...Why?" Nuelia asked, confused. "Couldn’t you make a massive profit from it?"

Nuelia was taught that humans, well, the majority of them, were selfish, driven by their greed and always looking for ways to maximize their own gain. However, the human before her kept contradicting everything she had been led to believe. Well, it’s not like she had doubts about these teachings before. She had always believed that judging others, let alone an entire race, without checking if it was even correct for herself was foolish, and Soren’s actions simply proved her right.
"There isn’t any complex reason behind it," Soren replied as he helped his wife drink her tea. "I just want people to enjoy what I created."

"I see..." Nuelia stared at him for a long moment, any lingering skepticism vanishing as a newfound sense of respect settled in her chest. ’He really must be a good human. Even the spirits seem to like him after all. What do you think, Reo?’
’You’re right, Nue,’ A voice echoed in her mind. ’The boy has a pure soul. You can trust him. However, I still advise you to be careful.’
’I understand.’ Nuelia nodded internally. ’But a pure soul, you say...’
"Is there something wrong with my face?"
"Huh? Your face?" Nuelia blinked, his voice pulling her right out of her thoughts. Heat crept up her neck when she realized she had been staring straight at him for more than necessary.
"Oh, no. Not at all," she said, sitting up straight and clearing her throat. "Forgive me. I... I was just checking the illusion magic I cast on you earlier... to make sure it was completely gone."
"Ah, that?" Soren waved his hand to dismiss it. "There’s no need to apologize. I don’t feel it anymore, so it must have been cleared away. By the way, what do you think about my offer?"
"Your offer..." Nuelia repeated and then went silent. Her expression gradually turned solemn as she met his eyes.
"Mr. Soren... I really respect you for your generous intention to share such a valuable recipe with the world. However..."
"..." Soren remained attentive, waiting for her to finish her words.
"However... There is no need for you to pay me any money or give another recipe."
Soren blinked, caught off guard.
"I am willing to teach you the recipe as a direct exchange," she continued. "Someone with your mindset deserves to learn it."

chapters.title: Chapter 275: Trust
paragraphs: "Thank you." Soren bowed his head in a polite manner. "Then, should we exchange the details right now, or would you prefer to write them down?"

"Speaking is fine." Nuelia replied as she adjusted her posture. "Since we both understand high-level culinary techniques, explaining the process, the steps, and energy flow verbally should be enough. However, let’s be as detailed as possible, in case we miss any subtle nuances in the energy integration or the process itself."
"Alright, then I will start first," Soren said and started explaining the whole process as requested, while occasionally helping Ethea drink tea, eat some snacks, and asking if she was not bored.
Nuelia listened intently, still ending up taking out a quill and a piece of paper to note down the important parts.
Eventually, Soren finished his explanation and allowed Nuelia to ask questions. Once she finished and understood everything, it was Soren’s turn to listen.

Surprisingly, Nuelia was great at explaining the intricate details of her dish, even more organized than Soren had expected and did. Fortunately, his cognitive abilities and memory had reached a level where he could absorb every piece of information without missing a single detail. He could even visualize himself cooking it in his mind now; however, he still took out a notebook and wrote down everything to keep a physical record for future reference.
As they finished the exchange, Soren couldn’t help but be curious about something. "Lady Nuelia, don’t you want me to swear an oath or sign some kind of contract?"

After all, he could share her recipe with others once he left. Of course, he wasn’t actually going to do that. He just wanted to remind her that trusting someone completely without any legal protection could prove dangerous.
"..." Nuelia stared at him, her lips curling up again. "Then tell me, will you spread it around to anyone else?"

"Then that’s it." Nuelia chuckled. "And I trust your character, Mr. Soren. Even if you did end up sharing it with others, I believe you would probably do it for free again and to help people in need. So, there’s no need for any binding oaths between us."
Soren looked at her for a moment, surprised by the sheer depth of her confidence in him. A sense of gratitude washed over him as he closed his notebook and put it away.
"I appreciate the faith you place in me," he said in a sincere tone. "I will make sure to honor it."

Nuelia nodded, her posture relaxing further as she leaned back slightly. "Good. Now that we’ve settled that, you should try practicing the recipe as soon as you can. Because that’s what I am gonna do, hehe~.
"I will give it a try." Soren smiled back. "Well then, we are going to take our leave."
"Alright, then let me walk you out to the gate." Nuelia offered as she stood up.
Soren complied, and the trio made their way back to the exit through the garden. Once they reached the gate, Soren turned toward her and bowed again. "...Let’s meet again, Lady Nuelia."
"See you tomorrow~" Nuelia waved at the couple. "Bye~"
She watched as they walked away, their figures fading into the distance.
’...Why do I feel like he was bidding farewell?’
She racked her brains but couldn’t find a plausible answer, so she just shrugged and made her way back to the garden, excited to try out the ’Our Life’ right away.
’I’ll surprise Ruelia with this when I get back home~’
Later evening.
Soren and Ethea finally finished their preparations and tied up loose ends, ready to set out.
’Is this really ok?’ Ethea asked as they stood at the door. ’Perhaps... nothing will happen, and you might win the competition like today?’

’...I want to... But I don’t want to risk it.’ Soren replied with a sigh. ’Besides, I think my chances of winning are actually low. I became certain of it after talking with Lady Nuelia earlier. So, I think it’s actually better if I leave now. At least, I won’t embarrass myself in front of everyone.’
He knew his own capabilities.

’Huh? There’s no way that would happen.’ Ethea countered, crossing her arms as she looked at him with conviction. ’You saw how impressed everyone was with your creation! Dear, you have far more skill than you give yourself credit for.’

’Haha, thank you for trusting me this much,’ Soren chuckled. ’But I am not going to change my mind. We already spent enough time here. However, since we got everything we wanted in the end, I guess it was a worthwhile trip after all.’
’...’ Ethea stared at him and sighed internally, choosing not to comment any further. ’Then, let’s go.’
Soren nodded and wheeled her outside.

They had to use their artifacts to change their appearances to get out without being noticed, too. However, the reception lady immediately recognized them since she was the one who welcomed them to the hotel. Soren had to make up an excuse to her when she asked and apologized if their service had fallen short of expectations.
However, no matter what he said, she didn’t believe him and almost ended up crying.
Fortunately, Soren had his reliable partner, Ethea, who stepped in and handled the situation smoothly, giving them the perfect opening to slip away into the night without further delay.

’Hoo, thanks a lot, dear.’ Soren wiped away the nonexistent sweat from his forehead. ’I didn’t think she would get that emotional just because we were leaving the hotel. I can’t imagine how she would react if she knew we were leaving the city.’
’It’s alright,’ Ethea chuckled. ’This just shows how much the locals love you now. They hold you in high regard after everything you did.’

’Haha, guess you’re right.’ Soren chuckled himself, recalling all the cheers he received. ’But that only means we need to hurry and reach the gate before anyone else recognizes us or notices our departure.’
’Thankfully, we can travel in a car.’
’Mm...’ Soren agreed as he helped her sit in the passenger seat. ’Let’s hope we won’t get recognized once we reach the gate...’

chapters.title: Chapter 276: Departure
paragraphs: Twenty minutes later, Soren and Ethea arrived at their destination. It was a modern type of building in a circular shape, with special barriers and an array of security nodes guarding the entrance.
After getting out, Soren stored the car in his ring and guided Ethea inside, tapping his ID against the glowing scanner panel by the entrance to clear their passage.
A pair of guards posted beside the door watched them with scrutiny, their eyes tracking Soren’s movements until the scanner chimed green.
Inside, the lobby was dominated by a tall metallic device humming softly at the center, with a dozen people gathered around it.

"Excuse me," an attendant near the entrance said as they approached them. "Please, take a seat in the waiting area over there. There are two groups ahead of you now, so you’ll have to wait for your turn."
"We understand." Soren gave a nod and wheeled Ethea to the waiting area.
"Wait." The attendant called out before they could take another step. "I need to check your destination coordinates first."
"Oh, right." Soren stopped. "We’re going to Adamery City. It should be visible on our application."

The attendant swiped through their tablet, inspected it, and nodded a moment later. "...Done. And one more thing: I advise you to carry your companion as you pass through the teleportation gate. While it’s not explicitly forbidden, being extra careful is highly recommended. Extra items might trigger field turbulence or cause unexpected distortions during the transition."
Soren nodded in understanding and thanked the man for his advice. Then they headed to the designated seating area to wait their turn.
’I guess we still aren’t at the level of spatial magic that makes long jumps much easier.’ Soren sighed internally.

’Mm,’ Ethea hummed in agreement. ’It’s spatial magi-tech we are talking about after all. Spatial mages are rare, and the space itself is a difficult concept to research, let alone bind to technology.’

’You’re right. But if we keep improving, I think we will be able to travel to other continents easily one day, or perhaps even to other worlds.’ Soren chuckled to himself, not noticing the strange glint passing through Ethea’s eyes. ’Don’t you think?’
’Mmm...’ Ethea replied. ’Perhaps...’
’By the way, can you talk more about Adamery City?’ Soren shifted the topic. ’You said you spent most of your time in there and at the academy before.’
’Ok.’ Ethea agreed and started telling more stories about her past.
Time passed, and the two groups before them stepped up to the platform and vanished into the shimmering light of the gateway.
It took a few minutes for the workers at the control console to set the new coordinates.
Soren stood up as they were called and wheeled Ethea closer to the platform. Once they reached it, he first picked Ethea up and then stored the wheelchair in the storage ring.
"Are you ready?"
Ethea wrapped her arms around his neck, holding on securely. "Ready."

The attendants at the control console began the activation sequence. The tall metallic device hummed louder, its core glowing brighter as rings of energy began to spin around it. The air shimmered above the platform, and a portal slowly formed, a swirling oval of pale blue light that widened with every passing second.
’Just a few more moments.’ Soren watched the portal stabilize, his body already tensed for the step forward. ’We’ll final-!’

Before he could finish the thought, a sudden pressure slammed down from above. It crashed through the building like an invisible wave, forcing the air from his lungs and making the ground tremble beneath his feet. Soren staggered, his arms tightening around Ethea as his knees threatened to buckle.
The next moment, a pulse of darkness surged from his shadow, wrapping around them both like a second skin.
’Master!’
Malakor’s voice echoed in his head.
’W-What is happening?!’ Soren asked as the pressure lifted almost instantly, swallowed by the shadow’s protective embrace.
’Several powerful figures are approaching us at an alarming speed. We are already inside a domain!’

’A domain?!’ Soren’s heart hammered. His eyes immediately flickered to the portal; however, it was swirling violently and clearly unstable. If they stepped through now, there was no telling what would happen. They might not even survive the transition.
’Damn it.’ He cursed inwardly. ’Get ready to fight!’
Whoever they were, it was clear they weren’t coming with good intentions.
’Ethea, hold on tight!’ He immediately activated one of the artifacts that would keep Ethea safe and took out the Nightfrost, his expression turning cold.
"W-What’s happening?!"
"Why are you taking out your weapon?"
"Are we under attack?!
"Should we stop the portal?!"
The staff and guards broke into chaos, some scrambling for cover while others drew their weapons. Soren ignored them all.
’Master, they’re here.’

The next second, the doors blasted inward with a deafening crash, sending glass and metal flying across the lobby. Several cloaked figures stormed through the smoke, their auras flaring as they scanned the room.
"We found him!"
Their gazes locked onto Soren in an instant.
"Catch the thief!"
"Don’t let him get away!"
’Thief?’ Soren’s confusion flickered for only a moment before one of the figures attacked.
Swoosh!

Vines exploded from beneath his feet, thick and writhing, shooting toward him like serpents. Soren activated Phantom Step and vanished, reappearing a few meters away. But the vines followed, twisting through the air with unnatural speed.

Soren kept dodging with chained Phantom Steps. But before he could gain any distance, a figure blurred toward the portal and slammed a palm against the floor. An earth barrier erupted from the ground in an instant, sealing off the platform entirely. At the same time, the others moved like phantoms, their forms flickering from point to point as if teleporting. Streams of pressurized water cut through the air from one side while jagged roots burst from the walls on the other.
Soren’s eyes darted between them, his body already moving. He kept using Phantom Steps, twisting and weaving through the onslaught while his mind worked at an alarming rate.
’They’re trying to trap us!’ He realized. ’Malakor! Can you get us out of here?’
There was no verbal reply, but the shadow beneath his feet rippled in acknowledgment. And then, everything went black.

chapters.title: Chapter 277: Thief
paragraphs: The shadow beneath Soren’s feet expanded outward like a living tide, engulfing the light, the sound, and everything around it in an instant.
Soren kept his guard up as they moved through the darkness.
Then, without warning, the pressure from before returned. It pushed against Malakor’s domain from the outside, grinding against the shadows like two invisible walls colliding.
The darkness split.

The night sky came back into view, stars and streetlights bleeding through the cracks. They had managed to make it outside, but the attackers had already caught up. Not far from them, a green-robed figure floated above in the air, staring down at them coldly.
Swoosh!

The next moment, Malakor materialized in front of them, his large frame low to the ground, a growl already building in his chest. He stood between Soren and the enemy, shielding both him and Ethea without a word.
Three more clones of him also appeared in a loose formation around them, each one positioned to guard a different side.
"Who are you!" Soren shouted while activating Advanced Appraisal. "What do you want from us?"
Name: Lariel vae Althara
Race: Elf
Age: 167
Status: Healthy
Rank: 7th Circle (Mid Stage)
Current Mana Level: 3,412,660
Mental State: Contemptuous, Furious, Desperate
Abilities: Mistwalk, Voice of Command, Mana Resonance Sight
Affinities: Water (Grade 6 - A Rank), Life (Grade 5 - B Rank), Wind (Grade 8 - SS Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Racial Superiority Complex, Terrain Attunement
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: Very High
While the figure was still staring at them with undisguised killing intent, Soren quickly analyzed their status.

’An elf... Could this have something to do with Nuelia?’ He squinted at the figure and spoke out loud again. He had to buy them some time and get a better read of the situation. "Why did you attack us?! Explain yourself."
"Explain?" The elf’s voice dripped with contempt, each word sharp as a blade. "You dare ask for an explanation, you filthy thief?"

He made a crushing motion with his hand, and the space around Soren and Ethea trembled violently. The air itself seemed to compress, rushing inward as if to crush them from all sides. The pavement beneath them cracked.
But Malakor was faster.

A pulse of shadow shot out from his body, swallowing the pressure before it could reach them. The crushing force shattered against the dark barrier like a wave against stone. The clones also moved, launching long-range attacks at the figure.
Soren didn’t flinch. He held Ethea closer and kept his eyes on the elf. "Why are you calling me a thief? Don’t throw accusations without proof."
The elf’s expression twisted with fury.

"Where is she?!" he demanded, his voice rising as he completely ignored Soren’s words. "Tell me where you’ve hidden her, and I might leave your corpses intact!" His mana surged, the streetlights flickering a few times before exploding. "Otherwise... don’t expect me to go easy on you."

"...Are you perhaps talking about Lady Nuelia?" Soren pretended to be confused, though his mind kept racing. "If so, I think you’re greatly mistaken. I have only met her after the competition and had no other contact with her."
"You!" However, his words only seemed to anger the elf. "How dare you speak her name with that filthy tongue of yours?!"

’...Is this elf retarded or what?’ Soren cursed inwardly. He didn’t expect the guy to be so unreasonable. It seems like his superiority complex and emotions had clouded his judgment. ’Malakor, status.’
’The others are already approaching.’ Malakor replied while blocking another attack from the enraged elf. ’The city lord and some other powerful people are also coming.’
’...I called the princess for help.’ Ethea, who had been silent till now, spoke. ’Can you try to buy some more time?’
’Good, let’s hold on until they arrive.’ Soren replied, realizing the other powerful people might have been sent by the princess. ’This guy is clearly not in his right mind.’
’Understood.’

’And let’s try not to drag the people nearby into this. If a serious battle breaks out, innocent bystanders will get hurt.’ He glanced at the shattered streetlights, destroyed pavement, and the people peeking out from their windows and cars. ’We are still inside the city after all.’
’...I’ll try my best.’
’Thanks.’ Soren replied and spoke again. "Look around you! There are innocent people here. If you keep attacking like this, you’ll hurt someone who has nothing to do with this."

The elf’s expression didn’t change. If anything, his sneer seemed to deepen. "Are you trying to shield yourself behind them? Then you’re mistaken." He scoffed, his voice filled with killing intent. "As long as I can save her, nothing else matters to me. In fact, I can turn the whole city into dust just to find her."
"Oh, I would like to see you try."

Two figures dropped from the sky and landed between them, stirring up dust that was instantly blown away with a wave of their hand. One was a bald man with a mustache, while the other was a figure clad in gray armor marked with the crest of the Temur Empire, their face hidden behind a helm.
The elf’s eyes widened for a moment before his expression turned cold. "This doesn’t concern you. Step aside."

"Are you hearing yourself? You are causing a commotion in my city and threatening my people, and you even want to destroy the city?" The bald man shook his head slowly, his voice carrying a dangerous edge. "Do you really think this doesn’t concern me, you fool?"

He then took another step forward, unleashing his own aura. "Let me make something clear. This is Bagdad. It is my city. If you raise another hand against my people, I’ll make sure you never leave it alive."
"You!" The elf clenched his fists, his aura flaring up again. "You think you can defeat me?"
"Yes." The bald man replied coldly.
However, before the elf could respond, the armored figure stepped in, staring at the elf. "If you don’t stop now, we’ll consider you an enemy of the Empire and respond accordingly."
Their voice was low, but the meaning behind it was clear.
"Think carefully before you make a grave mistake."

One was a bald man with a mustache, while the other was a figure clad in gray armor marked with the crest of the Temur Empire, their face hidden behind a helm.
The elf’s eyes widened for a moment before his expression turned cold.
"This doesn’t concern you.
Step aside."
"Are you hearing yourself?
You are causing a commotion in my city and threatening my people, and you even want to destroy the city?" The bald man shook his head slowly, his voice carrying a dangerous edge.
"Do you really think this doesn’t concern me, you fool?"
He then took another step forward, unleashing his own aura.
"Let me make something clear.
This is Bagdad.
It is my city.
If you raise another hand against my people, I’ll make sure you never leave it alive."
"You!" The elf clenched his fists, his aura flaring up again.
"You think you can defeat me?"
"Yes." The bald man replied coldly.
However, before the elf could respond, the armored figure stepped in, staring at the elf.
"If you don’t stop now, we’ll consider you an enemy of the Empire and respond accordingly."
Their voice was low, but the meaning behind it was clear.
"Think carefully before you make a grave mistake."

chapters.title: Chapter 278: No Longer a Guest
paragraphs: A few seconds passed as they stared at each other. Then more figures arrived from both sides, but since the elves were fewer in number, they were surrounded by City Lord Asad and Imperial Knight’s subordinates.
The elf, Lariel, finally realizing the severity of the situation, ordered his men to stand down.

"You made the right choice." The armored knight spoke and then turned toward Soren. His eyes landed on Ethea on his arms and then shifted to the large panther still standing in front of them in a protective manner. "You too. Please, unsummon your bond."
Soren nodded and asked Malakor to get inside.
Malakor’s clones dissolved first, fading into the darkness one by one. The original lingered a bit longer, throwing a deep look at the elf before merging with Soren’s shadow.
"Thank you for your cooperation." The armored knight nodded to Soren. "However, you’ll still have to follow us for further questioning. I hope you understand."

"...Yes. I would like to get a clear understanding of the situation too." Soren replied after giving the elf a cold look. "I also want them to pay the appropriate price for their attack. Not only us, but the other innocent people almost ended up losing their lives because of them."
"..." The knight stared at Soren for a moment. "We will decide on that after learning the truth. But be assured, we definitely won’t ignore their actions. Now please follow us. All of you."
He gestured to his subordinates to ’escort’ them while he walked toward Lariel himself. "Follow me."
As for City Lord Asad, he came over to Soren’s side. "Please, follow me."
Soren nodded, a little surprised by the polite tone.
’...He must have recognized me.’ He guessed. After all, Emperors could easily distinguish mana and see through ordinary disguises.
As they leaped into the night sky, Soren looked at the man. "Thank you for your help, Sir."
"I was just doing my job." City Lord Asad merely smiled. "But receiving thanks from our Savior sure feels nice."
’I was right.’ Soren shook his head. "You are flattering me too much. All I did was cook."
"You don’t have to be modest," City Lord Asad laughed. "But... I was really disappointed to hear about your departure.
"...You knew?" Soren raised a brow.

"Yes. I investigated you through Branch President Doran after the semi-final and learned it from him." City Lord Asad answered. "I initially wanted to meet you and ask you to stay, but he insisted I shouldn’t, saying it would be disrespectful to interfere with your private life and decision."
"...I see." Soren nodded. "Then, can I ask you something?"
"Yes, but if it is about the current situation, then we don’t have enough info either." City Lord Asad said with a bitter smile. "However, we managed to find out that Chef Nuelia had been kidnapped."

"...So I was right," Soren muttered. Then he realized how much of a problem it would cause for the City Lord. He said it himself. This was his city, and she was kidnapped right under his nose. But... ’They must be at least at the 7th circle to be able to kidnap her... After all, she was at the late stage of the 6th circle. But who could they be? Her own enemies or...’
Soren fell into deep thought, but a moment later, he shook his head. There would be time to figure that out later. Right now, there was something more important to focus on.
’Ethea, are you feeling ok?’ He sent the thought through their bond, his voice gentle. ’We’re safe for now. Just hold on a little longer.’
’Don’t worry. Nothing happened to me.’ Ethea reassured him. ’But what about you?’
’I am fine too.’ Soren replied as he really didn’t have to fight. Then he connected to his other bond. ’Malakor, you didn’t get hurt, right?’
’...No, Master.’
’Good. Rest and recover your strength for now.’
’Understood.’
Then he turned his attention back to Ethea and discussed the situation with her.
Meanwhile, City Lord Asad also became lost in his own thoughts. His usual easygoing attitude had long faded.
’...’ Even though he looked composed, there was a tension in his shoulders that hadn’t been there before.

He was the protector of this city, and something like this had happened during the biggest event of the year. The weight of that failure pressed down on him. Because it would not only affect the city but might also end up staining the relationship between elves and humanity.

’If I catch the culprits, I will give them hell for ruining the festival and putting my people in danger.’ He clasped his hands behind his back. A moment later, he threw a glance at Soren and squinted. ’Although it doesn’t seem like he is involved, I’ll keep an eye on him.’

His suspicion wasn’t without proof. Soren was too calm for someone who was attacked by a group of powerful people, including a literal Emperor. Maybe because he had a magic beast of equal strength, but it still didn’t add up.
’I hope he isn’t involved, though...’
He really didn’t want Bagdad’s Savior to turn out to be a villain in disguise.
’Time will tell us...’
He sighed and kept flying, and soon they reached their destination. The others also arrived not long after.
City Lord Asad led them inside.

The building was larger than it looked from outside, and the guards posted at the entrance watched them pass without a word. Asad guided them through a long hallway and into a meeting room where a long table had already been prepared.

Soren set Ethea down gently into a chair beside him before taking his own seat. Across from them, the elven representatives sat stiffly, their eyes fixed on Soren with open hostility. The armored knight and City Lord Asad took their places at opposite ends of the table, while a few other officials stood near the walls.

The armored knight was the first to speak. "Lord Asad and I have already dispatched people to search for Chef Nuelia. Every exit from the city is being monitored, and the festival grounds are being swept as we speak."
They paused, letting the words settle.

"Now, we are going to talk about what happened tonight. Both sides will present their version of events, and we will determine how to proceed." Their gaze shifted to the elves, then to Soren. "Let’s begin."

chapters.title: Chapter 279: The Price to Pay
paragraphs: "First, let’s hear it from you... Mr. Everly." The knight turned toward Soren, who was asked to reveal his real face. "And please, be honest. If you try to lie, the consequences will be severe."
"How can we be sure he’s not lying?" Lariel chimed in. "What if you are in cahoots and try to shield each other?"

The knight turned to him, his eyes cold. "If you keep interrupting, I will kick you out of here and give you the punishment you deserve." Then he took something round from his storage ring and set it on the desk. "This is called a Truth-Seeing Orb. It can help us detect falsehoods. I will show you a short demonstration."
"You just have to put your hand on it and speak. The orb turns red if you lie." The knight placed his hand on the orb and spoke. "I’m a woman."
The next moment, the orb glowed red, indicating he lied.
"I kidnapped an elf."
It glowed red again.
"I’ll ensure both sides will get justice."
Nothing happened this time.

"As you can see, we have a way to verify everything you say, so I suggest you think carefully before speaking." He paused and turned to the elves. "I advise you to listen silently and let him finish before making any accusations. We will hear your side afterward. And again, if you interrupt or make accusations, you know what awaits you."
Only after the elves nodded did he turn back to Soren. "You may begin."
Soren nodded and placed his hand on the orb. Then, he briefly recounted everything that happened after the semi-final.
However, some of the elves still ended up interrupting him, calling him a liar, a thief, and so on. Fortunately, the knight was a reasonable man and punished them accordingly.
"...And that is where you came in.
Soren ended his story. The orb didn’t turn red even once, which made the elves’ faces turn unsightly.
’...They still can’t accept the truth, huh.’ Soren sighed inwardly. ’Is there some kind of reason for it?’
He was curious, but since it was their turn to speak, he would soon find out.
"Mr. Knight," Lariel spoke up. "Can I ask him a question before I start?"

Lariel nodded and turned to Soren. "Can you tell me why you were in such a hurry to leave, then? Didn’t you advance to the finals? And how do you have a Cataclysm Class magic beast? It seems a lot suspicious to me."

"..." Soren coldly stared at the elf. "Why should I tell you about my private life? I have said what I needed to say, and the orb has proven my words are true. Just because you’re not satisfied with the answer doesn’t give you the right to pry into my personal matters."

Lariel’s eyes narrowed, but the knight raised a hand before he could respond. "He’s right. The investigation is about Chef Nuelia’s disappearance, not about his reasons for leaving the city. If you have questions related to the case, ask them. Otherwise, let it go."
The elf clenched his fists, clearly unsatisfied, but said nothing more to Soren.
"Mr. Knight," he said to the knight. "Can we start now?"
"Yes.

Lariel took a deep breath and started their side of the story. "After the semi-final, she was supposed to return to the villa. However, she told her attendant that she had an important matter to take care of and left alone. She ordered her not to follow her or inform any of us about it."

He paused, his jaw tightening. "Knowing her contracted spirit, a powerful being capable of rivaling an Emperor, the attendant believed she would be safe. So she kept quiet." His voice darkened. "But hours passed, and the attendant began to fear that something had gone wrong. So, she finally came to us and confessed everything."
The room was silent.

"We started searching immediately, but by then, the trail had already gone cold. Neither she nor her spirit has answered a single call. It is as if both of them have been erased. Fortunately, we managed to find where she last visited using a secret spell." He paused, his eyes landing on Soren. "It was that garden. And... there were signs of a brutal battle."
Soren’s expression remained neutral, but his mind was already piecing things together. ’She must have been taken shortly after we parted ways.’

"When we arrived, the surroundings were destroyed, and her belongings were scattered across the ground. Fortunately, her spirit had managed to leave behind a message, but it was fragmented and hard to understand." Lariel’s voice faltered for just a moment before he steadied himself. "We could only make out three words: mana... steal... save..."

"That is when we realized she had been kidnapped." He let the words hang in the air before continuing. "After that, we searched the area again and found another faint trace of mana. We tracked it through the city until it brought us to you."
Lariel’s gaze locked onto Soren. "Tell me, human. If you were truly innocent, why did her trail lead straight to you?"
"..." Soren looked at him as if he were looking at a fool. "Isn’t it obvious? You followedmymana; who else would it lead you to?"

"I understand it might have been your only lead at the time," Soren continued before the elves could retort. "But did you have to act like that? Destroying a building, opening a domain, putting innocent people in danger, and attacking us out of the blue?" His tone and gaze grew colder with each word. "What would happen if I didn’t have my bonded beast to protect us? You would have seriously hurt me, but also my wife!"
Soren radiated killing intent for the first time since everything started, the air around him dropping by several degrees.
"If... anything happened to her, we wouldn’t be sitting here and talking like this," Soren stated coldly. "I would have made sure you paid the price for that first."

chapters.title: Chapter 280: Logic And Pride
paragraphs: "...I would have made sure you would have paid the price for that first."
The room went silent.

The elves stiffened, their faces becoming unsightly again as genuine fear made them feel even more humiliated. However, knowing he was in the right, that powerful humans were around them, and that they were on their territory, they swallowed their pride and stayed silent.
The knight and City Lord Asad observed the exchange without a word, reaching a similar conclusion as Soren in their minds.

The elves had clearly acted rashly and let their desperation cloud their judgment. They had attacked first, endangered civilians, and damaged city property, all without solid proof. Even if their concern for Nuelia was genuine, their methods had crossed too many lines. If Soren and his wife hadn’t been capable of defending themselves, tonight could have ended with innocent blood on the elves’ hands. And that was something neither the knight nor Asad would forget.
’Why did the elves send this guy anyway?’
They both asked themselves the same question.

Lariel was supposed to be Nuelia’s guardian, but everything about his behavior tonight painted the opposite picture. He had let his target out of his sight for hours. Instead of controlling his subordinates, he started the chaos himself. And even now, he still seemed unable to let go of his pride long enough to think clearly.
’...How did he even become an Emperor?’
The thought crossed both their minds, though neither voiced it aloud. They exchanged a brief look, understanding each other without a single word.

"Mr. Everly is right." The knight finally spoke up. "And it matches his statement. But you... Didn’t you consider that the kidnapper had a way of erasing their own tracks and left Mr. Everly’s mana signature behind on purpose? To distract you and send you chasing the wrong person while they escaped the city or hid well enough?"
Lariel’s jaw tightened, but couldn’t find the words to respond.

"We welcomed you with open arms and showed the best hospitality we could," City Lord Asad joined the conversation. "But is this how you show your gratitude? I thought elves were friendly and wise, and here you are, attacking first and asking questions later."
He let out a disappointed sigh, and some of the elves hung their heads low, finally starting to realize how far they had overstepped.

"..." Lord Asad let the silence stretch a bit longer before continuing. "However, I am also partly at fault. I should have noticed it sooner and prevented these things from happening. For that, I apologize."
The elves were stunned by his words, their earlier hostility faltering as surprise took its place.

"I have a question." The knight cut in before they could respond. "Why didn’t you contact us first? Especially Lord Asad? He knows this city better than anyone. If you had gone to him the moment you realized she was missing, he could have responded properly and made everything easier. Instead, you took matters into your own hands and nearly started a war in the middle of a festival." His gaze landed on Lariel, full of suspicion. "So I’ll ask again. Why didn’t you ask for help?"
The room went deathly silent.

Everyone stared at Lariel, even his subordinates, whose eyes now held a mixture of confusion and doubt. They had followed him out of loyalty, but the question had struck at something they hadn’t dared to ask themselves.

Lariel felt like he was standing on the edge of a cliff with no way back. He looked like a cornered beast rather than a mighty Emperor. His mouth opened, but no words came out. Because... the truth was too humiliating.

He couldn’t tell them that he didn’t ask for help because of his pride and that he believed elves were above humans, and asking a human for help would have felt like bowing to a lesser race. It would have been a stain on his honor, a sign of weakness he couldn’t accept.

So he had chosen to act alone, trusting in his own strength and judgment. And now... that choice had led him here, sitting across from the very people he had looked down on, forced to swallow his arrogance in front of everyone.

Furthermore, deep down, he was afraid... afraid of what would happen if the elders learned he lost her on his watch and failed to protect her. He feared the shame and punishment that would follow, especially since this was his first big mission in the outside world after a long time. The elders had trusted him with this task despite his inexperience after he begged for the chance to prove himself.
And yet... he ended up failing!
If word of this reached them before he fixed it, his reputation, his position, everything he had worked so hard for, would crumble overnight.
That fear, more than anything, had pushed him to act rashly.

He had attacked first because he couldn’t bear the thought of returning empty-handed. He had accused Soren because he needed someone to blame. At least, that was what he told himself. If he could point the finger at someone else, maybe the elders would see him as a protector who had been outwitted rather than a fool who had failed his only duty.
But deep down, he knew the truth.

No matter how loudly he accused others, he was the one who had let her slip away. And now, because of his choices, he might never get the chance to make it right. The weight of that realization pressed down on him until even breathing felt heavy, and he could do nothing but sit there, silent and ashamed, as the others around him waited for an answer he couldn’t give.
’...I see. Thank you, dear.’
Soren had been talking with Ethea since he was free, and her insight was as sharp as always. And now, it was time to act on it.
"I would like to ask something too." He broke the ice. "Has it ever occurred to any of you that this might be an inside job? That there’s a traitor among-"
"You!" Lariel interrupted, seizing the opportunity to turn the attention away from himself. "Are you accusing us?!"

He had let his target out of his sight for hours.
Instead of controlling his subordinates, he started the chaos himself.
And even now, he still seemed unable to let go of his pride long enough to think clearly.
’...How did he even become an Emperor?’
The thought crossed both their minds, though neither voiced it aloud.
They exchanged a brief look, understanding each other without a single word.
"Mr.
Everly is right." The knight finally spoke up.
"And it matches his statement.
But you...
Didn’t you consider that the kidnapper had a way of erasing their own tracks and left Mr.
Everly’s mana signature behind on purpose?
To distract you and send you chasing the wrong person while they escaped the city or hid well enough?"
Lariel’s jaw tightened, but couldn’t find the words to respond.
"We welcomed you with open arms and showed the best hospitality we could," City Lord Asad joined the conversation.
"But is this how you show your gratitude?
I thought elves were friendly and wise, and here you are, attacking first and asking questions later."
He let out a disappointed sigh, and some of the elves hung their heads low, finally starting to realize how far they had overstepped.
"..." Lord Asad let the silence stretch a bit longer before continuing.
"However, I am also partly at fault.
I should have noticed it sooner and prevented these things from happening.
For that, I apologize."
The elves were stunned by his words, their earlier hostility faltering as surprise took its place.
"I have a question." The knight cut in before they could respond.
"Why didn’t you contact us first?
Especially Lord Asad?
He knows this city better than anyone.
If you had gone to him the moment you realized she was missing, he could have responded properly and made everything easier.
Instead, you took matters into your own hands and nearly started a war in the middle of a festival." His gaze landed on Lariel, full of suspicion.
"So I’ll ask again.
Why didn’t you ask for help?"
The room went deathly silent.
Everyone stared at Lariel, even his subordinates, whose eyes now held a mixture of confusion and doubt.
They had followed him out of loyalty, but the question had struck at something they hadn’t dared to ask themselves.
Lariel felt like he was standing on the edge of a cliff with no way back.
He looked like a cornered beast rather than a mighty Emperor.
His mouth opened, but no words came out.
Because... the truth was too humiliating.
He couldn’t tell them that he didn’t ask for help because of his pride and that he believed elves were above humans, and asking a human for help would have felt like bowing to a lesser race.
It would have been a stain on his honor, a sign of weakness he couldn’t accept.
So he had chosen to act alone, trusting in his own strength and judgment.
And now... that choice had led him here, sitting across from the very people he had looked down on, forced to swallow his arrogance in front of everyone.
Furthermore, deep down, he was afraid... afraid of what would happen if the elders learned he lost her on his watch and failed to protect her.
He feared the shame and punishment that would follow, especially since this was his first big mission in the outside world after a long time.
The elders had trusted him with this task despite his inexperience after he begged for the chance to prove himself.
And yet... he ended up failing!
If word of this reached them before he fixed it, his reputation, his position, everything he had worked so hard for, would crumble overnight.
That fear, more than anything, had pushed him to act rashly.
He had attacked first because he couldn’t bear the thought of returning empty-handed.
He had accused Soren because he needed someone to blame.
At least, that was what he told himself.
If he could point the finger at someone else, maybe the elders would see him as a protector who had been outwitted rather than a fool who had failed his only duty.
But deep down, he knew the truth.
No matter how loudly he accused others, he was the one who had let her slip away.
And now, because of his choices, he might never get the chance to make it right.

The weight of that realization pressed down on him until even breathing felt heavy, and he could do nothing but sit there, silent and ashamed, as the others around him waited for an answer he couldn’t give.
’...I see.
Thank you, dear.’
Soren had been talking with Ethea since he was free, and her insight was as sharp as always.
And now, it was time to act on it.
"I would like to ask something too." He broke the ice.
"Has it ever occurred to any of you that this might be an inside job?
That there’s a traitor among-"
"You!" Lariel interrupted, seizing the opportunity to turn the attention away from himself.
"Are you accusing us?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 281: Interrogation
paragraphs: "Are you accusing us?"

"...I wasn’t." Soren coldly replied. "But now I’m starting to. And considering how defensive you are, your reckless, illogical actions, and your inability to provide answers, you’re the biggest suspect."
"!" Lariel’s eyes widened, stunned into silence for a moment before his face twisted with fury. "You dare...!"
His mana flared, his hand rising, but before he could do anything, the knight’s voice cut through the air like a blade.
"Control yourself, elf." The knight didn’t raise his voice, but it was loud enough to be heard by everyone. "Unless you want to prove him right."
"Urgh..." Lariel’s mana wavered, then receded. His already fragile pride was shattered, his breathing becoming heavy, but he could only force himself to sit back down.

Soren watched him with a fearless expression while the other elves exchanged uncertain glances. The seeds of doubt had been planted. Now it was only a matter of time before they grew and the truth revealed itself.
’I only hope he is capable as he seems...’

The knight glanced at Soren, squinting. "...Mr. Everly has a point. Considering the info we have, the kidnappers must have known everything about her. When she would be alone, where she would go, her strengths and weaknesses, and even her contracted spirit." He started speculating. "The timing of the attack was too precise. I also think someone close to her might have leaked information. It could be a maid or the personal attendant you mentioned. Or... the culprit might even be among us right now."
His gaze swept over the elves before stopping on Lariel.
"If you really want to find her, you’ll have to cooperate with us. We must check everyone who came with her... starting with you."
"..." Lariel clenched his fists under the table, but eventually gave a nod, realizing there might indeed be a traitor. "Ok."
He then raised his right hand and put it on the orb. "I didn’t kidnap Lady Nuelia or provide any information to those who did. I am not involved in her disappearance in any way."
The truth-seeing orb remained unchanged.
Lariel secretly let out a breath of relief, but kept his expression as honest and composed as possible.

"...Good," The knight said, also relieved. If Lariel had really turned out to be a traitor, a battle would have broken out, and many lives would have been lost. No matter how stupid, he was still a 7th circle Awakened.

"Then, we’ll continue." He turned to the other elves. "One by one, each of you will place your hand on the orb and state your innocence. If anyone refuses, they’ll be treated as a suspect immediately. Understood?"
The elves nodded and started to rise from their seats one at a time.
"...I am not involved in Lady Nuelia’s disappearance."
True.
"...I am not involved in Lady Nuelia’s disappearance."
True.
They kept repeating the same lines.
"...I am not involved in Lady Nuelia’s disappearance."
"...I am involved in Lady Nuelia’s disappearance."
True.
"...Wait."
The room went still, all the eyes turning to the elf at the table. He stared down at the orb for a long moment, then at his own hand, and let out a strange laugh. "Ah... I still got caught, haha."
The words fell over the room like a stone in still water. For half a second, no one moved. Then everything broke loose.
Lariel, as the closest, was the first to move.
He shot forward, his hands catching the elf by the collar and slamming him down on the table. It cracked under the force, and the other elves scrambled back.
"You! Why did you betray us?!" Lariel shouted in fury. "Where is she?!"
"Keke-cough... cough... ke..."

The elf in question giggled. Even with his back against the table and Lariel looming over him, his smile didn’t falter. "Keke, it was all thanks to your stupidity and useless pride. It all went as planned." He paused, his grin widening even as blood trickled down his lips and nose. "No, wait. Considering how stupid you are, there was no need to plan at all! Haha-cough!"
Lariel’s eyes widened, his grip tightening around the elf’s neck.
"Cough-go ahead, kill-cough-me..." The elf’s smile twisted darker. "Prove... my words... right... keke..."
"!" Lariel’s hands trembled, his killing intent intensifying. Every fiber of his being wanted to snap the elf’s neck and be done with it, but a sliver of reason kept his fingers from closing.
"Tch!" He released his grip but still kept the traitor elf pinned down. "I’ll deal with you once this is all over."
Then, he looked at the knight. "...You take over. I fear I might end up killing him."

"Keke~" The traitor cackled, his voice hoarse but dripping with amusement. "Ask all you want, but you won’t get any answers from me. I don’t know anything." His gaze slid toward Soren, and his grin widened. "But that one... that one is the true culprit."
A strange glint passed through his eyes, as if something inside him was dimming.
All the gazes turned toward Soren.
"?" Soren frowned, and then his eyes suddenly widened.
"ARGH!" He groaned out loud, clutching his head as if in immense pain.
"Dear!"
"Soren?!"
Ethea and City Lord Asad reacted simultaneously, while others watched in confusion and shock.

"Something’s not right," Lariel muttered, his gaze shifting from Soren back to the traitor elf. He then saw it: the light returning to those hollow eyes, and a trace of surprise flickering across them. ’Don’t tell me?! M-Mind control magic?’
"You!" He realized in an instant what the guy tried to do. But before he could react, the elf’s mana surged, his body beginning to convulse.
’Is he... trying to self-destruct?!’
Lariel moved, but he was a step too late.
"DEATH TO YOU ALL!"
The elf roared derangedly, bleeding from every orifice as his body swelled with chaotic mana.
"HAHAHA-!"
Swoosh-!
"...Not on my watch." The knight struck the elf across the back of the neck with one precise blow.

The elf’s laughter cut off instantly, his eyes rolling back as he crumpled to the floor like a puppet with its strings cut. The knight didn’t stop there. He pressed a hand against the elf’s chest and channeled his mana inward, forcing his own energy through the elf’s mana circuits to suppress the violent surge before it could erupt.
"Everyone, watch out! They can use mind control!"

chapters.title: Chapter 282: Mysterious Enemy
paragraphs: Lariel shouted as his eyes swept over everyone.
"He tried to take over his mind before he attempted to self-destruct!" He pointed at Soren and then at the unconscious elf. "We need to check everyone! Right now!"

Everyone in the room stiffened, their expressions shifting from shock to wariness as they sized each other up. The guards reached for their weapons, and even the elves began to eye one another with fresh suspicion. The knight, having managed to stop the elf from self-destructing, rose to his feet.
"Calm down." He muttered. "We are already in my domain. Everything is under control."
"Oh, really?"

A cynical laugh broke out from one of the humans watching near the wall. Before the man could even blink, the knight vanished from the center of the room and reappeared directly beside him, driving a light elbow into his chest. The human collapsed instantly, unconscious before his body hit the floor.
"I wouldn’t be so certain if I-" another elf across the room began to mock.
The knight blurred forward again, striking the elf across the temple and dropping him like a sack of stone.
"-were you," a third elf finished from the far corner, his voice strangely calm despite the violent display.
This time, the knight didn’t attack. He stopped a foot away from the third elf, his armored finger hovering inches from the suspect’s forehead.
"What do you want?" the knight demanded, his voice dropping into a dangerous rumble. "And where is the girl?"
"Ok, ok, I will tell you," the elf said with a dramatic sigh. "But... only tomorrow."
"..." The knight squinted at the culprit. "Just what are you plotting?"
"Nothing noteworthy," the elf laughed. "However, I advise you not to cancel the competition."
"What do you mean by that?" The knight asked, his suspicion growing.
"As I said, you will find out tomorrow." The elf replied with a wicked smile.
"Both finalists should be present there too." He added, glancing at Soren. "Or else... you can forget about getting her back."
"...Alright." The knight nodded, choosing to play along with this mysterious enemy. "We promise to do it; however, you should also promise not to harm her.
"Deal." The elf smiled, waving. "See you tomorrow then."
A moment later, the elf stopped moving, his hands dropping, clarity slowly returning to his eyes. "W-What happened?"
The knight’s gaze swept over everyone, wondering if the guy really left.
"...Oops, I almost forgot." Just then, the closest elf beside him spoke up, staring intensely at the knight. "Was it really a good idea to leave your precious princess all alone?"
The room went deathly silent.
The knight froze, his eyes shaking from shock. ’D-Don’t tell me?!’
He turned to the elf. "You... You are messing with the wrong people. If you dare to touch a single hair on her head, I will make sure you suffer a fate worse than death."
"...Whoa. Scary. I almost wet myself there." The elf chuckled, looking down at his pants as if to confirm he really didn’t. "...Thank goodness. Hooh."
"And... are you sure about what you said?"

"Noted. Then, we won’t touch her hair at all. But I really can’t promise anything else." The elf paused, licking his lips as he continued. "Hands, legs, eyes... everything except hair is totally fine, right? Glad you are so generous-"
"..." The knight knocked the elf unconscious before he could finish, his gaze furious.
"Whoa! Why so aggressive?!" Another human spoke this time. "I was only repeating what you said!"
"...Get lost before I lose control." The knight muttered.
"Ok, ok, no need to be so touchy." The man raised his hands in mock surrender, taking a slow step back with a lazy smirk still playing on his lips. "I’m leaving..."
"...I said stop playing." The knight appeared behind the man and knocked him unconscious.
But he didn’t stop and kept moving, appearing in one spot after another, and knocking out everyone who could be taken over by the villain.

And the villain kept playing with the knight, infuriating him with each passing second. And soon, the room was filled with unconscious bodies, with only City Lord Asad, the elf leader Lariel, Soren, and his wife remaining.
The silence that followed was suffocating, broken only by the soft breathing of those left standing amidst the sea of fallen guards and elves.
The knight turned to the City Lord Asad. "I’m going to check up on Her Highness; he might have been bluffing. Please, take care of the rest."
"Understood." Asad nodded with a solemn expression.

The knight then turned to Soren. "Thank you for your warning earlier. And... I must ask you to stay. Given everything that has transpired, you cannot leave the city just yet, and your participation in the finals is now mandatory."
Soren stared back at the knight, his eyes narrowing in silence.
Before he could offer a response, the door creaked open. A guard peeked his head inside the room.
"Ah, my apologies for interrupting," the guard said, an apologetic smile spreading across his face. "I just forgot to say hello to someone."
His gaze bypassed the knight, sliding past Asad and Soren, until it locked directly onto Ethea.

"Long time no see, Miss Hero," the voice sneered, dripping with mock intimacy. "I truly thought you were long dead and was depressed for three whole weeks. But now I can rest easy... knowing I get to kill-"
A shadow blurred across the floor.
Soren appeared directly in front of the guard. Without a word, he delivered a strike, cutting the speech short and sending him crumpling to the floor.
"..." He caught the falling body and put it gently on the ground; however, his expression was anything but calm.
The knight watched the exchange in silence, his suspicion of Soren and his mysterious wife deepening. Unfortunately, he was in a hurry and had no time to press the issue right now.
"...We’ll talk later."
He muttered and disappeared from the room.
"..." Soren calmly walked back, kneeling beside his wife. "Are you ok, dear?"

chapters.title: Chapter 283: Who Are They?
paragraphs: "..." Lariel stood frozen on the spot, his mind racing non-stop, trying to understand just what kind of mess they were in.

His gaze swept over his fallen subordinates and the human couple he had wrongly accused. He believed the enemy was playing tricks again just now; he still couldn’t help but doubt the woman’s identity, especially after the attacker called her ’Miss Hero’. However, like the knight, he had important things to do, so he could only set the thought aside for now.
"...I’m also leaving. I have to investigate the rest of my people."
"Ok, don’t forget to return and share your findings," Asad replied.
"I will." Lariel nodded before taking his leave.
Asad sighed and turned toward Soren. "Mr. Everly, thank you for your cooperation."

’And thank you for your assistance. If you hadn’t noticed the abnormality and warned us, we would have walked straight into their trap.’ He added mentally, recalling what Soren said to him and the knight when the interrogation of the elves started.

"No need to thank me," Soren said, smiling. "I’m just glad that the misunderstanding was resolved and we managed to catch the hidden snake. However, given how easily they are moving through the city, I think it would be wise to reconsider the safety of the tournament." He paused for a moment, as if organizing his thoughts. "I strongly recommend only using guards with high cultivation bases and strong mental defenses or willpower, and calling for help. I also recommend closing the arena to the general public. With an enemy who can control even elves at will, leaving the stadium packed with ordinary citizens is a recipe for disaster. We are unaware of their actual capabilities or numbers. If they are a terror organization, they might be planning something horrific, such as... a massacre, since similar events have happened before."
"..." Lord Asad went silent at Soren’s words. ’He’s more intelligent than I gave him credit for.’
"Thank you for your advice." He smiled. "I will take it into consideration."
"Mm. And..." Soren paused, hesitating. "Would it be possible to provide us with a safe place to stay? I don’t want to stay in a hotel and put others in danger."
