"Then, let me give you a hand," Soren suggested. "It will be quicker that way."
"Good, I will take you up on that offer." Lord Asad smiled. "Let’s get to work then."

"This will be your temporary residence. If you need anything, you can call me using this button." An elderly butler in a pristine uniform bowed politely. "I will take my leave now. Please rest comfortably."
"Thank you."
Soren bowed back politely and saw him off before closing the door.
"Malakor." He called out, and the next moment, Malakor materialized in front of him, but in a smaller form. "You know what to do."
Malakor nodded, dispersed into shadows, and disappeared from the room.
Soren sighed and looked down at Ethea. "Let’s wash up and go to sleep. I have a feeling tomorrow is going to be a long day."
"Mmm." Ethea nodded.
Soren smiled and helped her through the rest of their nightly routine. Soon after, they both lay side by side on the bed, gazing up at the dark ceiling.

Soren inhaled deeply and turned his head left, locking eyes with Ethea. After a brief silence, he reached with his left hand, placing it on her right. Gently, he slid his fingers between hers, intertwining their hands.
"Goodnight, Ethea," he murmured softly.
She smiled, her eyes fluttering closed. "Goodnight, dear."
A few minutes passed.
’Shall we start now?’
’Yes.’ Ethea replied. ’Is there anything you want to ask?’

’Mm. It is obvious he or she recognized you after failing to possess you. That means they are your enemy. What I am curious about is who they are. Were they involved in the incident back then? Are you able to talk about them?’
’...Yes, I can.’ Ethea answered after a pause. ’And no, they weren’t involved in the incident. Probably.’
’What do you mean?’

’They... They are a small group known as the Outcasts.’ Ethea explained. ’Most of their members are people who were abandoned by society. Criminals, experiments, people with abilities that made them too dangerous to live among normal people. They gather together because no one else would accept them.’

’...They are dangerous, but they are not like other criminal factions who mainly operate for money or power. They have no interest in ruling the world. They simply want to destroy the people and systems that made them suffer.
Soren stayed silent, absorbing the info.

’They do whatever they want, whenever they want. Most of the time, there is no greater plan behind their actions. Just chaos, revenge, and the twisted belief that the world deserves to burn. But when they do have a goal... it is never something simple. They are patient when they need to be. And they always leave behind more damage than anyone expects. I...’
’...’ Soren sensed the fluctuation in her tone.

’I experienced it myself, years ago when I was in my final year at the Etenia Academy.’ Ethea paused, as if reliving the memory. ’...We were out on a secret mission assigned by the academy as part of the exam. Our task was to investigate a cluster of villages near the border. We arrived at our destination, but nothing seemed wrong at first. The villagers were going about their day, working the fields, tending to their homes. Yet something still felt off.’
She paused, her grip on his fingers tightening slightly.

’...It wasn’t until we attempted to speak with them that we realized it. They behaved as normal people, engaging in conversation and responding smoothly. Yet, once our focus was elsewhere, something shifted. They... They would lose their ’life’. They continued moving, but their eyes lacked any human spark. It was like watching puppets on invisible strings, carrying out their routines just to fool anyone watching.’

chapters.title: Chapter 284: Who Are They? [2]
paragraphs: ’We kept investigating and, in the end, uncovered the truth... that the villages had already been lost long before we arrived. The people had been turned into hollow shells, stripped of everything that made them who they were...’ Etha’s grip tightened even more. ’When we confronted the culprit, or at least we thought we did... he attacked us in a way none of us were prepared for... he turned us against each other... one by one, my teammates fell under his control. They drew their weapons against each other, their eyes empty and their bodies moving as if they weren’t entirely their own. But I could still see them in there, trapped...’

’In a matter of minutes, all of them were controlled. Since he couldn’t get into my mind, I managed to stay free... But as a result, I had to fight them all on my own. I had to keep them from killing each other and from killing me, and all the while he just stood there, watching us tear ourselves apart. Every time I disarmed one of them, another would attack from behind or try to kill the other. Every time I tried to reach them, he would twist their minds further. It went on for what felt like hours. By the end of it, I was the only one left standing. I managed to save everyone but... he had escaped. I... I couldn’t catch him. I... I let that monster get away...’

’...’ Soren opened his eyes, while imagining how difficult it must have been. He couldn’t, because he knew it must have been even more difficult than she just had described. Just like him back then, she too was trying to hide the worst parts, keeping the memories locked away where they couldn’t hurt as much.
’Ethea...’
He called out gently as he closed the distance between them, wrapping his arms around her and holding her gently but firmly.

’It’s okay... You did the best you could.’ He said, stroking her hair. ’You handled it better than anyone could have. You survived, and you saved everyone. That’s more than enough. And... When the time comes, I will be right beside you to help you catch every last one of them. I promise.’

’...’ Ethea didn’t say anything, but her throat tightened as she buried her face into his chest. Sliding her hands up over his arms, she gripped his shirt tightly, holding onto him with everything she had.
Time passed as they stayed lost in each other’s embrace, holding on until the tension finally drained from her body.
’Thank you, Soren...’ Ethea spoke up at last.

’But...’ She paused, taking a breath before her tone grew serious once more. ’We need to be careful tomorrow. His strength must have grown immensely compared to the past. As for what he displayed today... It was barely a fraction of what he can actually do. I’m sure of it. However, I know his weakness. He mainly relies on his ability and illusions, so as long as one bypasses his mental tricks and gets within close range, he becomes extremely vulnerable.’
’I understand. However, from what you said earlier, he isn’t alone in this. So I think he will have companions to cover up for his weakness... Do you perhaps know who else might be involved?’

’Yes, but I’m not entirely certain. However, since that elf said the spirit said those words, I can assume that the Leech and the Nullifier must be involved in it.’ Ethea speculated. ’They were probably the ones who kidnapped Lady Nuelia and Senior Roya.’
’I see. Do you know about their powers?’

’Yes. They are also incredibly powerful and difficult to deal with. The Leech can steal mana from anything, including living beings. The Nullifier, on the other hand, is the opposite. He has a strange constitution that creates an anti-mana zone. Within that zone, any active spell or cultivation method instantly dissipates, rendering one completely powerless. Furthermore, they are both extremely skilled at close combat. The Leech uses twin daggers, while the Nullifier relies solely on his monstrous body. And together, they are known as the Hollow Pair: one suppresses your power, while the other steals what remains.’

’...That indeed sounds troublesome.’ Soren thought. ’If one isn’t skilled in close combat and has a weak body, they would be turned into helpless prey the moment they step into their range. And I guess the same thing happened to Lady Nuelia and the princess.’
’Right.’ Ethea confirmed. ’They must have been caught off guard and neutralized before they even realized what was happening.’
’Then... do you think I stand a chance against them?’ Soren asked curiously.

’...I’m sorry, dear. But right now, no. While you have improved tremendously in the past months, you are still lacking in both experience and skills. The Leech and the Nullifier have spent years perfecting their abilities against enemies far stronger than you. Unless you have a very specific plan, facing either of them head-on would be suicide.’ She paused, her hand squeezing his. ’But that doesn’t mean you will be easily defeated. If you can fully utilize your unique constitution and outsmart them, I am sure you will be able to find an opening and strike where they least expect it.’
’Thank you for being honest.’ Soren smiled. ’And I’m guessing that their weakness is also tied to their abilities.’

’Mm, indeed.’ Ethea smiled, feeling reassured by his sharp mindset. ’While they make others unable to use their mana thanks to their special abilities, they also suffer from the exact same limitation. The Nullifier is inherently unable to use mana, while the Leech can’t use the mana he steals, even outside the anti-mana zone. His body acts like a temporary vessel. If he absorbs too much mana at once, he risks a core overload that will tear his body apart from the inside. So, they are completely reliant on their bodies and weapons. But of course, they aren’t 100% correct, as I am not certain whether they are still the same as before.’
’It’s still more than I could have hoped for,’ Soren replied. ’At least now I know what to expect. And what to look out for.’
’In that case, let me tell you everything else I knew about them.’

chapters.title: Chapter 285: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [1]
paragraphs: "Ladies and gentlemen!" Faris’s voice echoed through the massive stadium. However, there was no one in the stands. The seats were empty, and only a handful of staff and officials remained near the stage. He looked at the camera, his usual grin missing.

"Due to special circumstances, the final round of the Golden Ladle Championship will be held without a live audience. We apologize for the sudden change, but rest assured, the competition will continue as planned." He paused, glancing toward the stage. "Now, let us welcome the first finalist, the dark horse of the tournament, our city’s savior... Chef Soren!"
Applause filled the stadium; however, anyone could tell it was fake, a recorded audio being played.
All the cameras turned toward Soren.
’Urgh... Damn it! Why did it have to be like this?’ Faris cursed as he used the chance to take a look at the live stream chat.
[User0290: Urgh! F*ck! Why did they do this?]
[IAmHim: Who cares? As long as it’s happening.]
[RichGuy77: Urgh! Damn! I spent half my money on those tickets! I wanna get a refund! Gimme back my money!]
[User1207: ! ! These damn organizers!]
[Beatifull: Let’s report them all! ]

’Damn it!’ Faris cursed again as he scrolled, his eyes scanning one curse after another insult. Sure, there were some viewers who were cheering, but they were one in a fifty or so. And some were cheering just to rage-bait the other viewers.
’I shouldn’t have agreed to this!’ Faris regretted his decision. ’Why did I have to agree even when Senior Layla rejected it?!’
[Message: Get back to work!]
’Urgh!’
However, it was too late to back out now.
’At least they’re paying handsomely.’
He consoled himself as the cameras turned back to him.
"Now, let’s welcome the favorite of the competition, a disciple who is planning to surpass his master, Chef Damir!"
The scene repeated itself, the chat growing even more heated, to the point that more than a thousand viewers got banned in just five minutes.
"Now, the final contestant, our mysterious elf chef, lady who stole many hearts with both her beauty and dishes, Chef Nuelia!"
Applause filled the stadium again, but even after a minute, there was no sign of her.
"Chef Nuelia!" Faris called out again. "You can come out now.
Silence enveloped the stadium again.
Soren and Damir exchanged a glance, each of them confused by the situation.
’Did they lie?’ Soren expanded his perception, scanning the surroundings for their presence. ’No, they wouldn’t. They wouldn’t dare.’

Kidnapping a noble elf was one thing, but kidnapping the princess of the strongest Empire on the continent and not returning her? They would be morons to mess with the Imperial Family like that. No matter how busy the Paragon of Order was, Soren was sure he could spare some time to find his descendant and put those who dared to mess with his family in their place. Even if he wouldn’t, the retaliation from the current Emperor would be enough to wipe them all out.

’They must know that too.’ He squinted. ’So they will likely use her as a bargaining chip, and release her when the time is right. Or they already planned to return her from the start, knowing that holding her too long would bring the full might of the empire down on them. They need her for something specific, something we don’t know yet...’
’As for Lady Nuelia...’
He wasn’t completely certain. After all, they knew little about her and had no idea of her true nobility or the strength of her background.
’Let’s hope they will stick to their words.’

Just as the thought crossed his mind, the air above the stage rippled. A tear of light split the space, widening into a shimmering portal. The few staff members froze, and Faris’s voice cut through the silence.
"What’s happening?! Is this part of the show?!"
Soren and Damir both tensed.
The guards near the edge of the stage reached for their weapons. Everyone watched as a figure stepped through the portal, staggering slightly as her feet hit the ground.

"Oh! Is that... Chef Nuelia?!" Faris exclaimed, leaning over his platform to get a better look. "It’s really her! Thank goodness! I thought she-wait! Why does she look so pale?! Did something happen to her?"
"Lady Nuelia!" Soren reacted quickly and moved toward her, crossing the distance in a few strides to catch her before her knees gave out.

"Are you ok?" He asked as he checked her condition. Her face was pale, her breathing uneven, and there was a faint sheen of sweat on her brow. Whatever she had been through, it had clearly taken a toll on her.
However, he also didn’t forget to use the Advanced Appraisal to get a good look at her condition and confirm whether it was really her.
’Hmm...’ As he scanned the system while taking out health and vitality potions from his inventory, his hands froze for a moment before quickening. "H-Here, drink this!"
"M-Mr... So... ren?" Nuelia muttered weakly, her eyes struggling to focus on him as he helped her drink the potions.
"That’s right, it’s me," Soren replied, watching as color slowly returned to her face and her breathing steadied as the effects took hold. "You’re safe..."
"T-Thank... you..."
"It’s nothing, just relax and take it easy now..." His voice trailed off, and he fell silent, his mind racing as he held her steady. ’It worked...’

Actually, her condition was far worse than it looked. She was completely out of mana, and her life force was dangerously low. If he hadn’t used the Sovereign Vitality Elixir just now, the consequences would have been severe.
’Just what did they do to her?’ Soren’s eyes narrowed as he looked toward the portal. He could somehow sense there were people behind it. ’...’

"Ahem! Ahem! Oh, it’s working." Faris tapped the mic a few times, as if he was using it for the first time. "Ahem. Ladies and gentlemen, forgive the slight technical hiccup! As you can see, Chef Nuelia has been safely returned to the stage, courtesy of our... distinguished unexpected guests. And I received word that we have another contestant joining us in the final round!
’!’ Soren’s eyes widened as he looked toward the broadcasting platform. ’Is it him?! No, it must be him.’
Even though he sounded and acted like Faris, Soren knew it was the possessor guy.
’Then...’
His gaze shifted toward the portal as three figures stepped out, the atmosphere changing in an instant.

On either side stood a figure draped in long, hooded garments that concealed every inch of their features, casting deep shadows over their faces. Between these two shrouded companions walked a remarkably handsome youth. With immaculate blonde hair and an almost flawless face, he moved with an unbothered grace, as if he owned the stage.

"And there he is! A young gentleman who clearly needs no introduction, radiating an effortless perfection that captures the entire arena’s attention! We are truly blessed to have someone of his magnificent stature participating today!" Faris, the fake one, started clapping enthusiastically into his mic. "Just look at him! Look at that posture! That flawless complexion! A true diamond among stones, folks! You can practically feel the overwhelming majesty radiating from his very presence! An absolute prodigy of our era, stepping into the ring purely to grant us the honor of watching him work!"
Faris kept glazing until the young man looked in his direction with an annoyed stare.
"Give it up for the best chef in the continent, and the future best chef in the whole world," Faris exclaimed with a dramatic gesture, "Chef Lucent!"
Clap-! Clap-!
Faris and the two figures accompanying the young man clapped with enthusiasm. In fact, they were the only ones doing it; even the fake applause audio wasn’t being played.
"..." Faris abruptly stopped, staring at the cameras coldly. "I said, give it up."
A beat of quiet passed.
"WHOOO!"
"CLAP-!"
The speakers suddenly flared, unleashing a wave of deafening applause and cheering that flooded the entire arena.
"Hehe, now that is more like it." The bright smile instantly snapped back onto Faris’s face as if it had never left.
The applause continued for a whole minute before Faris stopped it.

"Now then, esteemed contestants, please take your respective cooking stations!" He paused, turning to the organizers with a raised hand. "And if you’d be so kind, prepare another one for Chef Lucent. We can’t have our guest of honor standing around empty-handed, now can we? And be quick; don’t keep us waiting."
He then turned his gaze back to the stage. "Now, two gentlemen, will you help the other two contestants ’get ready’ for the final round?"
The two hooded figures nodded and started moving.

"And Mr. Soren and Damir." Faris addressed the two, a meaningful smile playing on his lips. "If you don’t want any unnecessary complications during this grand showcase, I recommend not showing any resistance and letting the two gentlemen do their work."

’Damn it!’ Faris cursed again as he scrolled, his eyes scanning one curse after another insult.
Sure, there were some viewers who were cheering, but they were one in a fifty or so.
And some were cheering just to rage-bait the other viewers.
’I shouldn’t have agreed to this!’ Faris regretted his decision. ’Why did I have to agree even when Senior Layla rejected it?!’
[Message: Get back to work!]
’Urgh!’
However, it was too late to back out now.
’At least they’re paying handsomely.’
He consoled himself as the cameras turned back to him.
"Now, let’s welcome the favorite of the competition, a disciple who is planning to surpass his master, Chef Damir!"
The scene repeated itself, the chat growing even more heated, to the point that more than a thousand viewers got banned in just five minutes.
"Now, the final contestant, our mysterious elf chef, lady who stole many hearts with both her beauty and dishes, Chef Nuelia!"
Applause filled the stadium again, but even after a minute, there was no sign of her.
"Chef Nuelia!" Faris called out again.
"You can come out now.
Silence enveloped the stadium again.
Soren and Damir exchanged a glance, each of them confused by the situation.
’Did they lie?’ Soren expanded his perception, scanning the surroundings for their presence. ’No, they wouldn’t.
They wouldn’t dare.’
Kidnapping a noble elf was one thing, but kidnapping the princess of the strongest Empire on the continent and not returning her?
They would be morons to mess with the Imperial Family like that.
No matter how busy the Paragon of Order was, Soren was sure he could spare some time to find his descendant and put those who dared to mess with his family in their place.
Even if he wouldn’t, the retaliation from the current Emperor would be enough to wipe them all out.
’They must know that too.’ He squinted. ’So they will likely use her as a bargaining chip, and release her when the time is right.
Or they already planned to return her from the start, knowing that holding her too long would bring the full might of the empire down on them.
They need her for something specific, something we don’t know yet...’
’As for Lady Nuelia...’
He wasn’t completely certain.
After all, they knew little about her and had no idea of her true nobility or the strength of her background.
’Let’s hope they will stick to their words.’
Just as the thought crossed his mind, the air above the stage rippled.
A tear of light split the space, widening into a shimmering portal.
The few staff members froze, and Faris’s voice cut through the silence.
"What’s happening?!
Is this part of the show?!"
Soren and Damir both tensed.
The guards near the edge of the stage reached for their weapons.
Everyone watched as a figure stepped through the portal, staggering slightly as her feet hit the ground.
"Oh!
Is that...
Chef Nuelia?!" Faris exclaimed, leaning over his platform to get a better look.
"It’s really her!
Thank goodness!
I thought she-wait!
Why does she look so pale?!
Did something happen to her?"
"Lady Nuelia!" Soren reacted quickly and moved toward her, crossing the distance in a few strides to catch her before her knees gave out.
"Are you ok?" He asked as he checked her condition.
Her face was pale, her breathing uneven, and there was a faint sheen of sweat on her brow.
Whatever she had been through, it had clearly taken a toll on her.
However, he also didn’t forget to use the Advanced Appraisal to get a good look at her condition and confirm whether it was really her.
’Hmm...’ As he scanned the system while taking out health and vitality potions from his inventory, his hands froze for a moment before quickening.
"H-Here, drink this!"
So... ren?" Nuelia muttered weakly, her eyes struggling to focus on him as he helped her drink the potions.
"That’s right, it’s me," Soren replied, watching as color slowly returned to her face and her breathing steadied as the effects took hold.
"You’re safe..."
"T-Thank... you..."
"It’s nothing, just relax and take it easy now..." His voice trailed off, and he fell silent, his mind racing as he held her steady. ’It worked...’
Actually, her condition was far worse than it looked.
She was completely out of mana, and her life force was dangerously low.
If he hadn’t used the Sovereign Vitality Elixir just now, the consequences would have been severe.
’Just what did they do to her?’ Soren’s eyes narrowed as he looked toward the portal.
He could somehow sense there were people behind it. ’...’
"Ahem!
Ahem!
Oh, it’s working." Faris tapped the mic a few times, as if he was using it for the first time.
"Ahem.
Ladies and gentlemen, forgive the slight technical hiccup!
As you can see, Chef Nuelia has been safely returned to the stage, courtesy of our... distinguished unexpected guests.
And I received word that we have another contestant joining us in the final round!
’!’ Soren’s eyes widened as he looked toward the broadcasting platform. ’Is it him?!
No, it must be him.’
Even though he sounded and acted like Faris, Soren knew it was the possessor guy.
’Then...’
His gaze shifted toward the portal as three figures stepped out, the atmosphere changing in an instant.
On either side stood a figure draped in long, hooded garments that concealed every inch of their features, casting deep shadows over their faces.
Between these two shrouded companions walked a remarkably handsome youth.
With immaculate blonde hair and an almost flawless face, he moved with an unbothered grace, as if he owned the stage.
"And there he is!
A young gentleman who clearly needs no introduction, radiating an effortless perfection that captures the entire arena’s attention!
We are truly blessed to have someone of his magnificent stature participating today!" Faris, the fake one, started clapping enthusiastically into his mic.
"Just look at him!
Look at that posture!
That flawless complexion!
A true diamond among stones, folks!
You can practically feel the overwhelming majesty radiating from his very presence!
An absolute prodigy of our era, stepping into the ring purely to grant us the honor of watching him work!"
Faris kept glazing until the young man looked in his direction with an annoyed stare.
"Give it up for the best chef in the continent, and the future best chef in the whole world," Faris exclaimed with a dramatic gesture, "Chef Lucent!"
Clap-!
Clap-!
Faris and the two figures accompanying the young man clapped with enthusiasm.
In fact, they were the only ones doing it; even the fake applause audio wasn’t being played.
"..." Faris abruptly stopped, staring at the cameras coldly.
"I said, give it up."
A beat of quiet passed.
"WHOOO!"
"CLAP-!"
The speakers suddenly flared, unleashing a wave of deafening applause and cheering that flooded the entire arena.
"Hehe, now that is more like it." The bright smile instantly snapped back onto Faris’s face as if it had never left.
The applause continued for a whole minute before Faris stopped it.
"Now then, esteemed contestants, please take your respective cooking stations!" He paused, turning to the organizers with a raised hand.
"And if you’d be so kind, prepare another one for Chef Lucent.
We can’t have our guest of honor standing around empty-handed, now can we?
And be quick; don’t keep us waiting."
He then turned his gaze back to the stage.
"Now, two gentlemen, will you help the other two contestants ’get ready’ for the final round?"
The two hooded figures nodded and started moving.
"And Mr.
Soren and Damir." Faris addressed the two, a meaningful smile playing on his lips.
"If you don’t want any unnecessary complications during this grand showcase, I recommend not showing any resistance and letting the two gentlemen do their work."

Age: 42
Status: Healthy
Mental State: Observant, Cautious
Ability: Null Constitution
Affinities: None
Hidden Talent / Traits: Mana Void, Pain Tolerance
Potential: ?
Investment Value: High
’Null Constitution... Ethea guessed it right.’ Soren thought to himself as he scanned the status windows. ’It’s really the Hollow Pair. But... who is the third one?’
His gaze landed on the blonde young man.
Name: Lucent Starlight
Race: Human
Age: 24
Status: Healthy
Rank: Unawakened
Mental State: Amused, Confident, Unbothered
Hidden Talent / Traits: Keen Nose, Spoiled, Entitled
Potential: ?
Investment Value: Low
’He’s unawakened?’ He squinted in confusion. ’Why did they bring an ordinary person here?’
However, as he heard the fake Faris start to introduce the guy, the pieces started to fall into place.

At the same time, the surrounding mana suddenly began to fluctuate, like ripples spreading across the surface of a lake before vanishing into nothing. The air grew still, and within the span of a single breath, every trace of mana in the arena was gone. Soren felt it in his chest, a strange hollowness where his connection to the mana had been. It was as if the world itself had gone mute.
’...So this is how his constitution works. It’s indeed a terrifying thing to experience firsthand.’
Had it not been for his own constitution, he would be reacting like the guards below, gasping for breath and even collapsing.
’Fortunately, Lady Nuelia and Sir Damir look fine.’
A few more minutes, and she would be able to stand on her own. However, for the sake of safety, Soren carried her away from the portal and the three newcomers.
They noticed but fortunately didn’t act.

’...For now, things are going as planned.’ Soren thought to himself as he saw Lariel floating above the arena, staring coldly at the two hooded figures. ’I just hope he doesn’t lose control of his emotions and mess everything up again.’
"...Mr. Soren and Damir..."

Hearing the fake Faris address them, Soren shifted his gaze to the approaching figures. The pressure emanating from the two-meter-tall Nullifier intensified, and Soren even felt as if his vitality was being sucked out of his body from just standing too close.
’This explains why Nuelia was in that state. She must have been-’

His train of thought was cut short as Leech grabbed Damir’s wrist. Within seconds, the color drained from Damir’s face. His knees buckled, sending him straight to the floor. Before Soren could react, Leech casually reached out and grabbed his arm next.

The next moment, Soren felt the mana inside him surge toward the point of contact, pulled by an invisible current. It was like his blood was being drawn out through a wound he couldn’t see. His core convulsed, and his knees almost buckled as the draining continued. The world dimmed at the edges, and the hollow sensation spread through his chest.
"Hmm?" The Leech raised a brow as he continued to drain Soren’s mana. ’How does he have so much mana? Its purity is extremely high too...’
But Soren didn’t give him time to dwell on it and used the Pebble Among Stars to the fullest.
"Huff... Huff..."

For the sake of appearances, he let himself collapse onto his knees, breathing raggedly as if he had been drained to the brink. His shoulders heaved, and he kept his head low, hiding the faint gleam in his eyes.
The Leech watched him for a moment longer, then let out a short, dismissive snort.
"Hmph. Nothing special."

He finally took his hand away and walked away with the Nullifier. They paused briefly in front of the blonde young man, and Soren managed to overhear them saying, "Good luck, Young Master. We believe in you!"

’...I get it now.’ Soren continued to pretend as his mind raced. ’Lucent guy must be the son of their leader, and he is probably the reason why all of this is even happening, considering his traits...’
However, he didn’t let his guard down, recalling everything Ethea said about them yesterday.
’This might be a distraction from their actual plan, so we need to stick to the plan...’
"Hey."
Soren looked up just in time to see Lucent toss a small bottle toward him. It stopped just short of his knee, then another was thrown to Damir, who was still trying to catch his breath.
"Drink it," Lucent said with an annoyed expression. "I don’t wanna win by playing dirty. There’s no fun in that."
Soren’s eyes flicked to the vial, activating Advanced Appraisal. ’...It’s a high-quality vitality replenishment potion.’
’...He must really be spoiled.’ Soren thought as he uncorked it and drank, keeping his movements weak and hesitant. ’Throwing around something this expensive like it’s nothing.’
"Huff... Huff..." He let his breathing slowly begin to steady while watching color return to Damir’s face soon after he swallowed his own potion.
"Hey!" Lucent turned toward the broadcasting platform. "Explain the rules while they recover. We don’t have enough time to waste."
"Ah, yes! Sorry for the delay!" The fake Faris bowed apologetically, then straightened and looked at the camera.

"Ladies and gentlemen, due to the special circumstances I mentioned earlier, the rules of the final round have also changed. From this point on, contestants will not be allowed to use mana in any form. You may only use the basic tools provided at your stations and the ingredients already there. Everything must be done by hand, including creating and controlling the flames."
He paused, letting the rule settle before continuing.

"After all, a true chef must be able to create a masterpiece without relying on special ingredients or tools. In this world, too many have grown dependent on their gifts, hiding behind affinities, artifacts, and enchantments to make up for their lack of real skill. If you cannot create something magnificent with your own two hands, then you have no right to call yourself a chef."

chapters.title: Chapter 287: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [3]
paragraphs: "...Now then, let us see who among you has the soul of a true chef, and who has been hiding behind their power all along." Faris spread his arms wide as he finished his explanation. "Let the final round begin!"
The applause echoed from the speakers, and fireworks burst to life above the arena, coloring the sky in flashes of gold and crimson.

Lucent immediately moved toward his station, his hands already reaching for the ingredients with an eagerness that felt out of place. Meanwhile, Soren, Damir, and Nuelia exchanged uneasy glances, still processing what just happened.
"Hey!"

’...Let’s play along.’ Soren sent them a telepathic message, and they both flinched and looked at him, surprised. ’I know you’re confused, but keep your expressions in check. Act natural, and don’t let them notice it.’
He added out loud with a smile. "Good luck."
Damir and Nuelia quickly realized it and schooled their expressions, turning back to face their stations after returning a nod. "Good luck to you too."
’For now, do your best and aim to win. Treat it as the real final round.’ Soren added. ’Leave the rest to the Emperors.’
’...Gulp.’ Both Nuelia and Damir swallowed, inwardly relieved to have someone protecting them.

"...Now, let’s focus on the task," Soren muttered to himself as he scanned the ingredients. Surprisingly, they were all ordinary ingredients. He even peeked at the other three stations and found the same setup. ’At least they aren’t playing dirty, or there’s nothing poisonous.’

Relieved, he started thinking about what to make. He had countless recipes, even for ordinary meals, in his mind; however, he decided to play fair and challenge himself. Because the fake Faris’s words ignited something inside him. He liked cooking, even before he became a magic chef, even when he was alone. While he wasn’t exactly amazing back then, he had still found comfort in the act itself.
’...It really brings back memories, huh.’ He chuckled to himself as ideas started appearing in his mind. ’...Wait, what if I make that?’

He froze, memories rushing back to a time when he had nothing but flour and eggs. He didn’t have enough money to buy meat or vegetables, so he had to do with what little he had. Although it didn’t turn out that well the first time, he improved it after a few tries.
’...I don’t know whether it will count as an original recipe, but I am definitely going with this. After all, it was the first meal I ever created on my own.’
He took a deep breath and quickly prepared the materials he needed.
’First, let’s prepare the dough...’

He poured water into a large bowl and then cracked two eggs into it, one after the other, before adding a generous pinch of salt. He then whisked the mixture vigorously until the yolks broke and completely blended with the water, turning the liquid a rich yellow.

He then reached for the flour, scooping it into a sifter held over the bowl. With rhythmic taps of his palm against the rim, a fine white cloud rained down, burying the yellow liquid beneath a growing mound.

He plunged his hands into the center. His fingers twisted and turned, drawing the dry powder into the wet core. Strands of sticky paste began to cling to his knuckles as the loose particles bound together, forming a shaggy mass that gradually cleared the sides of the bowl.

He tipped the heavy cluster out onto the floured wooden table. Leaning his weight forward, he pressed the heels of both palms deep into the center, pushed the mass away from him, folded it back over itself, and pressed again.

He kept up the rhythmic motion for ten full minutes. With every turn, the shaggy edges tucked away, and the resistance beneath his hands changed. The stickiness disappeared, replaced by a smooth surface that sprang back slightly when pressed. Finally, he shaped it into a golden ball, placed it back in the bowl, and draped a damp cloth over the top.
’First step is done.’ He muttered inwardly. ’The next step is preparing the filling...’
He took another large bowl and put it right in front of him, next to the remaining eggs.

One by one, he picked them up, cracked the shells against the rim with a sharp ’tap’, and let the slick whites and golden yolks slide into the bottom of the bowl. He kept a steady rhythm until a dozen yolks floated together in a glossy pool.

He then grabbed a heavy wire whisk and plunged it into the center, breaking the yolks. The metallic sloshing echoed as he whipped the eggs in circular motions, blending them until the mixture became a completely pale yellow liquid.

Next, he poured in a splash of milk and a slow stream of vegetable oil, watching the liquids create swirling white and clear ribbons before the whisk forced them to merge. He finished it with a generous pinch of salt and a few shakes of black pepper, giving it one last stir. The filling remained completely fluid, sloshing easily against the sides of the bowl.
’This should be enough.’
He stopped and closed the bowl with a lid.
’I should prepare the fire now to boil the water...’ He paused as he looked at what he had. ’They were really serious about the rules, huh.’
The only things available were a pile of firewood, a metal grate, and a simple iron pot.
’Well, thankfully, I learned how to cook over an open fire.’ He didn’t think it would come in handy at a time like this. ’Guess no knowledge is ever truly useless.’

Smiling, he started stacking the wood carefully, leaving space for air, and reached for the flint and steel beside the station. A few strikes were all it took. The sparks caught, and soon the flames began to climb, crackling softly as the wood caught fire. He adjusted the grate over the flames and set the pot of water on top, watching as the first bubbles began to form at the bottom.
’Nice!’
He grinned and immediately turned his attention back to the table.
’The dough should be ready by now.’

’Well, thankfully, I learned how to cook over an open fire.’ He didn’t think it would come in handy at a time like this. ’Guess no knowledge is ever truly useless.’
Smiling, he started stacking the wood carefully, leaving space for air, and reached for the flint and steel beside the station.
A few strikes were all it took.
The sparks caught, and soon the flames began to climb, crackling softly as the wood caught fire.
He adjusted the grate over the flames and set the pot of water on top, watching as the first bubbles began to form at the bottom.
’Nice!’
He grinned and immediately turned his attention back to the table.
’The dough should be ready by now.’

chapters.title: Chapter 288: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [4]
paragraphs: Soren lifted the cloth, revealing the golden ball. Its surface had become smoother and slightly matte. He pressed a thumb into the side; the indentation stayed, showing the dough had lost its elasticity and was now perfectly supple.

He grabbed a handful of flour and scattered it across the table, creating a thin sheet of white to prevent any sticking. Using a knife, he sliced the dough ball cleanly down the middle, set one half back under the cloth, and placed the other half in front of him.

He then flattened the piece with the palm of his hand, then picked up a long wooden rolling pin. Starting at the center, he began rolling the dough outward. After a few strokes, he skillfully lifted the expanding sheet, gave it a quarter turn, and rolled again, keeping it circular.

Gradually, the dough grew wider and wider, stretching across the table until it was as thin as parchment. He ran his palms lightly across the surface, checking for any thick spots. Once he was fully satisfied, he paused, wondering whether to cut it into rectangles or circles.
’Hmm... We have to present them later too...’
Thinking of that, he decided to go with the circles first, as they would look like half-moon pillows once finished.
’I can make the other part rectangular.’
Nodding to himself, he searched the table, and his eyes landed on a glass. He took it in his hands and measured it. ’Yeah, this should do it.’
He turned it upside down and pressed firmly into the thin sheet of dough. With a swift twist of his wrist, the glass sliced through the dough, leaving a perfect disk behind.
’Good.’ He smiled and continued until the sheet resembled a honeycomb. He then peeled away the leftover dough scraps, leaving a grid of circles on the table.

’And now...’ He picked up a wrapper. After dipping his index finger into water, he lightly traced the dampness along the edge. He then carefully folded the circle over to create a semi-circle. Working from the outer corners inward, he pinched the edges together and stopped before reaching the center. He had to leave a small gap to put in the filling later.
’Hmm... It looks good enough.’ He smiled as he put it away on a plate he had already prepared. ’Though I will have to add some final touches to make it look more pleasing to the eye.’
With that in mind, he continued with the rest of the wrappers until a neat row of identical half-moon pouches lined the plate.
He then checked the water and noticed it was ready to use.
’Let’s add some salt and vegetable oil.’

’...Hmm. Now, the final step.’ He picked up a dough pouch and held the small gap open with his fingers. He poured the liquid egg filling straight into the opening, filling it three-quarters full. Next, he sealed the gap shut and dropped it into the boiling water. Within seconds, the dough ballooned into a plump shape and floated to the top. He worked quickly, dropping the rest until the pot was full.
’While they are boiling, I should get started on the other half,’ he muttered while adjusting the flames. ’And prepare some sauce to go with them...’
Time passed as he worked through the remaining dough, shifting between the bubbling pot and the floured table until he used the last of the filling and had no dough left.

Finally, he scooped the ready egg dumplings out of the water with a slotted spoon, letting the excess moisture drain away. He carefully placed each on a large ceramic platter and put a small bowl of sour cream sauce in the center.
"...Done!"
He smiled in satisfaction as he looked at his masterpiece.
The taste, the look, the smell, the texture... everything turned out exactly as he envisioned. He covered the platter with a lid to keep it warm, then finally allowed himself to glance at the others.

Nuelia was... she was struggling more than Soren had expected. Like usual, she was cooking something vegetarian. However, she struggled with the fire, her hands hovering uncertainly over the flames as she adjusted the wood again and again. It was clear she wasn’t used to cooking without mana, and open flame was too wild to her liking. Her usual calm expression had long since become tense, but Soren had to give it to her since she didn’t give up and kept trying.
’I guess she is more stubborn than she looks.’ Chuckling inwardly, he turned his attention to the next station where Damir was constantly stirring his pot. ’Hmm... Is he making some kind of soup?’
Soren guessed after giving a quick look at the station. ’Whatever it is, he seems like he’s doing well, at least.’

Soren guessed Grandmaster Tamimi must have taught him everything, including ordinary cooking. After all, one couldn’t become a magic chef without learning the basics first. There was even a chance Damir became his disciple at a young age, and since he had been just a kid with no mana, he could only learn traditional cooking.

Satisfied with that reasoning, Soren let his gaze drift past Damir to the last station at the other side of the stage. ’Hmm... It’s a bit hard to tell from here. However, it is clear that he is working hard, as everyone else.’
Lucent’s head was down, his hands moving non-stop, while a faint smile lingered on his lips. There was no hesitation in his movements; it was as if he had done it many times before.
’I guess he really loves cooking...’
The thought crossed his mind as he watched Lucent work.

’Perhaps he wanted to participate in this competition but couldn’t, since he is unawakened. So he asked, or ordered, these guys to help him. And since he was their spoiled young master, they had agreed and came up with this plan...’
It sounded ridiculous at first, but it also made sense somehow.
After all, Ethea said they do whatever they want whenever they want, and most of the time, there is no greater plan behind their actions.
’...Let’s just hope this theory is true.’

chapters.title: Chapter 289: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [5]
paragraphs: ’...Human. We have sealed the entire arena. They can’t open portals or teleport now, from either inside or outside. However, we have yet to locate your princess and the bastard possessor.’
’I see...’ Soren replied as he continued to act like he was still working. ’Then did you check it yet? That is... can you use mana inside?’

’Yes, we all tried it,’ the response came immediately, ’however, it didn’t work. Even when we opened our domains, nothing changed. We couldn’t even summon our magic beasts or spirits. His anti-mana constitution must be more powerful than we expected.’
’Hmmm... To think even 7th Circles would be affected by it.’ Soren squinted. ’That is indeed frightening.’

He paused for a few moments before adding. ’Actually, I think I uncovered something useful earlier. The two of them called this Lucent guy their young master and were quite respectful too.’ Soren quickly explained his earlier theory. ’...So, I have a proposal. What if we capture him and then trade him to the princess?’
’Is that so...’ The voice muttered back in surprise. ’...Let me share the info with the others then. I will come back as-’

’Wait.’ Soren cut the voice off. ’I have something else to say. I can participate in the battle, but we need someone who can fight well without their mana and has a strong body. Or else, you will be useless against those two, even if you are an emperor.’
’...Ok. I will share it too.’ The voice agreed. ’Though I think the human knight suits perfectly for the job.’
’Yeah, I had the same thought.’ Soren nodded inwardly. ’However, two of us might struggle to finish the task, so the more skillful fighters we have, the better our chances. Tell that to them too.’
’...Understood.’
The voice disappeared right after, leaving Soren alone with his own thoughts once again.
’...Good thing I prepared a backup plan.’

He hadn’t told the others because he feared that the possessor guy might learn about it somehow. However, if his plan worked, their chances of rescuing the princess and capturing them all would rise exponentially.

’...But before that, I have to use this chance to push myself to the limit and improve as much as I can!’ Soren tightened his fists, his gaze falling on the Hollow Pair. ’And you... you guys are the perfect whetstones!’
Even if he had to fight till death, he would still do it. Because that was the only way to truly grow stronger and survive in a world that showed no mercy to the weak!

’Hoo...’ Soren exhaled as he took control of his emotions. It was not the time to get worked up just yet. ’Hmm... there are ten minutes left...’ He looked at the countdown and then back at those three. ’Damir and Lucent will finish in a few minutes, but...’
He paused as he looked at Nuelia. She was sweating from both the fire and the tension. After all, she failed the first two portions of her meal, and this was her last chance. ’...Hey, calm down.’
’!’ Nuelia froze.
’Don’t react to me and just listen.’ Soren added. ’I will guide you on how to salvage what you have. You won’t be able to win at this point, but you can at least finish your meal properly.’
Nuelia’s hands trembled slightly, but she gave no other signs of their secret conversation.

’Throw away any distracting thoughts and emotions you have,’ Soren advised as he continued to clean his station. ’The previous failures don’t matter; what matters is what’s in front of you right now. Focus only on the task at hand and ignore everything else.’
Nuelia stood still, then closed her eyes. A moment later, she took a deep breath and let it all out.
’...Good, now listen carefully...’
"BOOOM!"

Fireworks exploded across the sky in a dazzling array of colors, painting the arena in a brilliant light. The applause audio was played once again. However, it seemed like the crowd had gathered outside the arena, as faint cheers could be heard coming from that direction too.
"Time’s up!" Faris’s excited voice echoed through the arena. "All contestants, step away from your stations!"
They did as they were told.

"Now then, let me explain the judging process." Faris continued. "Actually, it’s not that different from the semi-final. Judges will give their points, and contestants will also judge each other. However... we will also pick two random viewers from the chat to join us!"
Faris grinned as he looked at the cameras.

"That’s right, everyone! As long as you’re in Bagdad City and are watching the competition live, you have a chance to become one of the chosen ones! All you have to do is type ’I want to taste!’ in the chat. We will check your eligibility and add you to the random draw. Hurry up! You only have one minute!"
Another countdown appeared on the main screen and the livestream.
"Meanwhile, we will prepare and start with the judges’ evaluations!"
As soon as he announced it, the nearby staff started moving on their own toward the stations.
’...They’ve been taken over.’ Soren could tell it at a glance. First, it was the guards; now it is the staff. ’...What about the judges then?’

He couldn’t tell how powerful the possessor guy was anymore, since all the guards surrounding the stage were at the 6th circle or were A- and S-rank Hunters. ’I have a feeling we will end up fighting with them later too...’

He regretted his decision to advise the City Lord about this yesterday. But there was no point dwelling on the past now. What mattered was that they had kept up appearances and, in doing so, gained valuable info. They knew the possessor could control anyone below the 7th circle without much effort. The only exceptions seemed to be people like Soren or Ethea, whose mental power and defenses were strong enough to resist.
’As for the reason... he probably realized it too... that there will be an inevitable confrontation. He will try to overwhelm us with numbers.’

’It’s a good thing that I kept my real strength hidden and appeared as weak as possible. Since he thinks I’m not a threat because I can’t fight without my magic beast, I can catch them off guard when the time comes...’

chapters.title: Chapter 290: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [6]
paragraphs: "Let’s start with contestant Soren’s dish since he was the first to finish!"
Faris announced, and the staff immediately moved to carry Soren’s dish to the judges’ table.
"Now, let’s hear it from Chef Soren, Bagdad’s Savior, himself," Faris asked. "Can you tell us what kind of masterpiece have you prepared?"
"..." Soren glanced at the broadcasting platform and turned back to the judges. ’So this is how you wanna play...’

He took a deep breath and started his presentation speech. "Actually, I wouldn’t call it a masterpiece. It’s just a simple meal I made back when I had no money and no proper cooking skills, but it served its purpose well. It filled my stomach and kept me going through difficult times, which is more than enough for any meal to do."
He paused briefly, his gaze fixed on the judges.

"I believe food doesn’t need to be extravagant to hold meaning. A dish born from necessity can hold just as much value as one crafted from luxury, if not more. That’s what this dish represents to me, and that’s why I chose to present it here today."

"Furthermore, whether I win or not, I plan to share the recipe with everyone freely after the competition." Soren’s expression softened slightly. "I hope it reaches those who need it most, whether they’re struggling to make ends meet or simply looking for something to fill their stomachs. If it can do for them what it once did for me, then that alone would make this worth it."
He bowed subtly and finished his presentation.
"Whoa! What wise words!" Faris exclaimed as the speakers sang loudly with cheers. "As expected of Bagdad’s Savior! However, let’s see what the judges will have to say about that."
Everyone watched as the judges tasted Soren’s meal, their curious expressions shifting to surprise and even contentment. And, just like in the semi-final, they ended up finishing everything.
"As expected of Chef Soren." The first one said. "You never cease to amaze me! I give a perfect score again!"
"It was better than I expected, though it fell short of getting the perfect score this time." The second one sighed as if disappointed. "I will give eight points."
"...Nine."
"...Eight."
"...Nine."
"Whoa, I guess Chef Soren was truly a great chef!" Faris laughed as the judges finished their evaluations. "However, I wonder what his rivals will think of his dish?"
As soon as he finished speaking, the cameras zoomed in on the table specifically prepared for the finalists. They had also finished eating their portions.
Nuelia was the first to give her score: 10.
Damir followed up with a 9.

"I was right about you," Lucent spoke up as the attention shifted to him. "You truly have great talent in cooking. The flavors were well balanced, and the simplicity worked in your favor." He paused, a faint smile tugging at the corner of his lips. "I acknowledge you as my rival, Soren. That said, it wasn’t perfect. There were a few flaws, so I’ll give it a 9 as well."
"..." Soren started back at Lucent and nodded with a smile.
The next moment, the average of the finalists was calculated and added to the judges’ points. Soren’s current score shot up to 63.3 points on the main screen.
"Since the lucky judges are still on the way, let’s continue with the next contestant," Faris announced. "Chef Damir, please take the stage."

Damir nodded, swapped places with Soren, and presented his own dish. It was really a soup, as Soren had guessed earlier. According to Damir, this was also the first meal he had ever created. It had been a task given by his master before he could even begin learning how to make magic meals. He mentioned he prepared this because it was the first time his master had ever praised him back then.
Judges tasted his dish and gave their scores. It came close to Soren’s result, but in the end, it fell one point short of his total.

Soren tasted it himself and gave it a 9 since he noticed a flaw this time. Nuelia and Lucent, however, ended up giving 8 points. As a result, Damir’s score ended up at 61.3 points, just two points below Soren’s.
Next came Nuelia’s turn. She stepped forward hesitantly and couldn’t speak for a moment. Only after she saw a certain someone nodding at her with an encouraging smile did she calm down and speak.

"This... this is my first time cooking like this," she admitted, her gaze sincere. "I know I made mistakes, but I tried my best. Please judge me fairly and give me your honest opinions. I want to learn from this."
The judges nodded and started eating. Some stopped after taking a few bites, while some finished everything.
"This is amazing for your first try." One of the judges praised. "However, you still have a lot to improve. I recommend practicing how to control the fire first. But the rest is good."
They gave her a 7. Other judges followed up with their honest opinions and gave similar scores, but none of them gave more than 7.
"I saw how hard you worked," Soren said as his turn came. "And I am sure you will master it pretty soon if you keep practicing. It’s an 8 from me."
"I understand this was your first time," Damir followed, "but I’m sorry; your mistakes were too obvious to ignore. So I’ll give 6 too."

"..." Lucent stared at Nuelia and chuckled mockingly. "I guess what Sister Monie told me about you elves was true. You’re an arrogant race who rely on your innate talents and long lifespans to feel superior. But strip those away, and you’re useless. Take away your magic and your centuries of privilege, and you can’t even do something as simple as cooking a proper meal. I now understand how difficult it must have been for her... Anyway, don’t expect any mercy from me!"
He laughed coldly and raised his score.
It was... 3.
"I added an extra 2 points since you actually kept trying even after failing, and didn’t fear facing the judgment head-on. So I guess you’re somewhat better than the rest of your kind."

"It was better than I expected, though it fell short of getting the perfect score this time." The second one sighed as if disappointed.
"I will give eight points."
"...Nine."
"...Eight."
"...Nine."
"Whoa, I guess Chef Soren was truly a great chef!" Faris laughed as the judges finished their evaluations.
"However, I wonder what his rivals will think of his dish?"
As soon as he finished speaking, the cameras zoomed in on the table specifically prepared for the finalists.
They had also finished eating their portions.
Nuelia was the first to give her score: 10.
Damir followed up with a 9.
"I was right about you," Lucent spoke up as the attention shifted to him.
"You truly have great talent in cooking.
The flavors were well balanced, and the simplicity worked in your favor." He paused, a faint smile tugging at the corner of his lips.
"I acknowledge you as my rival, Soren.
That said, it wasn’t perfect.
There were a few flaws, so I’ll give it a 9 as well."
"..." Soren started back at Lucent and nodded with a smile.
The next moment, the average of the finalists was calculated and added to the judges’ points.
Soren’s current score shot up to 63.3 points on the main screen.
"Since the lucky judges are still on the way, let’s continue with the next contestant," Faris announced.
"Chef Damir, please take the stage."
Damir nodded, swapped places with Soren, and presented his own dish.
It was really a soup, as Soren had guessed earlier.
According to Damir, this was also the first meal he had ever created.
It had been a task given by his master before he could even begin learning how to make magic meals.
He mentioned he prepared this because it was the first time his master had ever praised him back then.
Judges tasted his dish and gave their scores.
It came close to Soren’s result, but in the end, it fell one point short of his total.
Soren tasted it himself and gave it a 9 since he noticed a flaw this time.
Nuelia and Lucent, however, ended up giving 8 points.
As a result, Damir’s score ended up at 61.3 points, just two points below Soren’s.
Next came Nuelia’s turn.
She stepped forward hesitantly and couldn’t speak for a moment.
Only after she saw a certain someone nodding at her with an encouraging smile did she calm down and speak.
"This... this is my first time cooking like this," she admitted, her gaze sincere.
"I know I made mistakes, but I tried my best.
Please judge me fairly and give me your honest opinions.
I want to learn from this."
The judges nodded and started eating.
Some stopped after taking a few bites, while some finished everything.
"This is amazing for your first try." One of the judges praised.
"However, you still have a lot to improve.
I recommend practicing how to control the fire first.
But the rest is good."
They gave her a 7.
Other judges followed up with their honest opinions and gave similar scores, but none of them gave more than 7.
"I saw how hard you worked," Soren said as his turn came.
"And I am sure you will master it pretty soon if you keep practicing.
It’s an 8 from me."
"I understand this was your first time," Damir followed, "but I’m sorry; your mistakes were too obvious to ignore.
So I’ll give 6 too."
"..." Lucent stared at Nuelia and chuckled mockingly.
"I guess what Sister Monie told me about you elves was true.
You’re an arrogant race who rely on your innate talents and long lifespans to feel superior.
But strip those away, and you’re useless.
Take away your magic and your centuries of privilege, and you can’t even do something as simple as cooking a proper meal.
I now understand how difficult it must have been for her...
Anyway, don’t expect any mercy from me!"
He laughed coldly and raised his score.
It was...
"I added an extra 2 points since you actually kept trying even after failing, and didn’t fear facing the judgment head-on.
So I guess you’re somewhat better than the rest of your kind."

chapters.title: Chapter 291: Golden Ladle Championship: Finale [7]
paragraphs: "!" Nuelia stared at Lucent, her expression full of shock.

Her total score ended up at 42.6 points. Even if she received perfect scores from the lucky judges later, it would be impossible for her to win. However, Soren could tell she was shocked for a different reason. ’It must be related to the Sister Monie he mentioned just now. And perhaps that’s another reason why they kidnapped her and not me or Damir...’
He kept his theory to himself and watched as Lucent’s turn came. ’Let’s see if he is really as good as he seems to be...’
Tap... Tap...

Lucent ascended to the stage and started his presentation speech. "I’m happy to be able to participate in such a grand tournament, and I’m grateful for this opportunity. But I have to ask... why is there no competition for normal chefs like me?" He paused, letting the question reach everyone. "This festival is meant to be a celebration for everyone in the empire, isn’t it? A time when all citizens, regardless of their background, come together to enjoy themselves. So why, then, are the events only open to the awakened? Does that mean the rest of us are only meant to watch from the sidelines? Are we being excluded simply because we were born without power?"
The arena felt deathly silent at his bold words. Even the judges seemed taken aback.

"I... I love cooking," Lucent continued. "I have spent years honing my craft, just like any other chef here. But when I tried to enter this competition, they turned me away. Not because my food was bad, not because I lacked skill, but simply because I was born without mana." He shook his head, his voice tightening with emotion. "And yet, are we not part of this empire too? Do we not share in its traditions, its culture, its joy? A festival that claims to unite its people should not be drawing lines between them."

He looked directly at the cameras, as if making a world-shaking declaration. "So I stand here today, representing every normal chef who was told they weren’t good enough simply because of how they were born. And I will prove, through my food, that we belong here just as much as anyone else!"
"WHOOOO!"

After a second of silence, the arena erupted in thunderous applause. One after another, the guards and staff started cheering; some were visibly moved to tears. Surprisingly, even the judges were clapping with genuine emotion.

"Whoa! Look at that, dear viewers!" Faris laughed loudly. "It seems like we discovered the true chef we have been searching for so long! Look at their expressions! I wonder if they are all going to give a perfect score and repeat yesterday and set another record?

’...Isn’t he overdoing it a bit?’ Soren thought as he held the urge to shake his head at the possessor’s actions. ’However... To those who are unaware, this definitely makes a convincing performance.’
But for Soren, it looked like a puppet show where the puppeteer was clapping for his own performance.

’Well, at least Lucent is making a valid claim.’ He thought as he repeated Lucent’s words in his mind. Really... Why didn’t they have events for normal people? Weren’t they citizens of the Empire too? More importantly, hasn’t anyone talked about this before? Didn’t City Lord Asad consider it?
The questions were many, but answers were probably simple enough.

An ordinary cooking competition wouldn’t be as flashy or exciting as one involving magic. It wouldn’t draw the same attention, wouldn’t generate the same revenue. In a festival built around spectacle, events for the unawakened likely just weren’t seen as profitable. Or they didn’t have enough time or people to organize another big event at the same time.

Whatever the reason, though, it didn’t justify what Lucent and his group were doing. Making a valid point didn’t give them the right to put innocent people in danger, forcibly enter the competition, change its rules, or even rig it.

’...Let’s keep playing along for now.’ He muttered inwardly as he watched the judges eat and immediately start praising Lucent’s food. However, surprisingly, they didn’t go as far as to give him a perfect score. Well, not all of them. ’The possessor guy must have done it so his young master would feel as if he were really competing fairly.’
However, once he tasted it himself, he knew it was actually good and deserved all the praise and points he got, well, almost.

"Your skills are truly amazing," Soren said as he started his evaluation. "They are comparable to a four- or even a five-star restaurant chef’s. However, I wonder if you realize how wrong your actions were in getting to this point. And whether you regret any of it...
"...I don’t regret anything," Lucent responded smugly. "In fact, you should be grateful that I restrained myself."

"...I see." Soren squinted. "Then, I’ll be honest. Your dish was excellent, but.. I also detected three fatal flaws. So, I’ll give it a 7. If you’re interested in knowing what they are, I will tell you later once the competition ends."
"..." Lucent stopped smiling, his gaze turning sharp as he stared at Soren. "...Alright."
"I will give 7 too," Nuelia added quickly from the side, which earned a sneer from Lucent.
"...I..." Damir paused, as if hesitating to decide. "I... I will give it a 9."
The main screen lit up once again, and at the end, Lucent’s score shot up to 62.6 points, currently in second place.

’...He got one more point than me from the judges.’ Soren analyzed the situation. ’But the points he got from us were 1.7 points lower than mine. So now, he is in second place, 1.3 points above Damir and 0.7 points below me...’

He glanced at the broadcasting platform, curious to see what kind of expression fake Faris was making, but unfortunately was unable to. ’Then again, there are still lucky judges left. I guess they’re the trump cards to bring victory to their young master.’
It was now obvious why the random judges rule was added.
’He... had planned everything from the start. To create an ’unforgettable’ play...’

chapters.title: Chapter 292: A Friendly Handshake
paragraphs: "The final has reached its peak! With only a few points separating our top three contestants, everything now rests in the hands of our lucky judges! And guess what? They’re finally here!"
At Faris’s announcement, two people - a red-haired woman in her early thirties and an obese man with coily hair entered the arena, led by staff. They waved enthusiastically at the cameras.
’...’ Soren quickly scanned the newcomers. ’...I was right, huh.’
He then glanced at Lucent, shaking his head.
’Guys... Get ready to run away. Leave the arena as fast as you can. Blink and rub your eye if you heard me, or smile.’
Nuelia and Damir froze, but quickly did as he said to show they understood.

’...Lady Nuelia, please knock Damir out as soon as ’it’ starts. He’s already been taken over once earlier. So...’ He trailed off, knowing Nuelia would understand the rest without him needing to spell it out.
’...It’s time.’ Soren spoke as he stood up from his seat. ’Wait for my signal.’

Despite receiving no response, he continued forward, his movements calm and unhurried as he wore a friendly smile on his face. "Chef Lucent. I think no matter who wins this, I have to admit your passion for cooking is genuine. It takes courage to stand on this stage and say what you said without hesitation. So allow me to show my respect with a proper handshake."

"Oh," Lucent studied him for a moment, suspicion flickering in his eyes. Then, as if deciding it didn’t matter, he smiled and extended his hand. "I guess you are finally acknowledging me as your rival too?"

"...You could say that," Soren replied, and the instant their hands touched, his smile vanished. His grip tightened like a vice, and with a sharp twist, he wrenched Lucent’s arm behind his back and drove him to his knees in one swift motion. Before Lucent could even react, Soren’s free hand clamped around his throat, fingers pressing just hard enough to make breathing difficult.
"NOW!"
"YOUNG MASTER!"
The two hooded figures roared loudly and charged toward Soren.
"YOU BASTARD! LET GO!"
"...Come and get him," Soren said coldly, "if you can; that is.
"BASTARD!"
His words infuriated them even more, as they leaped into the air.
Swoosh!
’...Hooh.’ Soren let out a breath as his leg snapped out in a blur, catching the two possessed staff in the chest and sending them crashing into others behind.
At the same time, he noticed Nuelia knocking Damir out with a clean strike. However, he also saw the small group of possessed guards charging at them from behind.
’Behind you.’ He warned her and kicked away another possessed staff.

"!" Nuelia spun around just in time, raising her arms to defend. But before the guards could reach her, two armored figures crashed down from above like thunderbolts, landing between her and the attackers.

At the same time, three more figures descended with a deafening boom in front of Soren, their armor gleaming brightly under the sunlight. They formed a protective line around him, shields raised and weapons held at the ready.
The Hollow Pair were already airborne, streaking toward Soren with murder in their eyes.
"DIE! YOU BAST-!"
Their roars were cut short as a gray-armored knight dropped from the sky like a falling star, his sword swinging in a wide arc. The Hollow Pair met him with their daggers and gauntlets.
"CLANG-!"

The clash of weapons echoed through the arena, sending a visible shockwave rippling outward. The possessed staff and guards nearby staggered, their movements disrupted by the force. For a brief moment, the knight held his ground, his blade locked against theirs, muscles straining under the pressure.
Swoosh!

The combined momentum of the Hollow Pair was too much, and the knight was hurled backward. However, he managed to twist mid-air and landed in a low crouch, skidding across the floor before coming to a stop, his cold gaze still fixated on the pair.
Thud!
The pair landed a short distance away before charging forward once again with all their speed.
"Protect him."
The gray armored knight muttered as he shot forward like an arrow, his sword trailing behind him as he closed the distance in the blink of an eye.
"Understood, Commander Ervin!"
The three knights surrounding Soren shouted as they tightened their formation.
"Boom!"
"Clang! Clang! Clang!"

The gray knight, Commander Ervin, met the Hollow Pair head-on, his blade a blur of silver as it danced between the two. The massive one, the Nullifier, led with his gauntlets, each swing carrying enough force to crush a building. Commander Ervin deflected the blows at an angle, letting their momentum slide past him while his sword flicked out in rapid counters.

However, it was hard to deal any real damage since the other one, the Leech, kept moving like a phantom, daggers darting in whenever Commander Ervin showed an opening or was about to land a decisive blow.

’...He’ll be defeated if this goes on.’ Soren squinted as he analyzed their situation. He also assessed the enemies and compared them to himself to see whether his plan would really work. ’...They are definitely hiding their strength, but... I have a chance. I believe I can do it.’
However, he had to make sure Lucent wouldn’t get taken away first. He needed someone else who wouldn’t be controlled by the enemy to watch over Lucent.
"...Nuelia." He muttered as he looked over to the side. She was being guarded by two elven warriors, with one being Lariel himself. ’If it’s her, she should be able to handle it.’
Thanks to her spirit, her mind was protected from the possessor, making her one of the few here who couldn’t be turned against them.
Soren tightened his grip on Lucent’s collar and raised his voice. "We’re joining the elves!" he shouted to the knights around him. "Hold the line and clear a path!"
Without waiting for a response, he dragged Lucent with him as the knights moved to cover his flank. Within seconds, they arrived at Luelia’s side.
Soren shoved Lucent forward, forcing him to stumble to his knees in front of Nuelia while coughing violently.
"Watch over him," Soren said, his eyes already turning back toward the battle. "Don’t let him escape."
"W-What about you?!" Nuelia asked in confusion.
"I..." Soren muttered as he summoned his beloved spear, Nightfrost. "I am going to help Commander Ervin!"

chapters.title: Chapter 293: Don’t Make Me Laugh
paragraphs: "I am going to help Commander Ervin!"
Soren declared with confidence.
"Huh?" Nuelia’s eyes widened. "W-What are you saying?! Y-You can’t! They’re strong, and y-you can’t use... mana."
"Thanks for worrying, but I know what I’m doing." Soren smiled at her and turned to Lariel, who was now wearing fine elven armor. "I’ll leave it to you. Don’t screw it up this time."
"...I won’t," Lariel replied after a pause. "However, the same goes for you."
Soren chuckled and, with one Phantom Step, broke out of the formation, surprising everyone. "Be careful."
He said and sprinted toward the ongoing battle.

"..." Lariel watched him run for a moment before ordering. "Don’t follow him. Just keep the formation. Our job is to protect these three. And... be careful. Just knocking them out is enough. Don’t seriously hurt them."
"Understood!"
The knights and the other elf shouted back in response as they kept engaging in battle with the possessed guards.

’Even though they were 6th circle awakened, it doesn’t make sense that they can fight this well,’ Lariel thought as he observed. ’They are even being controlled... Unless the possessor has enormous combat experience, it should be impossible to make them fight like this.’

He gritted his teeth as he parried another strike. The enemy’s coordination was perfect; each body moved as if it belonged to a single mind, because in a way, it did. But that only raised more questions. Controlling one person at full combat capacity was already a feat in itself, so coordinating dozens at this level would require more than sheer force of control or ability; it would demand a terrifying degree of mastery.
’Just how powerful is this ’possessor’?’ Lariel’s mind raced as he ducked under a swing. ’And... Was he mocking us yesterday? In the interrogation room?’
The thought of it alone made his blood boil. But he could only hold it in.
’Once this is over, once we find him, I will make him pay!’

Soren’s eyes swept across the chaos as he approached the ongoing battle between the Hollow Pair and Imperial Knight Commander Ervin. They were locked in a fierce exchange, with Ervin leading it further from where Lucent was. However, he was at a serious disadvantage now, with Leech darting in and out of range while Nullifier kept forcing him to dodge, destroying the surroundings with his every strike.

’Leech’s aim is to exploit openings and drain the commander’s strength over time with Nullifier’s endless assault.’ Soren analyzed as he readied his spear. ’He is a good match against me since I have a spear. I will be able to keep him at a distance and prevent him from messing with the commander or me easily.’
With his decision made, Soren used Phantom Step again. Although it only worked at a fraction of its usual strength due to the anti-mana zone, it was still enough to close the distance in an instant.
Swoosh!
He surged forward, Nightfrost cutting through the air in a wide arc, aimed straight at Leech’s back.
"!" Leech noticed it at the last second and twisted away, but Soren pressed the attack with a follow-up chain of thrusts, finally forcing him to break off from Ervin.
"I’ll take this one!" Soren shouted at Ervin. "You focus on the big guy!"
"...Thank you!" Commander Ervin shouted back. "But be careful! He’s hiding his strength!"
"Un-!" Soren couldn’t finish his reply as Leech suddenly exploded forward, his daggers flashing toward Soren’s throat, his gaze full of killing intent. "DIE, BASTARD!"
"Urgh!" Soren barely brought Nightfrost up in time.
"CLANG!"

The clash of weapons sent a spray of sparks scattering through the air, the force of the impact rippling outward as they both locked in a brief, deadly stalemate. Soren’s feet sank into the broken floor beneath him, making him grit his teeth as the Leech’s full momentum pressed down on him.
"Idiot."

Soren muttered as he suddenly shifted his weight, stepping to the side with a fluid twist of his body. Leech’s forward momentum carried him past Soren, and in that same breath, Soren spun on his heel, reversing his grip on Nightfrost and swinging its butt in a vicious arc toward Leech’s exposed back.
"THUD-!"
The attack landed solidly, sending Leech stumbling forward.

Soren didn’t just stop there; with another Phantom Step, he closed the distance once more, Nightfrost thrusting toward Leech’s side. Leech twisted, his body blurring as he slipped past the spear’s tip while sending flying daggers at Soren. Soren dodged them effortlessly and kept pressing, each thrust and sweep forcing Leech to retreat.
Then, in a heartbeat, everything changed.

The Leech’s eyes gleamed with cold amusement as his daggers started to emit an eerie red glow. His body dropped low, and in the space between one breath and the next, he vanished from Soren’s line of sight.
Soren reacted on instinct, raising his arms to guard.
"SLASH-!"
"SLASH-!"

Two long gashes tore across his forearms before he even registered the movement, and the sheer force of the blow sent him hurtling backward. His feet skidded against the broken ground, leaving twin trails of dust as he fought to stop himself. Blood dripped from his arms, staining the floor beneath him.
The Leech straightened, twirling his daggers as the eerie light faded from their edges. A wicked grin spread across his face. "Consider it payback for daring to lay a hand on our young master."
The next moment, he blurred and appeared in front of Soren, his daggers already slicing toward his neck in a deadly scissor motion.

"..." Soren kept his expression calm, tilting his head just enough to let the blades whistle past his ears. But Leech kept pressing forward with a relentless barrage of slashes and stabs, each strike flowing into the next without pause.

Soren backpedaled, Nightfrost spinning in his hands as he deflected what he could. But the Leech’s speed and techniques were overwhelming, his daggers slipping past Soren’s guard again and again. Thin cuts opened across his shoulders, his ribs, his thighs. None were deep, but each one stung, and together they began to take their toll.
"Hahaha!" The Leech laughed, his voice filled with cruel delight. "What’s wrong? Can’t keep up?"
Swoosh-!
"Where did all your arrogance go?!"
Clang-!
"Did you seriously think you could fight me?"
"Urgh-!"
"You! A f*cking chef?!" The Leech snarled, his daggers crossing in a lethal arc. "Stop making me laugh and just die already!"

"Huh?" Nuelia’s eyes widened.
"W-What are you saying?!
Y-You can’t!
They’re strong, and y-you can’t use... mana."

Our job is to protect these three.

Just knocking them out is enough.
Don’t seriously hurt them."

Unless the possessor has enormous combat experience, it should be impossible to make them fight like this.’

The enemy’s coordination was perfect; each body moved as if it belonged to a single mind, because in a way, it did.
