’Just how powerful is this ’possessor’?’ Lariel’s mind raced as he ducked under a swing. ’And...
Was he mocking us yesterday?
In the interrogation room?’
The thought of it alone made his blood boil.
But he could only hold it in.
’Once this is over, once we find him, I will make him pay!’

They were locked in a fierce exchange, with Ervin leading it further from where Lucent was.

chapters.title: Chapter 294: Bring It On!
paragraphs: "Just die already!"
Leech lunged, his daggers inches away from Soren’s vitals.
"Haha-!"

Leech’s laughter stopped abruptly, his wicked smile vanishing as Soren’s hands shot up and caught both of his wrists mid-strike. His eyes went wide, disbelief flashing across his face as he tried to push forward. But no matter how hard he tried, he couldn’t move them at all. In fact, the daggers were slowly being forced away from Soren.
"Honestly..." Soren muttered, staring dead in the Leech’s eyes. "I’m disappointed."
He tightened his grip.
"URGH!"
The Leech groaned in pain, his muscles straining as he tried to pull free.
"I thought you were strong."

The words struck deeper than any blade. The Leech’s face contorted with rage and humiliation, his teeth grinding so hard it seemed they might crack. "You... You bastard!" he snarled, thrashing wildly. "Don’t look down on me!"

In a desperate burst of fury, he kicked upward, putting all his strength into his legs as he drove them both straight into Soren’s abdomen. The sound of impact echoed in the surroundings, however... Soren didn’t budge an inch, his expression devoid of any pain or discomfort. The kick might as well have been a child’s tantrum.
’Is he using mana too?’ Leech’s mind raced as he tried to find an explanation for his absurd situation. ’One way to find out then!’
Without hesitation, he activated Mana Drain at full power. ’!’
"You!" His eyes widened as he sensed mana being pulled from Soren’s body into his own. "How do you ha-argh!"
"You really disappointed me..." Soren muttered as he tightened his grip even further.
"YOU BA-AAARGHH!"

The Leech screamed, the bones in his wrists creaking under the pressure. His fingers spasmed open, and his daggers clattered uselessly to the ground. Without another word, Soren hoisted him high into the air and then slammed him down with terrifying force.
"BOOOOM-!"
The ground cracked beneath the impact, dust and debris exploding outward as the Leech’s body cratered into the floor.
"GA-!" Leech let out a choked gasp, his body convulsing from the shock, but Soren didn’t release his wrists. Instead, he lifted Leech again and brought him crashing down on the other side.
"BOOOM-!"
Then again.
"BOOOM-!"
And again.
"BOOOM-!"

Each slam sent tremors through the ground, the Leech’s body flailing like a ragdoll in Soren’s grasp. Blood sprayed from his mouth, his screams reduced to broken gasps as the relentless assault continued, the sound of his body hammering against the shattered floor echoing through the arena.
It seemed like the possessor had finally noticed his ally’s dire situation, because a dozen possessed guards suddenly broke away from their positions and charged toward Soren.

However, Soren wasn’t worried in the slightest. He just swung Leech’s body in a wide arc, using him as a makeshift weapon. The first guard took a direct hit to the chest from Leech’s head and was sent flying, while the next got slapped by Leech’s flailing hands and crashed into two more coming behind him.
"Hey, I know you’re listening," Soren spoke up as he kept swinging Leech around. "If you wanna save your young master, return the princess at once. Or else..."
A moment passed, and the last attacking guard suddenly stopped, life returning to his eyes. "...Or else what?" he asked with a sneer. "You’re gonna kill him?"
Soren shook his head. "No."
"Then why-"

"But they can." Soren cut him off, pointing at Commander Ervin. "Unless you return her and pay enough compensation for all the damage you’ve caused... the Empire will hunt you down to the ends of Etenia. You should know that better than anyone else."
"..." The knight went silent for a moment.
Soren smiled faintly and slammed Leech once more, right in front of the possessor’s ’eyes’.
"What are you even thinking about so much? You don’t have much of a choice here."
"I..." The possessor spoke, looking up, his smile twisting. "I am thinking of how to torture your wife~"
"..." Soren stared at the possessed guard, his expression turning cold. "...Is that so?"
"Mhm~" The possessor’s grin widened, his voice dripping with mockery. "I wonder how long she’ll last. She’s got such a-urgh!
A slap landed on the guard’s face and knocked him to the floor.

"You talk too much." Soren lowered himself and sat on his knees, looking coldly at the possessor. "But since you’re so confident, let me make this clear. There’s no getting out of this for you now. I’ll find you myself and... I’ll make sure you regret every word you said."

The possessor’s twisted smile flickered on the guard’s lips, as if he was about to respond, but Soren didn’t give him the chance. The next moment, the guard’s eyes rolled back, his body going limp as he fell unconscious.

"Then let me make things clear to you too." A voice echoed from not too far away. It was the possessor speaking through another guard. "You are gravely mistaken if you think you can really defeat us. Especially me~"
The guard then looked in Commander Ervin and Nullifier’s direction and shouted at the top of his lungs. "Raven! You can go all out now! And release the Leech too!"
"..." Soren squinted as he glanced at the limp Leech at his feet and the Nullifier, who suddenly stopped attacking. ’...Is there a second phase to this? Really?’
The thought almost made him laugh.
It was like something straight out of the stories and games he grew up with, where the villain would dramatically power up right when things looked bad.
’I guess they weren’t so far from the truth after all.’
’Not that I mind it.’ His smile widened as he looked back at the possessor. ’I was hoping for a real fight anyway.’
He met the possessor’s confused gaze head-on and gestured with his finger. "Bring it on."
"...You," the possessor muttered before grinning even wider than before. "You are crazy! And I like it! Haha!"
"ARRRRRGH!!!
Soren watched as the Nullifier suddenly let out a thunderous roar and drove his fist into the ground.
"BOOOM-!"

The floor detonated on impact, cracks exploding outward like a web of lightning as shattered stone shot into the air. The shockwave ripped through the arena in an instant, tearing up everything in its path and throwing a thick cloud of dust and debris across the battlefield.
Through the chaos, the possessor’s voice rang out, laced with amusement.
"This is going to be so much fun~!"

chapters.title: Chapter 295: Cockroach
paragraphs: ’Finally going all out?’ Soren thought to himself as Leech started to move again, a reddish aura surrounding his body. ’As if I’d watch you recover!’

Soren stepped forward and drove his foot toward Leech’s abdomen. However, they passed through nothing but air. Leech had already disappeared, leaving behind only an afterimage that flickered once before vanishing.
’Wait...’ Soren narrowed his eyes as his senses stretched to the limit. ’Mana is back.’
He realized. However, it was only in a small radius surrounding him and Leech.

’Etheawasright. Nullifier can really control his constitution to some extent now. That only means...’ He trailed off as he scanned his surroundings. There was no trace of Leech, as if he had vanished into thin air. However, Soren knew he was here, waiting for the perfect moment to strike while recovering from his injuries. ’...I guess I really made the right choice in choosing him.’

He closed his eyes and took a deep breath, letting his senses expand outward. At the same time, he reached deep within himself, drawing on his mental power until it spread through the air like an invisible web.
’...Don’t force it... Feel it...’

Gradually, the world around him dimmed. It all went silent. In that silence, Soren reached deeper, past the noise, past the chaos, until all that remained was the faint pulse of the world itself. It was then that he finally felt it.
’There.’

A faint ripple stirred behind him before shifting quickly, circling to his left and vanishing, only to reappear a heartbeat later from another angle. The Leech was obviously probing him, testing his perception, and waiting for the right moment.
’...Let’s give him that then.’
Soren turned his head slightly to the right, as if he had misread the Leech’s position.

The air behind him tore apart. Leech shot forward like a crimson blur, his daggers aimed directly at Soren’s exposed neck. But Soren was already moving, his body twisting just enough to let the first blade whistle past his ear. The second dagger followed in a vicious arc, sliding across his shoulder, leaving a thin line of red in its wake.
Soren didn’t react to the cut and kept his composure.

The Leech didn’t stop. He came again and again, his body a streak of red shadow as he attacked from every angle: left, right, above, below. Each strike flowed into the next without pause, the daggers carving through the air in relentless patterns.
Swooosh-!
Clang-!
Swoosh-!

To any onlooker, it would have looked like Soren was being swarmed by a dozen attackers at once. Leech moved so fast that his form never fully solidified, his body flickering in and out of view like a flame caught in a storm.

Soren’s body was a mess of wounds, covered in cuts from head to toe. His clothes hung in tatters, soaked through with blood. Short and long gashes lined his arms, his legs, his chest, his back, even his face. He looked like he had been dragged through a storm of blades, and yet he remained standing, as if the pain belonged to someone else entirely.

"Fu*k!" Leech’s frustration boiled over. Almost every swing carried enough power to slice a fuc*king dragon, and he had landed more hits than he could count. By all logic, this bast*rd should have been reduced to chunks of meat by now. So why was he still alive? Why was he still standing?!
"Why won’t you just fu*cking die?!"
Leech cursed as he unleashed another barrage.
"DIE! DIE! DIE!"

His movements became wilder with each passing second, fueled by rage, each strike aimed to kill, to maim, to bring this bast*rd down once and for all. But no matter how many times the blades bit into flesh, the wounds sealed shut behind them almost instantly. As if it wasn’t enough, the bastard’s skin would glow silver and send a sharp jolt of force back through his arms, numbing his fingers with every impact.

’Damn it! Does he have some kind of abnormal physique too?’ Leech gritted his teeth, his breathing growing ragged. And it wasn’t just the healing or the damage reflection. Every time he thought he had landed a killing blow, this bastard would shift at the last second, turning what should have been a sure kill into a shallow cut. And even the hits that did land felt off most of the time, as if the force behind them was being drained away before it could do real damage. ’But... ’it’ should start soon.’

A faint smirk tugged at the corner of his lips as he adjusted his grip. He had been doing more than just attacking. Every cut, every graze, every drop of spilled blood had been part of a larger backup plan. He had been channeling various manas into the bastard’s body with each contact, and soon they would tear him apart from the inside out.
’There is no way he can survive now... All I need is a little more time.’
He laughed louder, and time passed.
’...Wait.’ Leech’s smile slowly faded. ’...Why isn’t it working?!’
He had used more than five different people’s mana. The bastard should have exploded by now!
"Urgh!" He cursed as he delivered another strike. ’Aeshvin! Lend a hand, will you!’
’...You can’t defeat him?’ A moment later, a mocking voice echoed in his mind. ’This weak cook...?’

’Urgh! It’s not time for this!’ Leech retorted. ’He’s abnormal! I can’t land a killing blow on him, and his regeneration speed is off the charts! His body is f*cking tough too! He must have an S-rank or even higher constitution. There’s no other explanation!’
’I see...’ The voice trailed off. ’Actually, he has high mental defense too. I couldn’t get into his mind yesterday or a little earlier. So I won’t be much of a help to you.’
’Then what should I do?!’ Leech roared furiously. ’My mana is gonna run out soon, and I will be at his mercy!’
’...Why don’t you just switch then?’ The voice suggested. ’If he is so confident in his constitution, let him face Raven instead.’

’...’ Leech went silent. Because doing that would be acknowledging he couldn’t defeat a f*cking 4th circle chef! But... He couldn’t keep this up for long. His body had yet to recover; his arms were growing numb from the repeated force of his own attacks reflecting back at him, and his backup plan had failed. Every second he spent here was a second wasted. And yet, the humiliation of it burned hotter than any of his wounds. ’...Damn it.’
"Raven!"

Soren turned his head slightly to the right, as if he had misread the Leech’s position.
The air behind him tore apart.
Leech shot forward like a crimson blur, his daggers aimed directly at Soren’s exposed neck.
But Soren was already moving, his body twisting just enough to let the first blade whistle past his ear.
The second dagger followed in a vicious arc, sliding across his shoulder, leaving a thin line of red in its wake.
Soren didn’t react to the cut and kept his composure.
The Leech didn’t stop.
He came again and again, his body a streak of red shadow as he attacked from every angle: left, right, above, below.
Each strike flowed into the next without pause, the daggers carving through the air in relentless patterns.
Swooosh-!
Clang-!
Swoosh-!
To any onlooker, it would have looked like Soren was being swarmed by a dozen attackers at once.
Leech moved so fast that his form never fully solidified, his body flickering in and out of view like a flame caught in a storm.
Soren’s body was a mess of wounds, covered in cuts from head to toe.
His clothes hung in tatters, soaked through with blood.
Short and long gashes lined his arms, his legs, his chest, his back, even his face.
He looked like he had been dragged through a storm of blades, and yet he remained standing, as if the pain belonged to someone else entirely.
"Fu*k!" Leech’s frustration boiled over.
Almost every swing carried enough power to slice a fuc*king dragon, and he had landed more hits than he could count.
By all logic, this bast*rd should have been reduced to chunks of meat by now.
So why was he still alive?
Why was he still standing?!
"Why won’t you just fu*cking die?!"
Leech cursed as he unleashed another barrage.
"DIE!
DIE!
DIE!"
His movements became wilder with each passing second, fueled by rage, each strike aimed to kill, to maim, to bring this bast*rd down once and for all.
But no matter how many times the blades bit into flesh, the wounds sealed shut behind them almost instantly.
As if it wasn’t enough, the bastard’s skin would glow silver and send a sharp jolt of force back through his arms, numbing his fingers with every impact.
’Damn it!
Does he have some kind of abnormal physique too?’ Leech gritted his teeth, his breathing growing ragged.
And it wasn’t just the healing or the damage reflection.
Every time he thought he had landed a killing blow, this bastard would shift at the last second, turning what should have been a sure kill into a shallow cut.
And even the hits that did land felt off most of the time, as if the force behind them was being drained away before it could do real damage. ’But... ’it’ should start soon.’
A faint smirk tugged at the corner of his lips as he adjusted his grip.
He had been doing more than just attacking.
Every cut, every graze, every drop of spilled blood had been part of a larger backup plan.
He had been channeling various manas into the bastard’s body with each contact, and soon they would tear him apart from the inside out.
’There is no way he can survive now...
All I need is a little more time.’
He laughed louder, and time passed.
’...Wait.’ Leech’s smile slowly faded. ’...Why isn’t it working?!’
He had used more than five different people’s mana.
The bastard should have exploded by now!
"Urgh!" He cursed as he delivered another strike. ’Aeshvin!
Lend a hand, will you!’
’...You can’t defeat him?’ A moment later, a mocking voice echoed in his mind. ’This weak cook...?’
’Urgh!
It’s not time for this!’ Leech retorted. ’He’s abnormal!
I can’t land a killing blow on him, and his regeneration speed is off the charts!
His body is f*cking tough too!
He must have an S-rank or even higher constitution.
There’s no other explanation!’
’I see...’ The voice trailed off. ’Actually, he has high mental defense too.
I couldn’t get into his mind yesterday or a little earlier.
So I won’t be much of a help to you.’
’Then what should I do?!’ Leech roared furiously. ’My mana is gonna run out soon, and I will be at his mercy!’
’...Why don’t you just switch then?’ The voice suggested. ’If he is so confident in his constitution, let him face Raven instead.’
’...’ Leech went silent.
Because doing that would be acknowledging he couldn’t defeat a f*cking 4th circle chef!
But...
He couldn’t keep this up for long.
His body had yet to recover; his arms were growing numb from the repeated force of his own attacks reflecting back at him, and his backup plan had failed.
Every second he spent here was a second wasted.
And yet, the humiliation of it burned hotter than any of his wounds. ’...Damn it.’
"Raven!"

chapters.title: Chapter 296: Real Strength
paragraphs: ’...He’s slowed down a little.’ Soren thought as he dodged Leech’s next deadly strike. ’Or... I have already adapted to it...’
He wanted to believe it was the latter, but he had a good idea of why Leech was slowing down. ’He must have noticed that his plan failed and is thinking of another plan.’

Honestly, if it hadn’t been for Core Purge and Hyper Regeneration, he would have been dead many times over by now. The foreign mana Leech had injected him with was chaotic and incompatible, rampaging through his system and nearly shredding his mana pathways from within.

Leech was truly a nightmare of an opponent, and Sore could admit that without shame. Because against anyone else, it would have been a death sentence. It was just unfortunate for Leech that he was anything but ordinary.

In fact, he was benefiting from it in a way even he hadn’t expected. The chaotic mana, once neutralized by Core Purge, had left behind some amount of pure energy that his core greedily absorbed with each passing second. In a way, what should have been a killing blow ended up becoming fuel for his growth.
Still, he couldn’t afford to get complacent now.
’...Perhaps he is communicating with his allies, considering how he stopped cursing.’ Soren guessed again. ’In that case, should I start our plan too?’
Before he could decide, the Leech let out a frustrated roar that echoed across the arena.
"Raven! Switch!"
The next moment, Soren’s vision went dark. He only managed to see a crimson blur shot in the opposite direction before the light returned.

His first instinct was to give chase, but he forced himself to stop. He had the strength and durability to outlast the Leech, but catching a 6th circle Awakened who specialized in agility was another matter entirely.
Besides, he had already gotten what he wanted from him. So chasing him now would only waste energy and put him in a worse position.
’Let’s recover some mana instead,’ he muttered inwardly and took out a few potions and gulped them down in quick succession.

’Be careful.’ Just then, a familiar voice echoed in his mind. ’In fact, it’s better if you stop now. Nullifier’s strength is on a completely different level. Even I am unable to hold him back. All I am doing is just dodging. And... He’s yet to use his full power. I am sure of it.’
’...Thank you for the warning, Commander Ervin.’ Soren replied. ’Leech is dangerous too. If you can, don’t let him touch you.’
’Understood.’
Commander Ervin replied in that indifferent tone and cut off the connection.
’...Malakor, let’s put an end to this.’
A moment later, a calm voice answered in his mind. ’...Master, can you buy me a minute or two?’

Soren stared ahead, his gaze locking onto the monstrous figure barreling toward him. Every step sent tremors rippling through the broken ground, fissures spreading outward like the earth itself was buckling under the pressure.
’...I’ll try my best.’
’...’ Aeshvin watched the chaotic arena with an indifferent gaze through Faris. ’Hmm...’
Eventually, his gaze landed on two figures exchanging blows. They were none other than Raven and Soren.

However, since this wasn’t his own body, it was difficult for Aeshvin to keep track of every movement. He could only catch glimpses of their battle through the swirling dust, the constant thunder of impacts shaking the arena like a drum. Then, for a brief moment, the two figures broke apart, only to collide again with enough force to send shockwaves rippling through the air. Dust and debris churned around them as the ground shattered beneath their feet.
’...Synchronization.’
Curiosity winning him over, Aeshvin ended up using a secret technique, and the next moment, the world sharpened before his eyes.
’This is much better...’
He could finally see everything now. And what he saw made him pause.
"BOOOM-!"
The two clashed like opposing storms.

Raven’s fists came down like meteors, each strike shattering the ground where Soren had stood a heartbeat before. Soren used his smaller frame to slip through the gaps between attacks, twisting and weaving with an almost unnatural precision.

He fought back whenever he could, delivering a quick jab to the ribs, a hook to the jaw, each blow landing with a crack that echoed through the arena. But Raven seemed to absorb them without flinching, his massive body pressing forward regardless.
’Soren... heisreally strong.’
He could fight against a 6th circle Assassin like Orvane and not die, and even force him to retreat. Heck, he could even fight an anomaly like Raven and hold his ground without being overwhelmed.
’But... strength like that only takes you so far.’

Aeshvin had seen it countless times before. Fighters who could shatter mountains but crumbled the moment their minds were tested. Soren was tough, sure. But toughness of the body meant nothing if the spirit broke first. And he had already brushed against Soren’s spirit once. It wasn’t as solid as the young chef liked to think.
’You’re strong, little chef. But the mind is a game you certainly don’t know how to play.’

His lips curled up as he imagined what expression Soren would make once he found out what was waiting for him beyond the arena. The shock, the despair, the helplessness... It would be a sight worth savoring.
With that pleasant thought lingering, he released the connection. The world blurred, and when he opened his eyes again, he was in front of a door.
He took a step and knocked on it a few times.
"...Who is it?"
A familiar female voice echoed from the inside.
’...Hehe, I finally found you.’ Aeshvin laughed inwardly while composing himself. He leaned slightly toward the door, letting just the right amount of familiarity seep into his voice.
"...It’s me, junior."
"...Princess?" The voice replied, laced with suspicion.

"...Yes." Aeshvin lowered his voice, making it tremble just slightly. "I have been saved thanks to Commander Ervin and your husband’s efforts. However, the enemy launched a surprise attack, and the situation is extremely dire right now. Lord Asad teleported me here to stay and protect you."
"...Why should I trust you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 297: It’s Over
paragraphs: "...Why should I trust you?"
’Oh, this is definitely her!’

"I understand your suspicion," Aeshvin replied. "After everything that’s happened, I would be careful too. No, in fact, it’s my fault since I couldn’t prevent this." He let out a shaky breath. "But your husband... he told me to tell you that he’s sorry for making you worry. And that he’ll come for you as soon as the battle is over."
"And... I’m sorry for saying those things about him before..."
"...Alright." The voice replied. "I’ll open the door now."
’...She’s gotten soft.’ Aeshvin sighed in disappointment inwardly. ’Love really does make people fools. To lower her guard so easily... how pitiful.’
But he wasn’t about to complain. If she wanted to hand herself over on a silver platter, who was he to refuse?
"Thank you." He said in a happy tone, with amusement dancing behind his eyes.
"...Hiss."
A moment later, the reinforced door slid open and the shimmering barrier around it faded away.
"I am coming in." Aeshvin stepped inside, his borrowed face arranged into a mask of concern.
Then he let his gaze sweep the room and spotted a woman seated alone in a wheelchair, her posture tense yet composed. And just in case, he used Synchronization again and probed the room.
’Hmm... There’s really no one else aside from us. Hehe. Hehe.’
He barely managed to stop himself from laughing out loud. He didn’t know whether it was truly because of love or her current condition. But to think she would be this stupid...

"...I see that you’re in good shape, Your Highness." The woman spoke, gesturing for him to take a seat. "They really must have been afraid of the Imperial Family’s retaliation to let you go unharmed like this.
"Mmm..." Aeshvin nodded as he walked over to the sofa beside the woman. "Actually, the real reason they let me go was to save their young master. They traded me with him."
"I see..." The woman muttered. "If they rescued their young master, why are they still fighting? Shouldn’t they have run away?"

"Well, from what I saw," Aeshvin replied in the body owner’s style, "our people stopped them. The whole arena was sealed, so they couldn’t use teleportation again." He then clenched his slender fists. "I wanted to fight too, but... I didn’t have any mana left, and Commander Ervin refused to let me stay. He said staying out of danger was the best thing I could do right now. Then City Lord escorted me away from the arena and had me teleport here."

Aeshvin slowly stood up, taking gentle steps toward the woman. Once he got near her, he knelt down in front of her and looked up. "I... I’m sorry, junior... This is happening because of me... The city, the people... your husband is in danger because I couldn’t foresee any of this. If I had just been stronger... smarter... maybe none of this would have happened."

He lowered his head, his shoulders trembling just enough to sell the act. "I know... that an apology isn’t enough. But I promise!" He raised his head, tears welling in his borrowed eyes. "I’ll do whatever it takes to make things right."
He reached out slowly, his fingers trembling as they moved toward her hands.
"Don’t touch me."
"!" Aeshvin ’froze’, his hand stopping mid-air. He looked up and found the woman staring down at him, her ice-blue eyes filled with nothing but disgust.

"...R-Right, I’m sorry." Aeshvin apologized, pretending to be startled and hurt by her reaction. He lowered his hand and let his shoulders slump, as if her rejection had struck something fragile inside him.
"Cut the act." The woman spoke. "I know it’s you."

"...Oh." Aeshvin’s expression shifted, the trembling act melting away in an instant. An amused smile spread across his lips. "You should have said that from the beginning! I really thought you’d actually gotten dumber for a moment there, you know."
"..." The woman stayed silent; however, her piercing gaze remained fixed on Aeshvin.
"Umm... Can you stop staring, please? You are making me feel a little nervous." He tilted his head, his smile still in place. "Or... is this your way of saying you missed me?"
"..." No response.
"...Sigh, alright, alright, I’ll stop it." Aeshvin raised both hands in mock surrender. Then, without warning, his hand shot forward, fingers aimed at her throat.
CLANG!
A golden barrier flared to life between them, stopping his strike inches from her skin.
"...Oh?" Aeshvin’s eyes widened for a split second before narrowing with interest. "Oh, is this why you let me in so easily?"
"...I advise you to surrender." The woman’s voice was indifferent. "It’s over. You’ve already lost... in your own game."
"Hmm? I lost?" Aeshvin tilted his head. "Now I’m really starting to think you became an idiot."
He reached into his dress and drew a dagger. Its blade was pure white, almost glowing, and the hilt was decorated with intricate engravings that screamed luxury.
"Do you really think your little artifact can withstand her?" he asked, his smile never faltering. Then he moved.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!

A flurry of strikes rained down on the barrier in the span of a single breath. Each hit was precise, aimed at the same spot with deadly accuracy. But the golden light held firm, flaring brightly with every impact and repelling the blade without so much as a crack.
Aeshvin stepped back, his expression unchanging.
"...I guess you were right. This thing is sturdier than I thought. But..." His smile widened as he suddenly raised the dagger to his own throat. "Can it protect her? Your precious Senior Sister?"
"!" The woman’s eyes widened before returning to their indifferent state. "...You can’t do it."
"...Tsk." Aeshvin lowered the dagger. "I guess you haven’t changed."

He let out a sigh and dropped onto the floor, sitting cross-legged like a scolded child. He tapped his temple lazily with the tip of the dagger. "Sigh... Did I really lose? All that planning, all those pawns... gone to waste?"
For a moment, he looked genuinely bored. Then his eyes widened, and a slow grin crept back onto his face. He snapped his fingers.
"Hey! Do you wanna see something interesting?"

chapters.title: Chapter 298: It’s Over [2]
paragraphs: "Do you wanna see something interesting?"
"..." Ethea kept staring at Princess Roya, or more precisely, at the Puppeteer who was controlling her body.

The next moment, the surroundings started blurring, and in just a few seconds, Ethea found herself looking at the arena, as if she were standing in the middle of it. Sounds of battles reached her ears: clash of weapons, desperate shouts, explosions, and the ground cracking apart.
The arena had truly become a battlefield.
"Let’s zoom in a little," Puppeteer said as he flicked his finger again.
The view shifted, the scene rushing forward until it focused on two figures near the center of the chaos. Soren and Raven, the Nullifier.
"!" Ethea’s breath caught in her throat.

Soren was a mess. Blood covered him from head to toe, his clothes torn and hanging in shreds. His face was swollen, bruised, and barely recognizable. The Nullifier’s fists rained down on him without pause, each blow heavy enough to crack the ground beneath them. Soren could only raise his arms to shield himself, his body buckling under the relentless assault.

"I guess your husband overestimated himself." Puppeteer’s voice dripped with mockery as he watched the scene unfold. "Look at him now. A few more punches from Raven, and he’s good as dead. Don’t worry, I told Raven not to kill him, at least not yet."

"..." Ethea clenched her fists, her heart beating faster. She wanted to deny it, to call it an illusion or some kind of mental trick. But through the bond between her and Soren, she could feel it, that it was real...

"Still think you’ve won?" Puppeteer asked, tilting his head. "Your husband’s life is in my hands. And do you know why? Yeah, it’s because of you! If you had warned him or stopped him from messing with us, perhaps I would have spared you both. But no, you had to meddle in things that didn’t concern you."
"Everything that happens to him from now on... is your fault," Puppeteer whispered in an accusatory tone. "Remember that as you watch."
Ethea bit her lip as Raven suddenly hit Soren and sent him flying.
’...No. He said he had a plan.’ She recalled what he said and promised. ’I have to trust him...’
Ethea steeled her heart and forced herself to keep watching.
Swoosh-!

Raven stomped forward, his massive frame casting a shadow over Soren’s crumpled form. He raised his fist for another strike, the air distorting from sheer force, and brought it down like a hammer to end it all.
Thwack-!
Soren’s hand shot up and caught it.
Swoosh-!
The impact sent a shockwave rippling outward, dust exploding around them, but Soren’s arm didn’t buckle or break. His fingers wrapped around Raven’s fist and held it in place.
Raven’s eye widened in surprise. After all, he poured all his strength into that strike.

"...This is quite a twist." Puppeteer also voiced his surprise, though his smile thinned slightly, and his fingers tapped once against his knee. For a brief moment, something flickered in his gaze, but he quickly masked it away. "But I guess it’s just a dying man’s last struggle."
’No...’ Ethea squinted as she remembered something. ’This must be the Limit Break ability he told me about before!’
That was the only explanation for the sudden increase in his strength.
But... She was certain it had side effects and a time limit. Unless he finished his opponent in the next few minutes, his body would give out on its own.
’...Dear.’
She whispered in her heart as she continued to watch.

Meanwhile, Soren’s cold gaze remained locked on Raven. Without a word, he tightened his grip on the massive fist, his fingers digging in until the bones beneath shifted. Raven tried to pull back, but Soren’s hold didn’t loosen.
"Grr..." Growing irritated, Raven punched Soren with his other fist.
Thwack-!
The blow caught Soren square in the jaw, snapping his head to the side. Blood dripped from his split lip as he turned back.
"Tfu." He spat a mouthful of blood onto the ground and muttered, "My... turn."
Swoosh-!

Soren’s free hand shot forward, knuckles driving into Raven’s face and whipping his head sideways. Blood exploded from his nose, the bone cracking under Soren’s fist, and Raven let out a strangled grunt as his face twisted in pain. Soren didn’t stop there; he twisted Raven’s arm and yanked him forward, driving his knee into his ribs.
The crack echoed through the arena.

Raven staggered back, his breathing coming in ragged gasps. Soren didn’t give him room to breathe. Stepping close, he grabbed the back of Raven’s head with both hands and pulled him down while driving his knee up.
THWACK-!
The collision was brutal, Raven’s head snapping back from the impact, blood and spit flying from his mouth as his body reeled.
Soren followed up with a horizontal elbow that connected with a heavy thud. The big man’s eyes rolled back, his large frame swaying for a long second before he crashed face-first into the ground.

Deathly silence settled over the arena as the dust slowly began to clear. Everyone froze, their eyes fixated on Soren, who stood in the center of the destruction like an unshaken pillar. Blood streaked his body, and his clothes hung in tatters, but his posture remained upright, his breathing steady, as if the brutal exchange had been nothing more than a warm-up. The sight of him standing over monstrous Raven’s fallen body sent a chill through every witness.

Then Soren’s head turned slowly, his gaze sweeping across the battlefield until it landed on the Leech. The assassin, who had been locked in fierce combat with Commander Ervin just moments before, went completely still. It was exactly like the stillness of prey that had just realized it was being hunted.

Leech’s eyes widened, his body tensing, and his instincts screaming at him to move, but for a single heartbeat, he couldn’t. Those cold eyes held him in place, and in that moment, it felt like death itself was staring down at him.
’Gulp.’ He swallowed hard, goosebumps across his skin as a cold shiver ran down his spine. ’W-Wait! Where did he go?!’

chapters.title: Chapter 299: It’s Over [3]
paragraphs: ’Where did he go?!’ Leech exclaimed as Soren disappeared from his vision. ’!’
’Not good!’
He instantly activated his movement technique on pure instinct, his body blurring to the side. But the moment he reappeared, Soren was already above him, fist cocked back.
Thwack!

The punch connected before Leech could even think to block, the impact folding him around Soren’s fist and launching him across the arena. He bounced twice on the broken floor before Soren appeared again, driving another blow into his skull mid-tumble. Leech’s body went limp instantly, skidding across the stone before coming to a stop in a heap.

Soren straightened, his gaze sweeping across the arena until it locked onto a lone figure standing at the edge of the battlefield. The figure stared back at him, frozen like a puppet whose strings had momentarily tangled.
"...I found... you..."
"...Sevihan."

The name barely left Soren’s mouth when the surroundings around them blurred, the arena bending and twisting like a reflection on disturbed water. And in just a heartbeat, the scene disappeared, and they were back in the room.
Aeshvin stood there, his borrowed face pale, his chest rising and falling as if he’d forgotten how to breathe. For the first time, his confident smirk was gone, replaced by a bizarre expression.
"I told you," Ethea said, her voice tinged with pride. "It’s over."
"..." Aeshvin didn’t respond this time.

"I also forgot to tell you something." She added, knowing he was listening despite pretending not to. "It wasn’t me who defeated you. It was my husband. And I guess..." Her lips curled up as she realized something. "...Sevihan is your true name?"
"!" Aeshvin’s body jerked, his head snapping toward her. His eyes burned with rage and madness, his shoulders shaking non-stop.
"D-Don’t...!" His voice cracked, no longer playful or amused. "Don’t you dare say that name!"
"Sevihan," Ethea repeated mockingly, meeting his gaze without a flinch. "Goodbye."
Then, her eyes began to glow, a brilliant silver light blooming from within. Countless tiny stars flickered in her irises, like a galaxy unfolding in her gaze.

"!" Aeshvin’s eyes widened. His lips parted, but no sound came out. Then his body went rigid, his expression freezing as the light swallowed him whole. A moment later, the possessed body went limp, the light fading from its eyes as consciousness slipped away.
Before it could hit the ground, the body stopped mid-air, hovering for a breath before drifting toward a nearby sofa and settling gently onto the cushions.
"Hmm..." Ethea let out a weary breath, her shoulders slumping as the glow in her eyes faded. "Hm.. Hm.."
She took quick breaths to steady herself. Despite the exhaustion, she looked at ease, as if a mountain had been lifted from her shoulders.
"Dear," She whispered with a gentle smile. "I will leave the rest to you..."
"Huff... Huff..."

Deep within an underground cave, far from the ruined arena, on the outskirts of Bagdad City, a cloaked figure collapsed onto the floor. His body hit the ground hard, and a mouthful of blood followed, splattering across the rocks as violent coughs wracked his frame. His chest heaved with every ragged breath, each inhale scraping against his throat.
"Damn it...!" His fist cracked against the stone, the impact splitting the surface beneath his knuckles. "How... how did she do that?!"

His voice came out hoarse, trembling with a mixture of pain and disbelief. The mental backlash had torn through him like a blade, severing his control and leaving his head pounding. He could still feel the echo of that silver light burning behind his eyes.

’Urgh...’ Gritting his teeth, he tried to reach out, to slip into one of his puppets above, but the moment he stretched his consciousness, a sharp spike of pain drove through his skull. He spat another mouthful of blood, his vision swimming as the connection shattered before it could even form.
"T-That b*tch!" He cursed out loud. "She must have done something!

"I... I’ll kill her... No... I’ll kill..." he growled, his fingers curling into the dirt. His eyes, wide and bloodshot, gleamed with murderous intent. "I’ll kill them both! That bi*tch and her bast*rd husband! But not before I make them suffer. I... I’ll break them slowly. I’ll make them beg for death... and I’ll give it to them... Hahaha!"

His manic laughter echoed through the cave. A moment later, he stopped laughing and, with great difficulty, took out a potion. He then raised his head to drink, his hand trembling as he brought the vial to his cracked lips.
But before the liquid could touch his tongue, his body went rigid.
Because...
He saw a pair of violet eyes staring at him from the darkness.

They belonged to a small black creature, its form barely distinguishable from the darkness around it. It sat just a few feet away, close enough that he could make out the faint outline of its body, but still enough to make his skin crawl.
’H-How is it here?!’

His mind raced. He recognized the identity of the creature right away, but that only made it worse. The cave was sealed off, hidden beneath layers of rock and dirt, and protected by dozens of barriers and traps. It was impossible even for an Emperor to locate, let alone enter unnoticed. And yet... There it sat, as if the concept of impossibility meant nothing to it. Heck, it looked like it had been waiting for him for a long time!
’...Gulp.’ He swallowed hard, his throat going dry. ’I-Is... Is this how it ends? Have I... truly lost?’
’Is it really... over?’
’Am I... going to die?’

His chest tightened at the thought. For the first time in years, true fear gripped him, sinking its claws deep into his heart. His grip on the vial loosened, and it slipped from his trembling fingers, hitting a stone and shattering upon impact. The sound echoed through the cave like a crack of thunder in the stillness.
The noise snapped him out of the spiraling fear that had taken hold of him. He blinked, his vision clearing, and gritted his teeth so hard his jaw ached.
’N-No... There must be a way out of this... I didn’t come this far to die like this!’

chapters.title: Chapter 300: It’s Over [4]
paragraphs: Aeshvin’s mind raced as he considered all the possibilities. However, each of them led to the same dead end: the creature would tear him apart the moment he made any move. There was only one way out, but the thought of it made his stomach churn.
’Urgh... I don’t want to end up as a monster, but... this is the only way to survive.’
’N-No! In fact, this might be the best way to take rev-!’
Aeshvin’s thoughts cut off as the creature suddenly rose to its feet. Its small body slipped free from the shadows, and it began walking toward him with deliberate small steps.
"!" Aeshvin even forgot to breathe.
"I really thought you would be more impressive than this," the creature said, its voice sounding somewhat eerie. "Especially after the way you’ve been acting till now."
"..." Aeshvin opened his mouth, but no word came out.
"I guess that deep down you’re just a weak coward who hides behind other people’s bodies because you can’t stand on your own. Hah, truly pathetic."
"..." Aeshvin gritted his teeth, his nails digging into his palms. ’I’ll show you who’s pathetic soon enough, you fleaball!’

"You’re lucky I’m not the one killing you," the creature muttered as it came to a stop a meter away, its violet eyes boring into him. "But I guess a cornered rat like you will do just fine for what comes next."
’?’ Aeshvin’s brow twitched, confusion flickering through the fear and anger.
What was that supposed to mean? Did it... discover what he was trying to do?
Before he could even think about it, the creature’s form wavered, its small body dissolving into wisps of black smoke. The smoke swirled for a heartbeat, then pulled together into a new shape.
A tall figure now stood where the creature had been.
"I-It’s you..."
Aeshvin’s blood ran cold and his body locked up. Every instinct screamed at him to run, to fight, to do anything, but he couldn’t move.

"..." Soren stood in front of him, looking exactly as he had earlier, but now his knuckles were stained with blackish blood. It was Raven and Orvane’s, to be more exact. The proof of their defeat was still fresh, dripping onto the cave floor.

The dim light of the cave cast long shadows over Soren’s frame, deepening the hollows of his face and sharpening the edges of his silhouette. He looked nothing like the innocent-looking chef from before. He looked more like something born from the dark itself, something that had crawled out from the deepest shadows.
And right now, that something was staring down at him without a shred of warmth in his eyes.
"I told you I would find you," Soren muttered. "That I would make you regret everything you said."

"Get a-rhh!" Aeshvin tried to scramble back, his hands scraping against the stone, but Soren’s hand shot out and closed around his throat. He was lifted off the ground before he could even think to scream, his feet dangling as the grip tightened.
Soren watched him struggle, his expression unchanged.
"And I always keep my word."
"Sevihan."
Soren muttered Aeshvin’s real name and slammed him to the ground.

The impact knocked the air from Sevihan’s lungs, and a spray of blood burst from his mouth as his body bounced against the stone. Before he could even gasp, Soren was on him again, his fist crashing into his face.
Once.
Twice.
Again.
And again.

Each hit landed with the same rhythm, snapping Sevihan’s head from side to side. His face split open in new places with each hit, blood pooling beneath him. His arms twitched, trying to rise, but there was no strength left to stop what was coming.
Thwack-!
Thwack-!

"Huff..." Soren paused after some time, clarity returning to his eyes. But as he stared at Sevihan’s disfigured face, he recalled everything he had done, everything he had heard from Ethea about his evil deeds, and the scene he’d seen with Malakor’s help... the image of countless lifeless people, the terrified victims, the lives he had stolen and twisted for his own amusement.
His grip on Sevihan tightened even further, his gaze hardening into pure ice.
"No... We’re not done yet."
Sevihan wasn’t just an enemy.
He was a plague that had festered in the shadows, feeding on the weak and leaving ruin wherever he went. He... He was a parasite that had to be wiped out before it could spread any further.

He had actually considered handing him over to the Empire before. Letting the authorities deal with him, letting the courts decide his fate. But now, that thought felt laughable. This man was too dangerous to leave alive, too slippery to be held by chains or cells. If given even the smallest opening, he would slip away and start again, and more innocent people would pay the price.
’If the Empire couldn’t put an end to you...’ Soren’s jaw tightened. ’Then I will.’

Still, he couldn’t let his guard down. Because Sevihan was still hiding something. The way his eyes kept flickering, the way his fingers twitched even now... he was waiting. Waiting for the right moment to use whatever trump card he had left.
’And it’s definitely related to his ability...’
Honestly, Soren wasn’t afraid at all. In fact, he wanted him to use the trump card. That way, he could crush whatever hope Sevihan had left and make him truly understand there was no escape.
It sounded twisted even to Soren himself, but a part of him wanted Sevihan to taste the same despair he had fed so many others.
The monster had spent years playing with people’s lives, using them, breaking them, discarding them like broken toys.
’Yeah... This is the least I can do for all the victims who never got justice.’
Having made his decision, Soren took out a high-grade healing potion and forced it down Sevihan’s throat. He then watched as the wounds slowly began to close.
"..." Sevihan stared at him, his eyes filled with confusion and simmering hatred. His breaths came slowly and raggedly, but life was returning to his broken body.
"We both know it’s not over yet." Soren met his gaze evenly. "So stop wasting time and show me what you’ve got."
